package db

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// largeCoverageFixture is a task scoped by 800 subdomains spread over 200 root
// domains and 20 companies, with 1,000 services, 1,200 endpoints and 2,000
// anchored facts. Every tenth root has no asset row, so the graph needs both
// real and synthetic ("r:<domain>") connector roots.
type largeCoverageFixture struct {
	taskID, expID int64
	suffix        string
}

const (
	lcRoots     = 200
	lcCompanies = 20
	lcSubs      = 800
	lcServices  = 1000
	lcEndpoints = 1200
	lcFacts     = 2000
)

func seedLargeCoverageFixture(tb testing.TB, d *DB) largeCoverageFixture {
	tb.Helper()
	task, err := d.CreateTask("large coverage graph", "large coverage graph", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		tb.Fatal(err)
	}
	f := largeCoverageFixture{taskID: task.ID, expID: task.ExplorationID, suffix: fmt.Sprintf("lc%d", task.ID)}
	tb.Cleanup(func() {
		_, _ = d.Exec(`DELETE FROM explorations WHERE id=$1`, f.expID)
		_ = d.DeleteTask(f.taskID)
		_, _ = d.Exec(`DELETE FROM assets WHERE root_domain LIKE '%-'||$1||'.cov.test'`, f.suffix)
		_, _ = d.Exec(`DELETE FROM companies WHERE nkey LIKE 'lcco-'||$1||'-%'`, f.suffix)
	})
	exec := func(q string, args ...any) {
		tb.Helper()
		if _, err := d.Exec(q, args...); err != nil {
			tb.Fatalf("%v\n%s", err, q)
		}
	}
	// root g: r<g>-<suffix>.cov.test, company 1+(g-1)%lcCompanies.
	// subdomain i: s<i>.<root 1+(i-1)%lcRoots>.
	exec(`INSERT INTO companies(name,nkey)
SELECT 'large co '||g||' '||$1, 'lcco-'||$1||'-'||g FROM generate_series(1,$2) g`, f.suffix, lcCompanies)
	exec(`INSERT INTO assets(type,domain,root_domain,company_id)
SELECT 'root_domain', 'r'||g||'-'||$1||'.cov.test', 'r'||g||'-'||$1||'.cov.test',
       (SELECT id FROM companies WHERE nkey='lcco-'||$1||'-'||(1+(g-1)%$3))
FROM generate_series(1,$2) g WHERE g%10<>0`, f.suffix, lcRoots, lcCompanies)
	exec(`INSERT INTO assets(type,domain,root_domain,company_id)
SELECT 'subdomain', 's'||i||'.r'||r||'-'||$1||'.cov.test', 'r'||r||'-'||$1||'.cov.test',
       (SELECT id FROM companies WHERE nkey='lcco-'||$1||'-'||(1+(r-1)%$4))
FROM generate_series(1,$3) i, LATERAL (SELECT 1+(i-1)%$2 AS r) x`, f.suffix, lcRoots, lcSubs, lcCompanies)
	// service j hangs off subdomain 1+(j-1)%lcSubs: port 443 for the first
	// lcSubs services, 8443 for the rest.
	exec(`INSERT INTO assets(type,service_type,url,domain,root_domain,port,company_id)
SELECT 'service','http', 'https://'||s.domain||':'||p||'/', s.domain, s.root_domain, p, s.company_id
FROM generate_series(1,$2) j
CROSS JOIN LATERAL (SELECT CASE WHEN j<=$3 THEN 443 ELSE 8443 END AS p) port
JOIN assets s ON s.type='subdomain' AND s.root_domain LIKE '%-'||$1||'.cov.test'
 AND s.domain LIKE 's'||(1+(j-1)%$3)||'.%'`, f.suffix, lcServices, lcSubs)
	exec(`INSERT INTO assets(type,url,method,domain,root_domain,port,company_id)
SELECT 'endpoint', 'https://'||s.domain||'/p/'||k, 'GET', s.domain, s.root_domain, 443, s.company_id
FROM generate_series(1,$2) k
JOIN assets s ON s.type='subdomain' AND s.root_domain LIKE '%-'||$1||'.cov.test'
 AND s.domain LIKE 's'||(1+(k-1)%$3)||'.%'`, f.suffix, lcEndpoints, lcSubs)
	exec(`INSERT INTO task_scope(task_id,kind,domain,source)
SELECT $1,'subdomain',domain,'manual' FROM assets
WHERE type='subdomain' AND root_domain LIKE '%-'||$2||'.cov.test'`, f.taskID, f.suffix)
	exec(`INSERT INTO exploration_nodes(exploration_id,kind,state,payload)
SELECT $1,'fact','confirmed',jsonb_build_object('summary','large coverage fact '||g) FROM generate_series(1,$2) g`, f.expID, lcFacts)
	exec(`WITH fn AS (
  SELECT id, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY id) rn FROM exploration_nodes
  WHERE exploration_id=$1 AND kind='fact' AND payload->>'summary' LIKE 'large coverage fact %'),
an AS (
  SELECT id, row_number() OVER (ORDER BY id) rn FROM assets
  WHERE type<>'root_domain' AND root_domain LIKE '%-'||$2||'.cov.test')
INSERT INTO exploration_anchors(node_id,asset_id) SELECT fn.id, an.id FROM fn JOIN an USING (rn)`, f.expID, f.suffix)
	exec(`ANALYZE assets, task_scope, exploration_nodes, exploration_anchors, companies`)
	return f
}

func TestBuildCoverageGraphLargeInvariants(t *testing.T) {
	d, err := Open(testDSN(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) - skipping", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { d.Close() })
	f := seedLargeCoverageFixture(t, d)

	g, err := d.Assets().BuildCoverageGraph(f.taskID, f.expID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}

	const (
		syntheticRoots = lcRoots / 10
		realRoots      = lcRoots - syntheticRoots
		inScope        = lcSubs + lcServices + lcEndpoints
		wantNodes      = inScope + lcRoots + lcCompanies
		// subdomain→root, service→subdomain, endpoint→service (port 443), and
		// real root→company; a synthetic root has no company.
		wantEdges = lcSubs + lcServices + lcEndpoints + realRoots
	)
	if len(g.Nodes) != wantNodes || len(g.Edges) != wantEdges {
		t.Fatalf("graph size: nodes=%d edges=%d, want %d/%d", len(g.Nodes), len(g.Edges), wantNodes, wantEdges)
	}

	byKey := make(map[string]CoverageGraphNode, len(g.Nodes))
	kinds := map[string]int{}
	var tested, scoped, synthetic, realConnector int
	for _, n := range g.Nodes {
		if _, dup := byKey[n.Key]; dup {
			t.Fatalf("duplicate node key %q", n.Key)
		}
		byKey[n.Key] = n
		kinds[n.Kind]++
		if n.Tested {
			tested++
		}
		if n.InScope {
			scoped++
		}
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(n.Key, "r:"):
			synthetic++
			if n.Kind != "root_domain" || n.InScope || n.AssetID != 0 || n.Key != "r:"+n.Domain {
				t.Fatalf("synthetic root: %+v", n)
			}
		case n.Kind == "root_domain":
			realConnector++
			if n.InScope || n.AssetID == 0 || n.CompanyID == 0 {
				t.Fatalf("connector root: %+v", n)
			}
		case n.Kind == "company":
			if n.InScope || n.Label == "" || n.Key != companyKey(n.CompanyID) {
				t.Fatalf("company node: %+v", n)
			}
		}
	}
	if kinds["subdomain"] != lcSubs || kinds["service"] != lcServices || kinds["endpoint"] != lcEndpoints ||
		kinds["root_domain"] != lcRoots || kinds["company"] != lcCompanies {
		t.Fatalf("node kinds: %v", kinds)
	}
	if synthetic != syntheticRoots || realConnector != realRoots {
		t.Fatalf("connector roots: synthetic=%d real=%d, want %d/%d", synthetic, realConnector, syntheticRoots, realRoots)
	}
	if scoped != inScope || tested != lcFacts {
		t.Fatalf("in_scope=%d tested=%d, want %d/%d", scoped, tested, inScope, lcFacts)
	}

	seenEdge := map[CoverageGraphEdge]bool{}
	for _, e := range g.Edges {
		src, okSrc := byKey[e.Src]
		dst, okDst := byKey[e.Dst]
		if !okSrc || !okDst || e.Src == e.Dst {
			t.Fatalf("edge %+v points to a missing node", e)
		}
		if seenEdge[e] {
			t.Fatalf("duplicate edge %+v", e)
		}
		seenEdge[e] = true
		want := map[string]string{"subdomain": "root_domain", "service": "subdomain", "endpoint": "service", "root_domain": "company"}[src.Kind]
		if dst.Kind != want {
			t.Fatalf("edge %s(%s) -> %s(%s), want parent kind %s", e.Src, src.Kind, e.Dst, dst.Kind, want)
		}
	}
}

// BenchmarkBuildCoverageGraphLarge locks in the cost of the coverage graph on
// the large fixture (statement count and query plan). No time assertion.
func BenchmarkBuildCoverageGraphLarge(b *testing.B) {
	dsn, _, err := DSN()
	if err != nil {
		b.Skipf("no database config (%v) - skipping", err)
	}
	d, err := Open(dsn)
	if err != nil {
		b.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) - skipping", err)
	}
	b.Cleanup(func() { d.Close() })
	f := seedLargeCoverageFixture(b, d)
	store := d.Assets()
	b.ResetTimer()
	for i := 0; i < b.N; i++ {
		g, err := store.BuildCoverageGraph(f.taskID, f.expID)
		if err != nil {
			b.Fatal(err)
		}
		if len(g.Nodes) == 0 {
			b.Fatal("empty graph")
		}
	}
}

=====================================================================
FILE: db/coverage_ledger.go

package db

import (
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"time"
	"unicode"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// Coverage ledger (modeled on Strix strix/report/coverage.py, skill_coverage_gaps).
// Two layers: agent_reported = the entries workers write with record_coverage;
// machine_observed = execution facts (asset coverage from TaskCoverageWithSources,
// findings). The ledger adds the risk-class dimension and the negative results; it
// never recomputes tested assets. A risk class with no entry is unexamined, never
// clean, and a no_issue_found is never derived from the absence of a finding.

// Ledger outcomes.
const (
	OutcomeReported      = "reported"
	OutcomeNoIssueFound  = "no_issue_found"
	OutcomeRuledOut      = "ruled_out"
	OutcomeNotApplicable = "not_applicable"
	OutcomeNeedsFollowUp = "needs_follow_up"
)

// Gap kinds.
const (
	GapNeedsFollowUp       = "needs_follow_up"
	GapUnrecordedRiskClass = "unrecorded_risk_class"
	GapMissingEvidence     = "missing_evidence"
	GapMissingReason       = "missing_reason"
)

// EndReasonBudget is the tasks.end_reason of a run settled by the run-budget
// wrap-up (server/engine_timeout.go); completeness reads it back. The column is
// per run: a revive to running clears it (ApplyTaskAdmission, SetStatus).
const EndReasonBudget = "budget"

// Ledger field limits (characters, after normalisation). Over a limit the write
// is refused, never truncated.
const (
	maxCoverageSurface  = 200
	maxCoverageRiskArea = 64
	maxCoverageEvidence = 500
	maxCoverageReason   = 500
	// MaxCoverageRowsPerTask caps the current rows of one task: a new key beyond
	// it is refused, an update of an existing key is always allowed. The history
	// is append-only and not capped.
	MaxCoverageRowsPerTask = 2000
)

// ValidCoverageOutcome reports whether o is one of the five ledger outcomes.
func ValidCoverageOutcome(o string) bool {
	switch o {
	case OutcomeReported, OutcomeNoIssueFound, OutcomeRuledOut, OutcomeNotApplicable, OutcomeNeedsFollowUp:
		return true
	}
	return false
}

// CoverageEntry is one agent_reported row: surface + risk_area + outcome + evidence + reason.
type CoverageEntry struct {
	Surface   string    `json:"surface"`
	RiskArea  string    `json:"risk_area"`
	Outcome   string    `json:"outcome"`
	Evidence  string    `json:"evidence"`
	Reason    string    `json:"reason"`
	Worker    string    `json:"worker,omitempty"`
	IntentID  int64     `json:"intent_id,omitempty"`
	UpdatedAt time.Time `json:"updated_at"`
}

// CoverageGap is one open item: a follow-up, an unrecorded mandatory class, or an
// entry missing its required evidence/reason.
type CoverageGap struct {
	Kind     string `json:"kind"`
	Surface  string `json:"surface,omitempty"`
	RiskArea string `json:"risk_area"`
}

func (g CoverageGap) String() string {
	if g.Surface == "" {
		return g.Kind + " " + g.RiskArea
	}
	return g.Kind + " " + g.Surface + " " + g.RiskArea
}

// CoverageCompleteness says whether the run ended as a complete scan. Caveat is
// always set: an incomplete run is never reported silently.
type CoverageCompleteness struct {
	Complete bool   `json:"complete"`
	State    string `json:"state"` // complete | in_progress | paused | timeout | budget | aborted
	Caveat   string `json:"caveat"`
}

// CoverageLedger is the ledger document of one task.
type CoverageLedger struct {
	Entries         []CoverageEntry       `json:"entries"`
	Gaps            []CoverageGap         `json:"gaps"`
	Unexamined      []string              `json:"unexamined"`        // mandatory classes with no entry
	FindingsByClass map[string]int        `json:"findings_by_class"` // machine_observed
	Completeness    *CoverageCompleteness `json:"completeness"`
}

func normRiskArea(s string) string { return strings.ToLower(NormalizeCoverageField(s)) }

// NormalizeCoverageField folds an agent-reported ledger field to one line: every
// control character (C0, DEL, C1) and the Unicode line/paragraph separators become
// a space, runs of whitespace collapse to one space, and the ends are trimmed. The
// fields reach the planner prompt and the report, so they must not carry newlines.
func NormalizeCoverageField(s string) string {
	s = strings.Map(func(r rune) rune {
		if unicode.IsControl(r) || r == ' ' || r == ' ' {
			return ' '
		}
		return r
	}, s)
	return strings.Join(strings.Fields(s), " ")
}

// normalizeCoverageEntry normalises the agent-reported fields of e and checks
// them: required fields, the outcome and the length limits.
func normalizeCoverageEntry(e CoverageEntry) (CoverageEntry, error) {
	e.Surface, e.RiskArea = NormalizeCoverageField(e.Surface), normRiskArea(e.RiskArea)
	e.Evidence, e.Reason = NormalizeCoverageField(e.Evidence), NormalizeCoverageField(e.Reason)
	if e.Surface == "" || e.RiskArea == "" {
		return e, fmt.Errorf("task, surface and risk_area are required")
	}
	if !ValidCoverageOutcome(e.Outcome) {
		return e, fmt.Errorf("outcome must be one of reported, no_issue_found, ruled_out, not_applicable, needs_follow_up")
	}
	for _, f := range []struct {
		name, v string
		max     int
	}{{"surface", e.Surface, maxCoverageSurface}, {"risk_area", e.RiskArea, maxCoverageRiskArea},
		{"evidence", e.Evidence, maxCoverageEvidence}, {"reason", e.Reason, maxCoverageReason}} {
		if utf8.RuneCountInString(f.v) > f.max {
			return e, fmt.Errorf("%s too long (max %d)", f.name, f.max)
		}
	}
	return e, nil
}

// RecordCoverage upserts the current row of (task, surface, risk_area) and appends
// the write to the history, in one transaction. The fields are normalised and
// checked here (normalizeCoverageEntry), whatever the caller.
func (s *AssetStore) RecordCoverage(taskID int64, e CoverageEntry) error {
	if taskID <= 0 {
		return fmt.Errorf("task, surface and risk_area are required")
	}
	e, err := normalizeCoverageEntry(e)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	tx, err := s.db.Begin()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer tx.Rollback() //nolint:errcheck
	// Serialise the writers of one task so the row cap holds under concurrency.
	if _, err := tx.Exec(`SELECT 1 FROM tasks WHERE id=$1 FOR UPDATE`, taskID); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	var exists bool
	var current int
	if err := tx.QueryRow(`SELECT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM coverage_ledger WHERE task_id=$1 AND surface=$2 AND risk_area=$3),
  (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM coverage_ledger WHERE task_id=$1)`, taskID, e.Surface, e.RiskArea).Scan(&exists, &current); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if !exists && current >= MaxCoverageRowsPerTask {
		return fmt.Errorf("coverage ledger full for this task (max %d entries): update an existing surface and risk_area instead", MaxCoverageRowsPerTask)
	}
	args := []any{taskID, e.Surface, e.RiskArea, e.Outcome, e.Evidence, e.Reason, e.Worker, nullID(e.IntentID)}
	if _, err := tx.Exec(`INSERT INTO coverage_ledger_history(task_id, surface, risk_area, outcome, evidence, reason, worker, intent_id)
VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8)`, args...); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	if _, err := tx.Exec(`INSERT INTO coverage_ledger(task_id, surface, risk_area, outcome, evidence, reason, worker, intent_id)
VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4,$5,$6,$7,$8)
ON CONFLICT (task_id, surface, risk_area) DO UPDATE SET outcome=EXCLUDED.outcome, evidence=EXCLUDED.evidence,
  reason=EXCLUDED.reason, worker=EXCLUDED.worker, intent_id=EXCLUDED.intent_id, updated_at=now()`, args...); err != nil {
		return err
	}
	return tx.Commit()
}

func nullID(id int64) any {
	if id <= 0 {
		return nil
	}
	return id
}

// CoverageEntryCount returns the number of current ledger rows of a task.
func (s *AssetStore) CoverageEntryCount(taskID int64) (int, error) {
	var n int
	err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT COUNT(*) FROM coverage_ledger WHERE task_id=$1`, taskID).Scan(&n)
	return n, err
}

// CoverageLedger loads the ledger document of a task: its entries, the mandatory
// classes (goal vulnclass), the findings per class and the task's end state.
func (s *AssetStore) CoverageLedger(taskID int64) (*CoverageLedger, error) {
	var entries []CoverageEntry
	rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT surface, risk_area, outcome, evidence, reason, worker, COALESCE(intent_id,0), updated_at
FROM coverage_ledger WHERE task_id=$1 ORDER BY risk_area, surface`, taskID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	for rows.Next() {
		var e CoverageEntry
		if err := rows.Scan(&e.Surface, &e.RiskArea, &e.Outcome, &e.Evidence, &e.Reason, &e.Worker, &e.IntentID, &e.UpdatedAt); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		entries = append(entries, e)
	}
	if err := rows.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var classes []string
	if err := s.scanStrings(&classes, `SELECT DISTINCT lower(btrim(n.payload->>'vulnclass')) FROM exploration_nodes n
JOIN tasks t ON t.exploration_id=n.exploration_id
WHERE t.id=$1 AND n.kind='goal' AND COALESCE(btrim(n.payload->>'vulnclass'),'')<>'' ORDER BY 1`, taskID); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	byClass := map[string]int{}
	frows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT lower(btrim(vulnclass)), COUNT(*) FROM findings WHERE task_id=$1 AND btrim(vulnclass)<>'' GROUP BY 1`, taskID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer frows.Close()
	for frows.Next() {
		var c string
		var n int
		if err := frows.Scan(&c, &n); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		byClass[c] = n
	}
	if err := frows.Err(); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	var status string
	var paused, budget, pastDeadline bool
	// end_reason is per run (cleared when a revive moves the task back to running),
	// so a budget wrap-up of an earlier run never marks a later one.
	if err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT t.status, COALESCE(t.paused,false), t.end_reason=$2,
  COALESCE(t.deadline_at IS NOT NULL AND t.completed_at IS NOT NULL AND t.completed_at >= t.deadline_at, false)
FROM tasks t WHERE t.id=$1`, taskID, EndReasonBudget).Scan(&status, &paused, &budget, &pastDeadline); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	l := BuildCoverageLedger(entries, classes, CoverageCompletenessFor(status, paused, budget, pastDeadline))
	l.FindingsByClass = byClass
	return l, nil
}

func (s *AssetStore) scanStrings(out *[]string, q string, args ...any) error {
	rows, err := s.db.Query(q, args...)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	for rows.Next() {
		var v string
		if err := rows.Scan(&v); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		*out = append(*out, v)
	}
	return rows.Err()
}

// BuildCoverageLedger derives the gaps from the entries and the mandatory classes.
// Gap sources: (a) needs_follow_up entries; (b) a mandatory class with no entry at
// all (unrecorded_risk_class, also listed as unexamined); (c) an entry missing its
// required evidence (no_issue_found) or reason (ruled_out, not_applicable). Nothing
// here reads findings: an absent finding never closes a class.
func BuildCoverageLedger(entries []CoverageEntry, mandatory []string, c CoverageCompleteness) *CoverageLedger {
	l := &CoverageLedger{Entries: entries, Gaps: []CoverageGap{}, Unexamined: []string{}, FindingsByClass: map[string]int{}, Completeness: &c}
	if l.Entries == nil {
		l.Entries = []CoverageEntry{}
	}
	seen := map[string]bool{}
	for _, e := range entries {
		seen[normRiskArea(e.RiskArea)] = true
		switch {
		case e.Outcome == OutcomeNeedsFollowUp:
			l.Gaps = append(l.Gaps, CoverageGap{GapNeedsFollowUp, e.Surface, e.RiskArea})
		case e.Outcome == OutcomeNoIssueFound && strings.TrimSpace(e.Evidence) == "":
			l.Gaps = append(l.Gaps, CoverageGap{GapMissingEvidence, e.Surface, e.RiskArea})
		case (e.Outcome == OutcomeRuledOut || e.Outcome == OutcomeNotApplicable) && strings.TrimSpace(e.Reason) == "":
			l.Gaps = append(l.Gaps, CoverageGap{GapMissingReason, e.Surface, e.RiskArea})
		}
	}
	classes := map[string]bool{}
	for _, m := range mandatory {
		if m = normRiskArea(m); m != "" && !seen[m] && !classes[m] {
			classes[m] = true
			l.Unexamined = append(l.Unexamined, m)
		}
	}
	sort.Strings(l.Unexamined)
	unrecorded := make([]CoverageGap, 0, len(l.Unexamined))
	for _, m := range l.Unexamined {
		unrecorded = append(unrecorded, CoverageGap{Kind: GapUnrecordedRiskClass, RiskArea: m})
	}
	l.Gaps = append(unrecorded, l.Gaps...) // the central invariant first
	return l
}

// CoverageCompletenessFor maps a task's end state to completeness. Only a task that
// reached done on its own is complete; timeout, budget wrap-up (even when the final
// round met the goals), pause, abort (failed) and a still-running task are not.
func CoverageCompletenessFor(status string, paused, budget, pastDeadline bool) CoverageCompleteness {
	state := "complete"
	switch {
	case budget:
		state = "budget"
	case status == "timeout" || (status == "done" && pastDeadline):
		state = "timeout"
	case status == "failed":
		state = "aborted"
	case paused || status == "paused":
		state = "paused"
	case status != "done":
		state = "in_progress"
	}
	if state == "complete" {
		return CoverageCompleteness{true, state, "Run ended normally. Classes listed as unexamined were not tested and are not clean."}
	}
	return CoverageCompleteness{false, state, "Incomplete scan (" + state + "): the absence of a finding does not mean the target is clean; unexamined classes and open gaps were not covered."}
}

package db

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"reflect"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

func TestBuildCoverageLedgerGaps(t *testing.T) {
	e := func(surface, risk, outcome, evidence, reason string) CoverageEntry {
		return CoverageEntry{Surface: surface, RiskArea: risk, Outcome: outcome, Evidence: evidence, Reason: reason}
	}
	cases := []struct {
		name       string
		entries    []CoverageEntry
		mandatory  []string
		want       []string // CoverageGap.String()
		unexamined []string
	}{
		{"mandatory class with no entry is unexamined, never clean", nil, []string{"SQLi"},
			[]string{"unrecorded_risk_class sqli"}, []string{"sqli"}},
		{"needs_follow_up is a gap", []CoverageEntry{e("/login", "idor", OutcomeNeedsFollowUp, "", "")}, nil,
			[]string{"needs_follow_up /login idor"}, nil},
		{"no_issue_found without evidence is a gap", []CoverageEntry{e("/q", "sqli", OutcomeNoIssueFound, " ", "")}, []string{"sqli"},
			[]string{"missing_evidence /q sqli"}, nil},
		{"no_issue_found with evidence closes the class", []CoverageEntry{e("/q", "sqli", OutcomeNoIssueFound, "fact 12", "")}, []string{"SQLi "},
			nil, nil},
		{"ruled_out without reason is a gap", []CoverageEntry{e("/a", "xss", OutcomeRuledOut, "", "")}, nil,
			[]string{"missing_reason /a xss"}, nil},
		{"not_applicable without reason is a gap", []CoverageEntry{e("/a", "ssrf", OutcomeNotApplicable, "", "")}, nil,
			[]string{"missing_reason /a ssrf"}, nil},
		{"all three sources, unrecorded first", []CoverageEntry{e("/b", "xss", OutcomeNeedsFollowUp, "", ""), e("/c", "rce", OutcomeNoIssueFound, "", "")}, []string{"xss", "idor"},
			[]string{"unrecorded_risk_class idor", "needs_follow_up /b xss", "missing_evidence /c rce"}, []string{"idor"}},
		{"no goals and no entries: no obligation, no gap", nil, nil, nil, nil},
		{"reported closes the class", []CoverageEntry{e("/r", "sqli", OutcomeReported, "", "")}, []string{"sqli"}, nil, nil},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			l := BuildCoverageLedger(c.entries, c.mandatory, CoverageCompleteness{})
			got := []string{}
			for _, g := range l.Gaps {
				got = append(got, g.String())
			}
			if c.want == nil {
				c.want = []string{}
			}
			if c.unexamined == nil {
				c.unexamined = []string{}
			}
			if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, c.want) || !reflect.DeepEqual(l.Unexamined, c.unexamined) {
				t.Fatalf("gaps=%v unexamined=%v, want %v %v", got, l.Unexamined, c.want, c.unexamined)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestCoverageCompletenessFor(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		status               string
		paused, budget, past bool
		state                string
	}{
		{"done", false, false, false, "complete"},
		{"timeout", false, false, true, "timeout"},
		{"done", false, false, true, "timeout"}, // goals met on the final timeout round
		{"timeout", false, true, false, "budget"},
		{"done", false, true, false, "budget"}, // budget wrap-up that met the goals
		{"failed", false, false, false, "aborted"},
		{"running", true, false, false, "paused"},
		{"running", false, false, false, "in_progress"},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		got := CoverageCompletenessFor(c.status, c.paused, c.budget, c.past)
		if got.State != c.state || got.Complete != (c.state == "complete") || got.Caveat == "" {
			t.Errorf("%+v: got %+v", c, got)
		}
	}
}

// The GET coverage document carries entries, gaps and completeness at top level.
func TestCoverageJSONCarriesLedger(t *testing.T) {
	l := BuildCoverageLedger(nil, []string{"sqli"}, CoverageCompletenessFor("timeout", false, false, true))
	b, _ := json.Marshal(&Coverage{Enabled: true, ByType: []CoverageByType{}, CoverageLedger: l})
	var m map[string]json.RawMessage
	_ = json.Unmarshal(b, &m)
	for _, k := range []string{"entries", "gaps", "unexamined", "completeness", "by_type"} {
		if _, ok := m[k]; !ok {
			t.Fatalf("missing %q in %s", k, b)
		}
	}
	if !strings.Contains(string(m["gaps"]), "unrecorded_risk_class") {
		t.Fatalf("gaps=%s", m["gaps"])
	}
}

// PG: upsert keeps one current row per (task, surface, risk_area) and appends history;
// the loaded ledger reads goal vulnclass and the budget end marker.
func TestRecordCoverageUpsertHistory(t *testing.T) {
	d, err := Open(testDSN(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	// Registered FIRST so it runs LAST, after the row cleanup below.
	t.Cleanup(func() { d.Close() })
	task, err := d.CreateTaskWithOptions("coverage ledger", "g", TaskCreateOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { cleanupErr(t, "task", d.DeleteTask(task.ID)) })
	as := d.Assets()
	store := d.Exploration(task.ExplorationID)
	for _, vc := range []string{"SQLi", "XSS"} {
		if _, err := store.AddGoal(map[string]any{"text": "g " + vc, "vulnclass": vc}, "test"); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	for _, e := range []CoverageEntry{
		{Surface: "/q", RiskArea: "SQLi", Outcome: OutcomeNeedsFollowUp},
		{Surface: "/q", RiskArea: "sqli", Outcome: OutcomeNoIssueFound, Evidence: "fact 7"},
	} {
		if err := as.RecordCoverage(task.ID, e); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if err := as.RecordCoverage(task.ID, CoverageEntry{Surface: "/q", RiskArea: "x", Outcome: "clean"}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("invalid outcome accepted")
	}
	var current, history int
	_ = d.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM coverage_ledger WHERE task_id=$1`, task.ID).Scan(&current)
	_ = d.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM coverage_ledger_history WHERE task_id=$1`, task.ID).Scan(&history)
	if current != 1 || history != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("current=%d history=%d, want 1 and 2", current, history)
	}
	l, err := as.CoverageLedger(task.ID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(l.Entries) != 1 || l.Entries[0].Outcome != OutcomeNoIssueFound || len(l.Gaps) != 1 || l.Gaps[0].String() != "unrecorded_risk_class xss" {
		t.Fatalf("ledger=%+v", l)
	}
	if l.Completeness.State != "in_progress" {
		t.Fatalf("completeness=%+v", l.Completeness)
	}
	if won, err := d.SetTerminalStatusGuarded(task.ID, "done", EndReasonBudget); err != nil || !won {
		t.Fatalf("settle won=%v err=%v", won, err)
	}
	if l, _ = as.CoverageLedger(task.ID); l.Completeness.Complete || l.Completeness.State != "budget" {
		t.Fatalf("completeness after budget=%+v", l.Completeness)
	}
}

// PG: the budget end reason belongs to one run. Budget wrap-up, then a revive,
// later planner/worker activity (even one carrying the old activity marker) and
// a normal done: the task is complete, not budget.
func TestCoverageCompletenessBudgetThenReviveDone(t *testing.T) {
	d, err := Open(testDSN(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	// Registered FIRST so it runs LAST, after the row cleanup below.
	t.Cleanup(func() { d.Close() })
	task, err := d.CreateTaskWithOptions("coverage revive", "g", TaskCreateOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { cleanupErr(t, "task", d.DeleteTask(task.ID)) })
	as, store := d.Assets(), d.Exploration(task.ExplorationID)
	state := func() string {
		t.Helper()
		l, err := as.CoverageLedger(task.ID)
		if err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		return l.Completeness.State
	}
	if won, err := d.SetTerminalStatusGuarded(task.ID, "timeout", EndReasonBudget); err != nil || !won {
		t.Fatalf("budget settle won=%v err=%v", won, err)
	}
	if s := state(); s != "budget" {
		t.Fatalf("after budget settle: %s", s)
	}
	if won, _ := d.SetTerminalStatusGuarded(task.ID, "done", ""); won { // a losing writer stores nothing
		t.Fatal("guard overwritten")
	}
	if s := state(); s != "budget" {
		t.Fatalf("after losing writer: %s", s)
	}
	if err := d.SetStatus(task.ID, "running"); err != nil { // revive
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, w := range []string{"planner", "worker-1", "system"} {
		if _, err := store.AppendActivity(Activity{Worker: w, Kind: "text", Metadata: json.RawMessage(`{"end_reason":"budget"}`)}); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
	}
	if s := state(); s != "in_progress" {
		t.Fatalf("revived run: %s", s)
	}
	if won, err := d.SetTerminalStatusGuarded(task.ID, "done", ""); err != nil || !won {
		t.Fatalf("done won=%v err=%v", won, err)
	}
	if s := state(); s != "complete" {
		t.Fatalf("revived run ended normally: %s, want complete", s)
	}
	// ClearRunEndReason never touches a terminal task.
	if _, err := d.Exec(`UPDATE tasks SET status='timeout', end_reason='budget' WHERE id=$1`, task.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if err := d.ClearRunEndReason(task.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if s := state(); s != "budget" {
		t.Fatalf("terminal end_reason cleared: %s", s)
	}
}

// PG: a task holds at most MaxCoverageRowsPerTask current rows; a new key beyond
// the cap is refused, an existing key is still updated.
func TestRecordCoverageRowCap(t *testing.T) {
	d, err := Open(testDSN(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	// Registered FIRST so it runs LAST, after the row cleanup below.

	if _, err := d.Exec(`INSERT INTO coverage_ledger(task_id, surface, risk_area, outcome)
SELECT $1, '/s' || g, 'xss', 'needs_follow_up' FROM generate_series(1, $2::int) g`, task.ID, MaxCoverageRowsPerTask); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	as := d.Assets()

}

// Every agent-reported field is folded to one line and length-checked before any
// write; an over-long field is refused, never truncated.
func TestNormalizeCoverageEntry(t *testing.T) {
	e, err := normalizeCoverageEntry(CoverageEntry{
		Surface: " /a\r\n\n\t[[x]]\x00\x7f\u0085 b  ", RiskArea: " SQLi\n", Outcome: OutcomeNoIssueFound,
		Evidence: "fact\n\n12", Reason: "\tr\x1b[31m",
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if e.Surface != "/a [[x]] b" || e.RiskArea != "sqli" || e.Evidence != "fact 12" || e.Reason != "r [31m" {
		t.Fatalf("normalised=%+v", e)
	}
	ok := CoverageEntry{Surface: "/s", RiskArea: "xss", Outcome: OutcomeReported}
	for _, c := range []struct {
		name string
		edit func(*CoverageEntry, int)
		max  int
	}{
		{"surface", func(e *CoverageEntry, n int) { e.Surface = strings.Repeat("s", n) }, 200},
		{"risk_area", func(e *CoverageEntry, n int) { e.RiskArea = strings.Repeat("r", n) }, 64},
		{"evidence", func(e *CoverageEntry, n int) { e.Evidence = strings.Repeat("é", n) }, 500},
		{"reason", func(e *CoverageEntry, n int) { e.Reason = strings.Repeat("x", n) }, 500},
	} {
		at, over := ok, ok
		c.edit(&at, c.max)
		c.edit(&over, c.max+1)
		if _, err := normalizeCoverageEntry(at); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s at the limit refused: %v", c.name, err)
		}
		want := c.name + " too long (max " + strconv.Itoa(c.max) + ")"
		if _, err := normalizeCoverageEntry(over); err == nil || err.Error() != want {
			t.Errorf("%s over the limit: err=%v, want %q", c.name, err, want)
		}
	}
	if _, err := normalizeCoverageEntry(CoverageEntry{Surface: "\n\t", RiskArea: "xss", Outcome: OutcomeReported}); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("blank surface accepted")
	}
}

package db

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"testing"

// TestCustomToolCRUD exercises create/list/update/delete of a user-defined tool
// (system=false) with kind/exec/deferred. Skips when no Postgres is configured.
func TestCustomToolCRUD(t *testing.T) {
	d, err := Open(testDSN(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	// Registered FIRST so it runs LAST, after the row cleanup below.
	t.Cleanup(func() { d.Close() })

	key := "ct_test_tool"
	_ = d.DeleteCustomTool(key) // clean slate

	in := &Tool{
		Key:         key,
		Description: "test",
		Schema:      json.RawMessage(`{"type":"object","properties":{"x":{"type":"string"}}}`),
		Agents:      []string{"worker"},
		Enabled:     true,
		Kind:        "script",
		Exec:        json.RawMessage(`{"code":"print(1)"}`),
		Deferred:    true,
	}
	if err := d.CreateCustomTool(in); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("create: %v", err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { cleanupErr(t, "custom tool", d.DeleteCustomTool(key)) })

	got, err := d.GetTool(key)
	if err != nil || got == nil {
		t.Fatalf("get after create: %v (nil=%v)", err, got == nil)
	}
	if got.System || got.Kind != "script" || !got.Deferred || len(got.Agents) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected row: %+v", got)
	}

	// custom tools appear in ListCustomTools, not among system-only.
	customs, err := d.ListCustomTools()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	found := false
	for _, c := range customs {
		if c.Key == key {
			found = true
			if c.System {
				t.Fatal("custom tool should have system=false")
			}
		}
	}
	if !found {
		t.Fatal("created tool not in ListCustomTools")
	}

	// update: change kind + disable + rebind.
	in.Kind = "command"
	in.Exec = json.RawMessage(`{"command":"echo hi"}`)
	in.Enabled = false
	in.Agents = []string{"worker", "planner"}
	in.Deferred = false
	if err := d.UpdateCustomTool(in); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("update: %v", err)
	}
	got2, _ := d.GetTool(key)
	if got2.Kind != "command" || got2.Enabled || got2.Deferred || len(got2.Agents) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("update not applied: %+v", got2)
	}

	// delete only removes non-system rows.
	if err := d.DeleteCustomTool(key); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("delete: %v", err)
	}
	if g, _ := d.GetTool(key); g != nil {
		t.Fatal("tool still present after delete")
	}
}

// Package db is the PostgreSQL data source for HIVE (replacing the old graph
// single-file SQLite). It opens the connection, applies the schema, and seeds
// the built-in agents and variable catalog.
//
// Schema changes:
//   - schema.sql remains the idempotent base, executed on every startup.
//   - Any new DDL goes in a numbered migration, migrations/NNNN_slug.sql.
//     Open applies pending migrations once, in version order, and records
//     each in schema_migrations with the SHA-256 of its file.
//   - A published migration is never edited: Open refuses to start when an
//     applied migration's checksum no longer matches its file. Fix forward
//     with a new migration instead.
package db

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	_ "embed"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io/fs"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/config"
	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgconn"
	_ "github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/stdlib" // pgx database/sql driver ("pgx")
)

//go:embed schema.sql
var schemaSQL string

const schemaMigrationLockKey int64 = 7337741001

// maxOpenConns is the connection pool cap; see the note in Open. It sits well
// below PostgreSQL's default max_connections=100, yet well above the
// application's own nested checkout depth (the startup schema advisory lock
// lets seedBuiltins check out another connection while holding one), so it
// never deadlocks itself.
const maxOpenConns = 32

var schemaDeadlockRetryDelays = [...]time.Duration{
	100 * time.Millisecond,
	250 * time.Millisecond,
	500 * time.Millisecond,
	time.Second,
}

type schemaExecer interface {
	ExecContext(context.Context, string, ...any) (sql.Result, error)
}

func isPostgresDeadlock(err error) bool {
	var pgErr *pgconn.PgError
	return errors.As(err, &pgErr) && pgErr.Code == "40P01"
}

func applySchemaWithRetry(ctx context.Context, execer schemaExecer, sleep func(time.Duration)) error {
	for attempt := 0; ; attempt++ {
		if _, err := execer.ExecContext(ctx, schemaSQL); err != nil {
			if !isPostgresDeadlock(err) || attempt >= len(schemaDeadlockRetryDelays) {
				return err
			}
			sleep(schemaDeadlockRetryDelays[attempt])
			continue
		}
		return nil
	}
}

// withSchemaMigrationLock pins the session-level lock to one checked-out
// connection. Running pg_advisory_lock through *sql.DB is incorrect because a
// later schema or unlock call may use a different pooled PostgreSQL session.
func withSchemaMigrationLock(ctx context.Context, sqlDB *sql.DB, action func(*sql.Conn) error) (err error) {
	conn, err := sqlDB.Conn(ctx)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer conn.Close()
	if _, err := conn.ExecContext(ctx, `SELECT pg_advisory_lock($1)`, schemaMigrationLockKey); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("advisory lock: %w", err)
	}
	defer func() {
		if _, unlockErr := conn.ExecContext(context.Background(), `SELECT pg_advisory_unlock($1)`, schemaMigrationLockKey); unlockErr != nil && err == nil {
			err = fmt.Errorf("advisory unlock: %w", unlockErr)
		}
	}()
	return action(conn)
}

// coordinateWithSchemaMigration makes long, multi-table archive transactions
// mutually exclusive with startup DDL while allowing ordinary runtime queries
// to continue normally.
func coordinateWithSchemaMigration(tx *sql.Tx) error {
	if _, err := tx.Exec(`SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock($1)`, schemaMigrationLockKey); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("coordinate with schema migration: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// DSN resolves the PostgreSQL connection string and reports where it came from.
// Precedence: env HIVE_PG_DSN > config file (config.json). There is no
// built-in default — it errors if neither source is configured.
func DSN() (dsn, source string, err error) {
	return config.PostgresDSN()
}

// SuffixTestDatabase rewrites the HIVE_PG_DSN environment variable so its
// database name carries the given suffix (hive -> hive_agent). Called from
// package TestMain functions so every go test package runs against its own
// database: parallel package processes then cannot contend on the same tables
// (the under-load deadlock family, #80). No-op when HIVE_PG_DSN is unset —
// config-file and production paths are untouched. Open creates the suffixed
// database automatically (ensureDatabase).
func SuffixTestDatabase(suffix string) {
	v := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv("HIVE_PG_DSN"))
	if v == "" {
		return
	}
	u, err := url.Parse(v)
	if err != nil || u.Path == "" || u.Path == "/" {
		return
	}
	u.Path = "/" + strings.TrimPrefix(u.Path, "/") + "_" + suffix
	_ = os.Setenv("HIVE_PG_DSN", u.String())
}

// DB wraps the shared *sql.DB. PG handles its own connection pool + concurrency
// (MVCC), so unlike the old SQLite store there is no process-wide write mutex.
type DB struct{ *sql.DB }

// ensureDatabase connects to the postgres system database and creates the target
// database if it does not exist. dsn must be a postgres:// URL.
func ensureDatabase(dsn string) error {
	u, err := url.Parse(dsn)
	if err != nil {
		return nil // unparseable DSN — let the normal Open fail with a clear error
	}
	dbName := strings.TrimPrefix(u.Path, "/")
	if dbName == "" || dbName == "postgres" {
		return nil
	}
	// connect to the postgres maintenance database instead
	adminDSN := *u
	adminDSN.Path = "/postgres"
	admin, err := sql.Open("pgx", adminDSN.String())
	if err != nil {
		return nil // best-effort; let Open surface the real error
	}
	defer admin.Close()
	if err := admin.Ping(); err != nil {
		return nil
	}
	var exists bool
	_ = admin.QueryRow(`SELECT true FROM pg_database WHERE datname=$1`, dbName).Scan(&exists)
	if !exists {
		if _, err := admin.Exec(`CREATE DATABASE "` + dbName + `"`); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("create database %q: %w", dbName, err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// Open connects, applies the schema (idempotent) and the embedded versioned
// migrations, and seeds builtin rows.
func Open(dsn string) (*DB, error) {
	return openWithMigrations(dsn, migrationsFS())
}

// openWithMigrations is Open with the migration set as a parameter, so tests
// can pass an fstest.MapFS.
func openWithMigrations(dsn string, migrations fs.FS) (*DB, error) {
	if err := ensureDatabase(dsn); err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	sqlDB, err := sql.Open("pgx", dsn)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	// database/sql does not limit connections by default: when the pool has no
	// idle connection it unconditionally opens a new one, all the way up to
	// PostgreSQL's max_connections (default 100) before being refused — so
	// peak-load queries get an **error** like `FATAL: sorry, too many clients
	// already`. With a cap, excess queries instead queue waiting for an idle
	// connection — under the same load they become slower rather than failing,
	// and callers no longer have to distinguish "cannot read" from "not there".
	// maxOpenConns must leave headroom for psql / reset-password.sh and any
	// coexisting instances; if max_connections is lowered, lower this too.
	sqlDB.SetMaxOpenConns(maxOpenConns)
	sqlDB.SetMaxIdleConns(maxOpenConns)
	sqlDB.SetConnMaxLifetime(30 * time.Minute)
	sqlDB.SetConnMaxIdleTime(5 * time.Minute)
	if err := sqlDB.Ping(); err != nil {
		sqlDB.Close()
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("ping postgres (%s): %w", config.Redact(dsn), err)
	}
	d := &DB{sqlDB}
	// pgx runs multi-statement Exec via the simple protocol when there are no args.
	// Keep the dedicated lock connection checked out until both DDL and seeding
	// finish so concurrent application instances cannot initialize out of order.
	err = withSchemaMigrationLock(context.Background(), sqlDB, func(conn *sql.Conn) error {
		if err := applySchemaWithRetry(context.Background(), conn, time.Sleep); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("apply schema: %w", err)
		}
		// Runs on conn, the lock holder; it must not call EnsureLLM*Table,
		// whose own lock request would wait on conn forever.
		if err := applyMigrations(context.Background(), conn, migrations); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("apply migrations: %w", err)
		}
		if err := d.seedBuiltins(); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("seed builtins: %w", err)
		}
		return nil
	})
	if err != nil {
		sqlDB.Close()
		return nil, err
	}
	return d, nil
}

// builtinAgent describes one of the fixed agents and its prompt-variable catalog.
type builtinAgent struct {
	key, name, role, desc string
	vars                  []promptVar
	interactiveShell      bool // default interactive-shell switch at row creation; ON CONFLICT does not override a user's later manual toggle
	runSeconds            *int // per-run wall-clock limit (seconds) at row creation; nil = use the seed default (1200), 0 = unlimited
}

type promptVar struct{ name, desc, example, source string }

// intp returns a pointer to v, for explicitly setting builtinAgent optional
// fields (e.g. runSeconds).
func intp(v int) *int { return &v }

// builtinAgents mirrors docs §5(a). Built-in tools are not stored in the DB;
// only agents + the variable catalog are seeded here.
// Note: the interactive-shell default for planner/worker/mainagent/auto is set
// to true uniformly by the interactive_shell_default_v1 block below (respecting
// later toggles); interactiveShell here is only for new agents that need
// "on by default at row creation".
var builtinAgents = []builtinAgent{
	{"goals", "Goal Decomposer", "goals", "Breaks a penetration testing task's goal into several independent, verifiable sub-goals.", []promptVar{
		{"EngagementDescription", "Task description (test target/background)", "Test the example.com site", "exploration"},
		// Now is a global runtime variable (see server.globalPromptVars) and is no
		// longer defined in each agent's catalog, otherwise withGlobalVars would
		// collide with the global entry when appending.
	}, false, nil},
	{"planner", "Planner", "planner", "Reads the posture, judges goals, and only adds exploration intents when there is a genuinely uncovered new direction (one planning loop per task).", []promptVar{
		{"Goal", "Overall task goal", "Gain admin access to example.com", "exploration"},
		{"AssetSummary", "Asset count/type distribution summary (optional)", "domain:3 ip:5 site:2", "distilled"},
	}, false, nil},
	{"mainagent", "Main", "main", "Human-machine interface: observes progress and turns human intent into hints or high-priority intents.", []promptVar{
		{"Goal", "Current task goal", "Gain admin access to example.com", "exploration"},
		{"AssetSummary", "Initial posture summary (optional)", "domain:3 ip:5", "distilled"},
		{"FindingsSummary", "Confirmed vulnerability summary (optional)", "high:1 medium:2", "distilled"},
	}, false, nil},
	{"worker", "Worker", "worker", "Picks up one intent and executes it, writes discovered facts/vulnerabilities back to the knowledge graph, then stops.", []promptVar{
		{"ProxyAddr", "Recorded proxy address (drives the if/else dual wording)", "127.0.0.1:8080", "runtime"},
		{"WorkerName", "Worker self-identifier (optional)", "worker-1", "runtime"},
	}, false, nil},
	// Auto: built-in "platform operations" agent. Does not join the pentest
	// orchestration loop; driven from the chat page, operates the platform with tools.
	{"auto", "Auto", "assistant", "Platform operations assistant: manages tasks (create/view/pause/hint) and assets with tools, and can create/modify skills, custom tools, and MCP.", nil, false, nil},
	// Pentest: built-in "solo pentest" agent. Driven from the chat page, it walks the
	// full pentest chain alone from recon to wrap-up, planning, executing and
	// verifying by itself. Interactive shell is on by default.
	{"pentest", "Penetration Testing", "assistant", "Solo pentest agent: single-handedly walks the full chain from recon → attack surface → deep exploitation → verification → wrap-up, with its own planning, execution, and adversarial verification.", nil, true, intp(0)},
}

// seedBuiltins inserts the fixed built-in agents and their variable catalog (idempotent).
func (d *DB) seedBuiltins() error {
	for _, a := range builtinAgents {
		var agentID int64
		err := d.QueryRow(`
INSERT INTO agents(key, name, description, role, builtin, enabled, interactive_shell, run_seconds)
VALUES ($1, $2, NULLIF($3,''), $4, true, true, $5, COALESCE($6, 1200))
ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET name = EXCLUDED.name, description = EXCLUDED.description
RETURNING id`, a.key, a.name, a.desc, a.role, a.interactiveShell, a.runSeconds).Scan(&agentID)
		if err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("agent %s: %w", a.key, err)
		}
		for _, v := range a.vars {
			if _, err := d.Exec(`
INSERT INTO agent_prompt_vars(agent_id, var_name, description, example, source)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, $4, $5)
ON CONFLICT (agent_id, var_name) DO UPDATE
  SET description = EXCLUDED.description, example = EXCLUDED.example, source = EXCLUDED.source`,
				agentID, v.name, v.desc, v.example, v.source); err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("agent %s var %s: %w", a.key, v.name, err)
			}
		}
	}
	// Drop catalog entries for variables that were renamed, so the white-list no
	// longer advertises a name templates can't resolve (EngagementTitle→Description).
	// After 'Now' was promoted from each agent's catalog to a global runtime
	// variable, old DBs still carry a leftover 'Now' entry for goals, which would
	// collide with the global one (duplicate key in the frontend variable list);
	// clean it up here too.
	if _, err := d.Exec(`DELETE FROM agent_prompt_vars WHERE var_name IN ('EngagementTitle', 'CoverageGaps', 'Now')`); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("cleanup renamed vars: %w", err)
	}
	// Default-on interactive_shell for the runtime agents (planner/worker/mainagent/auto)
	// ONCE — respects a later user toggle-off (guarded by a settings flag). goals(one-shot
	// decomposer) stays off. Runs after the column exists (schema applied before seed).
	if v, _, _ := d.GetSetting("interactive_shell_default_v1"); v != "true" {
		if _, err := d.Exec(`UPDATE agents SET interactive_shell=true WHERE key IN ('planner','worker','mainagent','auto')`); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("seed interactive_shell defaults: %w", err)
		}
		_ = d.SetSetting("interactive_shell_default_v1", "true")
	}
	// Seed the built-in browser (Playwright) MCP once — DISABLED by default (the
	// user enables it when needed), no proxy by default. The traffic-capture
	// toggle injects/strips
	// the recording proxy + CA at runtime (server.Manager.syncBrowserMCPProxy).
	// Insert only if absent so we never clobber user edits (args/env/enabled/
	// visibility) on restart.
	if _, err := d.Exec(`
INSERT INTO mcp_servers(name, transport, command, args, env, enabled)
VALUES ('browser', 'stdio', 'npx', $1, '{}', false)
ON CONFLICT (name) DO NOTHING`,
		`["@playwright/mcp","--headless"]`); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("seed browser mcp: %w", err)
	}
	// NOTE: the placeholder ScopeSentry data-source MCP (empty URL + empty X-API-Key,
	// disabled) is seeded directly in schema.sql §F so a raw `psql < schema.sql` init
	// also gets it. schema.sql is Exec'd on every startup, so it stays idempotent.
	if err := d.seedBuiltinSkillVisibility(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("seed skill visibility: %w", err)
	}
	if err := d.seedDefaultInterceptRules(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("seed intercept rules: %w", err)
	}
	if err := d.seedDefaultInterceptRulesV2(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("seed intercept rules v2: %w", err)
	}
	if err := d.seedDefaultInterceptRulesV3(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("seed intercept rules v3: %w", err)
	}
	if err := d.seedDefaultAssetInterceptRules(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("seed asset intercept rules: %w", err)
	}
	if err := d.seedTargetGateExemptions(); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("seed target-gate exemptions: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

// seedDefaultAssetInterceptRules inserts the built-in asset blocklist (fuzzy
// domain matches for government / education sites) once on first startup. Gated
// by a settings flag so a user's later disable/delete is never resurrected on
// restart — same policy as the intercept-rule seed.
func (d *DB) seedDefaultAssetInterceptRules() error {
	if v, _, _ := d.GetSetting("asset_intercept_default_rules_v1"); v == "done" {
		return nil
	}
	rules := []struct {
		kind    string
		pattern string
		note    string
	}{
		{"fuzzy_domain", ".gov", "[built-in] Government websites (.gov)"},
		{"fuzzy_domain", ".gov.cn", "[built-in] Government websites (.gov.cn)"},
		{"fuzzy_domain", ".edu", "[built-in] Education websites (.edu)"},
		{"fuzzy_domain", ".edu.cn", "[built-in] Education websites (.edu.cn)"},
	}
	for _, r := range rules {
		if _, err := d.Exec(`
INSERT INTO asset_intercept_rules(enabled, kind, pattern, note, builtin)
VALUES (true, $1, $2, $3, true)
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`, r.kind, r.pattern, r.note); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("asset rule %q: %w", r.pattern, err)
		}
	}
	return d.SetSetting("asset_intercept_default_rules_v1", "done")
}

// builtinSkillVisibility maps a shipped skill's directory name → the built-in
// agent keys that should see it by default. The skill FILES themselves live on the
// filesystem (SkillDir, loaded by norma at runtime); DB only carries this visibility
// binding. Skills omitted here (e.g. playwright-cli, scopesentry) ship invisible by
// default — the user turns them on per-agent when needed. scopesentry additionally
// declares `mcps: ScopeSentry`, which only takes effect once it's made visible and
// that MCP is enabled/configured.
var builtinSkillVisibility = map[string][]string{
	"api-recon": {"auto", "pentest", "worker"},
}

// seedBuiltinSkillVisibility binds the shipped built-in skills to their default
// agents. Insert-if-absent (ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING) so a user's later toggle-off is
// never resurrected on restart — matches the browser-MCP / intercept-rule seed policy.
func (d *DB) seedBuiltinSkillVisibility() error {
	for skillName, agentKeys := range builtinSkillVisibility {
		for _, key := range agentKeys {
			if _, err := d.Exec(`
INSERT INTO agent_skill_visibility(agent_id, skill_name, enabled)
SELECT id, $2, true FROM agents WHERE key=$1
ON CONFLICT (agent_id, skill_name) DO NOTHING`, key, skillName); err != nil {
				return fmt.Errorf("skill %s → agent %s: %w", skillName, key, err)
			}
		}
	}
	return nil
}

// seedDefaultInterceptRules inserts built-in safety intercept rules once on
// first startup. The seed is gated by a settings flag so user edits (disable,
// delete, re-order) are never overwritten on subsequent restarts.
func (d *DB) seedDefaultInterceptRules() error {
	if v, _, _ := d.GetSetting("intercept_default_rules_v1"); v == "done" {
		return nil
	}
	type rule struct {
		name     string
		target   string // tool_name | tool_input
		typ      string // string | regex
		pattern  string
		action   string
		message  string
		priority int
	}
	rules := []rule{
		// ── System-destructive commands (priority 100) ───────────────────────
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Recursive force delete rm -rf",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `(?i)\brm\b.{0,80}(?:-[a-z]*r[a-z]*f[a-z]*|-[a-z]*f[a-z]*r[a-z]*|--recursive|--no-preserve-root)`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Recursive force delete is forbidden (rm -rf / rm --recursive); it can permanently damage the system or the target machine environment",
			priority: 100,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Delete critical system directories",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `\brm\b[^"'\n]{0,60}["'\s](/|/etc|/bin|/usr|/boot|/var|/lib|/sys|/proc|/dev|/sbin|/root)`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Deleting critical system paths is forbidden",
			priority: 100,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Disk formatting mkfs",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `\bmkfs\b`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Formatting disks is forbidden (mkfs)",
			priority: 100,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Overwrite disk device dd",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `\bdd\b[^|\n]{0,100}\bof=\s*/dev/[a-zA-Z]`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Using dd to overwrite disk devices is forbidden",
			priority: 100,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Fork bomb",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `:\(\)\s*\{[^}]*:\|:`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Executing a fork bomb is forbidden",
			priority: 100,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Shutdown / reboot",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `\b(?:shutdown|reboot|halt|poweroff|init\s+[06])\b`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Executing shutdown or reboot commands is forbidden",
			priority: 100,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Kill all processes",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `\bkill\s+-9\s+-1\b|\bkillall\s+-9\b`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "kill -9 -1 or killall -9 is forbidden (kills all processes)",
			priority: 100,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Disk wipe shred / wipe",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `\b(?:shred|wipe)\b[^|\n]{0,80}/dev/[a-zA-Z]`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Running shred/wipe erasure against disk devices is forbidden",
			priority: 100,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Flush firewall rules",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `\biptables\s+(?:-F|--flush)\b|\bnft\s+flush\s+ruleset\b`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Flushing firewall rules is forbidden (iptables -F / nft flush)",
			priority: 100,
		},
		// ── Database-destructive operations (priority 90) ────────────────────
		{
			name:     "[built-in] SQL DROP DATABASE / TABLE / SCHEMA",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `(?i)\bDROP\s+(?:DATABASE|TABLE|SCHEMA|INDEX|VIEW|TABLESPACE|USER|ROLE)\b`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "DROP operations are forbidden; they can irreversibly destroy database objects",
			priority: 90,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] SQL TRUNCATE",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `(?i)\bTRUNCATE\s+(?:TABLE\s+)?\w`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "TRUNCATE is forbidden; it can wipe all data in a table",
			priority: 90,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] MongoDB drop / dropDatabase",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `(?i)\.(?:dropDatabase|dropCollection|drop)\s*\(`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "MongoDB drop operations are forbidden",
			priority: 90,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Redis FLUSHALL / FLUSHDB",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `(?i)\b(?:FLUSHALL|FLUSHDB)\b`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Redis FLUSHALL / FLUSHDB is forbidden; it can wipe all cached data",
			priority: 90,
		},
		// ── Destructive HTTP requests (priority 80) ──────────────────────────
		// The three common ways an Agent sends a DELETE request:
		//   1. curl -X DELETE / --request DELETE (run directly by the Bash tool or written into a script)
		//   2. Python HTTP client .delete() method
		//   3. method: 'DELETE' / method="DELETE" in JS/generic scripts
		{
			name:     "[built-in] curl / wget sending DELETE requests",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `(?i)\bcurl\b[^|\n&;"]{0,300}(?:-X\s*DELETE|--request\s+DELETE|-XDELETE)|\bwget\b[^|\n&;"]{0,300}--method[=\s]+DELETE`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Sending HTTP DELETE requests via curl/wget is forbidden; it may delete data on the target system",
			priority: 80,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Python HTTP client DELETE (requests/httpx/aiohttp)",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `(?i)\b(?:requests|httpx|aiohttp|urllib\.request)\.delete\s*\(|session\.delete\s*\(|client\.delete\s*\(`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Sending DELETE requests with Python HTTP clients is forbidden",
			priority: 80,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Declaring the HTTP DELETE method in scripts (JS/generic)",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `(?i)axios\.delete\s*\(|method\s*[:=]\s*['"]DELETE['"]`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Declaring and sending HTTP DELETE requests in scripts is forbidden",
			priority: 80,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Bulk clear / wipe endpoint paths",
			target:   "tool_input",
			typ:      "regex",
			pattern:  `(?i)/(?:clear|wipe|flush|purge|truncate|drop|destroy|factory[-_]reset|reset[-_]all)(?:[/?#"'\s]|$)`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Calling bulk-clear or destroy-style endpoints is forbidden (/clear /wipe /flush /purge etc.)",
			priority: 80,
		},
	}
	for _, r := range rules {
		if _, err := d.Exec(`
INSERT INTO intercept_rules(name, enabled, priority, match_target, match_type, pattern, action, message, timeout_enabled, timeout_seconds, timeout_action)
VALUES ($1, true, $2, $3, $4, $5, $6, $7, false, 60, 'deny')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`,
			r.name, r.priority, r.target, r.typ, r.pattern, r.action, r.message,
		); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("rule %q: %w", r.name, err)
		}
	}
	return d.SetSetting("intercept_default_rules_v1", "done")
}

// seedDefaultInterceptRulesV2 migrates the two safety patterns that used to be
// hard-coded in guard.go (destructive shell + data-exfil pipe) into ordinary
// intercept rules. Gated by its own flag so it also lands on DBs that already ran
// v1. Unlike the old guard.go floor, these are plain [built-in] rules — the user can
// disable or delete them. The exfil rule ships DISABLED by default (its
// curl/wget/nc pipe pattern mis-fires on legitimate CTF/pentest reverse-shell and
// data-transfer pipes); enable it manually when exfil gating is actually wanted.
func (d *DB) seedDefaultInterceptRulesV2() error {
	if v, _, _ := d.GetSetting("intercept_default_rules_v2"); v == "done" {
		return nil
	}
	rules := []struct {
		name     string
		pattern  string
		action   string
		message  string
		enabled  bool
		priority int
	}{
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Destructive system commands",
			pattern:  `(?i)\b(rm\s+-rf\s+/|mkfs|dd\s+if=|:\(\)\s*\{|shutdown|reboot|>\s*/dev/sd)`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Destructive command rejected (rm -rf / / mkfs / dd / fork bomb / shutdown-reboot / overwriting disk devices)",
			enabled:  true,
			priority: 100,
		},
		{
			name:     "[built-in] Data exfiltration pipe",
			pattern:  `(?i)(curl|wget|nc|ncat)\b[^|]*\b(\|\s*(curl|wget|nc))`,
			action:   "deny",
			message:  "Suspected data exfiltration pipe rejected (command output piped out via curl/wget/nc)",
			enabled:  false,
			priority: 80,
		},
	}
	for _, r := range rules {
		if _, err := d.Exec(`
INSERT INTO intercept_rules(name, enabled, priority, match_target, match_type, pattern, action, message, timeout_enabled, timeout_seconds, timeout_action)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, 'tool_input', 'regex', $4, $5, $6, false, 60, 'deny')
ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING`,
			r.name, r.enabled, r.priority, r.pattern, r.action, r.message,
		); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("rule %q: %w", r.name, err)
		}
	}
	return d.SetSetting("intercept_default_rules_v2", "done")
}

// seedDefaultInterceptRulesV3 adds the delete-endpoint path rule. The v1 HTTP rules
// only catch the DELETE *method* (curl -X DELETE, requests.delete(, method:'DELETE'),
// and v1's path rule covers only /clear /wipe /flush /purge /truncate /drop /destroy
// /factory-reset /reset-all — so a plain `curl 'http://t/api/user/delete?id=1'` (a
// delete endpoint reached with GET/POST, which is how most web apps expose deletion)
// slipped through every built-in rule. Own flag so it also lands on DBs that already
// ran v1/v2, where editing the v1 seed would have no effect.
//
// The pattern deliberately requires a separator after the verb so /delivery,
// /details, /delta and /delegate do not match, while /deleteAll, /delete_user and
// /delete-user do. destroy is re-covered here because v1's rule does not allow a
// suffix (/destroyAll was missed).
//
// Exported as a package const only so the seeded regex is unit-testable without a DB.
const deleteEndpointPathPattern = `(?i)/(?:(?:delete|remove|unlink|erase|destroy)[-\w]*|del)(?:[/?#"'\s]|$)`

func (d *DB) seedDefaultInterceptRulesV3() error {
	if v, _, _ := d.GetSetting("intercept_default_rules_v3"); v == "done" {
		return nil
	}
	const name = "[built-in] Delete-style endpoint paths"
	if _, err := d.Exec(`
INSERT INTO intercept_rules(name, enabled, priority, match_target, match_type, pattern, action, message, timeout_enabled, timeout_seconds, timeout_action)
SELECT $1, true, 80, 'tool_input', 'regex', $2, 'deny', $3, false, 60, 'deny'
WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM intercept_rules WHERE name = $1)`,
		name,
		deleteEndpointPathPattern,
		"Calling delete-style endpoints is forbidden (/delete /remove /unlink /erase etc.), regardless of the HTTP method — most apps' delete endpoints can be triggered with GET/POST and will still really delete target data",
	); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("rule %q: %w", name, err)
	}
	return d.SetSetting("intercept_default_rules_v3", "done")
}

package db

import (
	"context"
	"database/sql"
	"errors"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgconn"
)

type schemaExecFunc func(context.Context, string, ...any) (sql.Result, error)

func (f schemaExecFunc) ExecContext(ctx context.Context, query string, args ...any) (sql.Result, error) {
	return f(ctx, query, args...)
}

func TestApplySchemaRetriesOnlyDeadlocks(t *testing.T) {
	deadlockAttempts := 0
	delays := []time.Duration{}
	err := applySchemaWithRetry(t.Context(), schemaExecFunc(func(context.Context, string, ...any) (sql.Result, error) {
		deadlockAttempts++
		if deadlockAttempts < 3 {
			return nil, &pgconn.PgError{Code: "40P01", Message: "deadlock detected"}
		}
		return nil, nil
	}), func(delay time.Duration) {
		delays = append(delays, delay)
	})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if deadlockAttempts != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("schema attempts=%d, want 3", deadlockAttempts)
	}
	if len(delays) != 2 || delays[0] != schemaDeadlockRetryDelays[0] || delays[1] != schemaDeadlockRetryDelays[1] {
		t.Fatalf("schema retry delays=%v", delays)
	}

	nonRetryable := errors.New("permission denied")
	nonRetryableAttempts := 0
	err = applySchemaWithRetry(t.Context(), schemaExecFunc(func(context.Context, string, ...any) (sql.Result, error) {
		nonRetryableAttempts++
		return nil, nonRetryable
	}), func(time.Duration) {
		t.Fatal("non-deadlock error must not be retried")
	})
	if !errors.Is(err, nonRetryable) || nonRetryableAttempts != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("non-retryable result: attempts=%d err=%v", nonRetryableAttempts, err)
	}
}

// testDSN returns the configured DSN, skipping the test when neither the env var
// nor a config file supplies one (DSN no longer has a built-in default).
func testDSN(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	dsn, _, err := DSN()
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("no database config (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	return dsn
}

// TestOpenSeed opens the live dev PG, applies schema, seeds, and verifies the
// builtin agents + their variable catalog exist. Skips if PG is unreachable.
func TestOpenSeed(t *testing.T) {
	d, err := Open(testDSN(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("postgres unavailable (%v) — skipping", err)
	}
	defer d.Close()

	wantAgents := len(builtinAgents)
	var agents int
	if err := d.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM agents WHERE builtin`).Scan(&agents); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if agents != wantAgents {
		t.Fatalf("want %d builtin agents, got %d", wantAgents, agents)
	}

	// planner should have at least its seeded catalog vars
	wantPlannerVars := 0
	for _, a := range builtinAgents {
		if a.key == "planner" {
			wantPlannerVars = len(a.vars)
			break
		}
	}
	var plannerVars int
	if err := d.QueryRow(`
SELECT count(*) FROM agent_prompt_vars v
JOIN agents a ON a.id = v.agent_id
WHERE a.key = 'planner'`).Scan(&plannerVars); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if plannerVars < wantPlannerVars {
		t.Fatalf("want at least %d planner vars, got %d", wantPlannerVars, plannerVars)
	}

	// re-open must be idempotent (no duplicate agents)
	d2, err := Open(testDSN(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer d2.Close()
	if err := d2.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM agents WHERE builtin`).Scan(&agents); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if agents != wantAgents {
		t.Fatalf("after re-open want %d agents, got %d", wantAgents, agents)
	}
}

package db

// cold-digest §1/§2.3/§5: persistence for cold-node compression — the round
// counter, cold_since_round stamps, content versions, digest nodes and the
// covers edges that are the source of truth for "which digest folds node X".

import (
	"database/sql"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"
)

// BumpRound advances this exploration's planner-round counter and returns the
// new value (§2.3). Called once per planner wake-up.
func (s *ExplorationStore) BumpRound() (int64, error) {
	var r int64
	err := s.db.QueryRow(`UPDATE explorations SET round_no = round_no + 1 WHERE id=$1 RETURNING round_no`, s.expID).Scan(&r)
	return r, err
}

// RoundNo returns the current planner-round counter.
func (s *ExplorationStore) RoundNo() (int64, error) {
	var r int64
	err := s.db.QueryRow(`SELECT round_no FROM explorations WHERE id=$1`, s.expID).Scan(&r)
	return r, err
}

// ColdStamps returns cold_since_round for every foldable node (intent/fact):
// id → *round (nil when the node is hot / unstamped). Used to compute the ≥R
// debounce and to know which stamps to set/clear this round.
func (s *ExplorationStore) ColdStamps() (map[int64]*int64, error) {
	rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT id, cold_since_round FROM exploration_nodes
		WHERE exploration_id=$1 AND kind IN ('intent','fact')`, s.expID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	out := map[int64]*int64{}
	for rows.Next() {
		var id int64
		var cs sql.NullInt64
		if err := rows.Scan(&id, &cs); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if cs.Valid {
			v := cs.Int64
			out[id] = &v
		} else {
			out[id] = nil
		}
	}
	return out, rows.Err()
}

// StampOp is one cold_since_round change: Set stamps Round; !Set clears it.
type StampOp struct {
	ID    int64
	Set   bool
	Round int64
}

// ApplyStampOps writes a batch of cold_since_round changes in one transaction.
func (s *ExplorationStore) ApplyStampOps(ops []StampOp) error {
	if len(ops) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	tx, err := s.db.Begin()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer tx.Rollback()
	for _, o := range ops {
		if o.Set {
			if _, err := tx.Exec(`UPDATE exploration_nodes SET cold_since_round=$1 WHERE id=$2 AND exploration_id=$3`, o.Round, o.ID, s.expID); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		} else {
			if _, err := tx.Exec(`UPDATE exploration_nodes SET cold_since_round=NULL WHERE id=$1 AND exploration_id=$2`, o.ID, s.expID); err != nil {
				return err
			}
		}
	}
	return tx.Commit()
}

// ContentVersions returns id → content_version for all nodes (§5.3 signature).
func (s *ExplorationStore) ContentVersions() (map[int64]int, error) {
	rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT id, content_version FROM exploration_nodes WHERE exploration_id=$1`, s.expID)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	out := map[int64]int{}
	for rows.Next() {
		var id int64
		var v int
		if err := rows.Scan(&id, &v); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		out[id] = v
	}
	return out, rows.Err()
}

// ActiveDigests returns the exploration's live digest nodes (state='active'),
// oldest first.
func (s *ExplorationStore) ActiveDigests() ([]*Node, error) {
	rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT `+nodeCols+` FROM exploration_nodes
		WHERE exploration_id=$1 AND kind=$2 AND state=$3 ORDER BY id`, s.expID, KindDigest, StateDigestActive)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	return scanNodes(rows)
}

// AddDigest writes one digest node and its covers edges (digest→member) in a
// single transaction. payload is the digest body + member_ids + generation +
// signature (see cold-digest §1). Returns the new digest id.
func (s *ExplorationStore) AddDigest(payload map[string]any, memberIDs []int64) (int64, error) {
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(payload)
	tx, err := s.db.Begin()
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	defer tx.Rollback()
	var id int64
	if err := tx.QueryRow(`
INSERT INTO exploration_nodes(exploration_id, kind, payload, priority, state, origin)
VALUES ($1, $2, $3, 0, $4, 'compactor') RETURNING id`,
		s.expID, KindDigest, string(raw), StateDigestActive).Scan(&id); err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	for _, m := range memberIDs {
		if m == id {
			continue
		}
		if _, err := tx.Exec(`
INSERT INTO exploration_edges(exploration_id, src_id, rel, dst_id) VALUES ($1,$2,$3,$4)
ON CONFLICT (exploration_id, src_id, rel, dst_id) DO NOTHING`, s.expID, id, RelCovers, m); err != nil {
			return 0, err
		}
	}
	return id, tx.Commit()
}

// CoveredMembers maps member id → covering digest id, for ACTIVE digests only
// (§6.1 point 1). A node with no entry is not currently folded. Should a member
// carry covers edges from two digests (a torn major write), the lowest digest id
// wins deterministically — callers dedupe on this.
func (s *ExplorationStore) CoveredMembers() (map[int64]int64, error) {
	rows, err := s.db.Query(`
SELECT e.dst_id, e.src_id
FROM exploration_edges e
JOIN exploration_nodes d ON d.id=e.src_id AND d.exploration_id=e.exploration_id
WHERE e.exploration_id=$1 AND e.rel=$2 AND d.kind=$3 AND d.state=$4
ORDER BY e.src_id`, s.expID, RelCovers, KindDigest, StateDigestActive)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	out := map[int64]int64{}
	for rows.Next() {
		var member, digest int64
		if err := rows.Scan(&member, &digest); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		if _, seen := out[member]; !seen { // first (lowest digest id) wins
			out[member] = digest
		}
	}
	return out, rows.Err()
}

// DigestMembers returns the member ids a digest covers (covers edges), sorted.
func (s *ExplorationStore) DigestMembers(digestID int64) ([]int64, error) {
	rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT dst_id FROM exploration_edges
		WHERE exploration_id=$1 AND src_id=$2 AND rel=$3`, s.expID, digestID, RelCovers)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var ids []int64
	for rows.Next() {
		var id int64
		if err := rows.Scan(&id); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	sort.Slice(ids, func(i, j int) bool { return ids[i] < ids[j] })
	return ids, rows.Err()
}

// SupersedeDigests retires digest nodes (state→superseded) AND removes their
// covers edges, atomically, so the active-coverage set (CoveredMembers) never
// double-counts a member during a major recompaction (§5.1). The digest node
// itself is kept (node_detail can still resolve it).
func (s *ExplorationStore) SupersedeDigests(ids []int64) error {
	if len(ids) == 0 {
		return nil
	}
	tx, err := s.db.Begin()
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	defer tx.Rollback()
	for _, id := range ids {
		if _, err := tx.Exec(`DELETE FROM exploration_edges
			WHERE exploration_id=$1 AND src_id=$2 AND rel=$3`, s.expID, id, RelCovers); err != nil {
			return err
		}
		if _, err := tx.Exec(`UPDATE exploration_nodes SET state=$1 WHERE id=$2 AND exploration_id=$3 AND kind=$4`,
			StateDigestSuperseded, id, s.expID, KindDigest); err != nil {
			return err
		}
	}
	return tx.Commit()
}

// NodeAssets maps each of the given node ids → the asset ids it is anchored to
// (exploration_anchors). Used to group cold digests by asset (§6.2 index).
func (s *ExplorationStore) NodeAssets(ids []int64) (map[int64][]int64, error) {
	out := map[int64][]int64{}
	if len(ids) == 0 {
		return out, nil
	}
	placeholders := make([]string, len(ids))
	args := make([]any, 0, len(ids)+1)
	args = append(args, s.expID)
	for i, id := range ids {
		placeholders[i] = fmt.Sprintf("$%d", i+2)
		args = append(args, id)
	}
	rows, err := s.db.Query(`SELECT a.node_id, a.asset_id
		FROM exploration_anchors a
		JOIN exploration_nodes n ON n.id=a.node_id
		WHERE n.exploration_id=$1 AND a.node_id IN (`+strings.Join(placeholders, ",")+`)`, args...)
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	for rows.Next() {
		var node, asset int64
		if err := rows.Scan(&node, &asset); err != nil {
			return nil, err
		}
		out[node] = append(out[node], asset)
	}
	return out, rows.Err()
}

// evidenceFixture records a finding. With legacy=false the snapshot goes through
// the normal insert path; with legacy=true it is written in clear by raw SQL.
func evidenceFixture(t *testing.T, d *DB, tag string, legacy bool) (*Task, int64, TrafficEvidenceSnapshot) {
	t.Helper()
	task, err := d.CreateTask("evidence heads at rest "+tag, "goal", nil, 0, 0)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	s := TrafficEvidenceSnapshot{SourceTrafficID: "t-sec-ev-" + tag, CapturedAt: 1, URL: "http://ev.example/" + tag, Method: "GET", Status: 200,
		ReqHead:  "GET /" + tag + " HTTP/1.1\nCookie: " + evCookie + "\nAuthorization: " + evBearer + "\n",
		RespHead: "HTTP/1.1 200 OK\nSet-Cookie: " + evCookie + "\n", ReqHash: "rh-" + tag, RespHash: "ph-" + tag}
	s.ID = TrafficSnapshotID(s)
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		d.Exec(`DELETE FROM task_archives WHERE task_id=$1`, task.ID)
		d.DeleteTaskCascade(task.ID, false, true) // findings and their bindings too
		if _, err := d.Exec(`DELETE FROM traffic_evidence_snapshots WHERE id=$1`, s.ID); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("cleanup snapshot: %v", err)
		}
	})
	f, err := d.Exploration(task.ExplorationID).RecordFinding(t.Context(), RecordFindingInput{TaskID: task.ID, ExplorationID: task.ExplorationID, Summary: "evidence " + tag, Severity: "low"})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if legacy {
		_, err = d.Exec(`INSERT INTO traffic_evidence_snapshots(id,source_traffic_id,captured_at,url,method,status,req_head,resp_head,req_hash,resp_hash,req_len,resp_len)
VALUES($1,$2,1,$3,'GET',200,$4,$5,$6,$7,0,0)`, s.ID, s.SourceTrafficID, s.URL, s.ReqHead, s.RespHead, s.ReqHash, s.RespHash)
		if err == nil {
			_, err = d.Exec(`INSERT INTO finding_traffic_bindings(finding_id,snapshot_id,position) VALUES($1,$2,0)`, f.FindingID, s.ID)
		}
	} else {
		err = d.WithEvidenceTx(t.Context(), func(tx *sql.Tx) error {
			return AddFindingTrafficTx(tx, f.FindingID, []PreparedTrafficEvidence{{Ref: TrafficRef{TrafficID: s.SourceTrafficID, Role: "proof"}, Snapshot: s}})
		})
	}
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return task, f.FindingID, s
}

// rawHeads reads the stored heads; both must be sealed and hide the secrets.
func rawHeads(t *testing.T, d *DB, id string) (req, resp string) {
	t.Helper()
	if err := d.QueryRow(`SELECT req_head,resp_head FROM traffic_evidence_snapshots WHERE id=$1`, id).Scan(&req, &resp); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for _, v := range []string{req, resp} {
		if !isEncrypted(v) || strings.Contains(v, evCookie) || strings.Contains(v, evBearer) {
			t.Fatalf("head stored in clear: %q", v)
		}
	}
	return req, resp
}

// assertClearHeads checks the application read and that the stored value is
// sealed exactly once.
func assertClearHeads(t *testing.T, d *DB, findingID int64, want TrafficEvidenceSnapshot) {
	t.Helper()
	got, err := d.GetFindingTraffic(t.Context(), findingID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if len(got.Bindings) != 1 || got.Bindings[0].Snapshot.ReqHead != want.ReqHead || got.Bindings[0].Snapshot.RespHead != want.RespHead || got.Bindings[0].SnapshotID != want.ID {
		t.Fatalf("read back: %+v", got.Bindings)
	}
	req, resp := rawHeads(t, d, want.ID)
	box := activeSecretBox.Load()
	if p, err := box.decrypt(colEvReqHead.aad(), req); err != nil || p != want.ReqHead {
		t.Fatalf("req_head not sealed once: %q %v", p, err)
	}
	if p, err := box.decrypt(colEvRespHead.aad(), resp); err != nil || p != want.RespHead {
		t.Fatalf("resp_head not sealed once: %q %v", p, err)
	}
}
