package intercept

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// Block codes a target request can end with. They are carried in the
// model-facing text of the blocked call.
const (
	// TargetApprovalPending: no decision within the wait bound. The request
	// stays open, so a later approval still creates the pin.
	TargetApprovalPending = "TARGET_APPROVAL_PENDING"
	// TargetDenied: the request was closed without an approval.
	TargetDenied = "TARGET_DENIED"
	// TargetGateUnavailable: the request could not be written or read.
	TargetGateUnavailable = "TARGET_GATE_UNAVAILABLE"
)

// targetPollInterval is how often a waiter re-reads its request row. The poll
// covers a decision taken on another instance that shares the database.
var targetPollInterval = 2 * time.Second

// TargetRequest is one target of a gated call that no pin covers.
type TargetRequest struct {
	Host string // normalised name, IP literal or CIDR; with Port the key of the request
	Port int    // 0 = port not declared
	Kind string
	// ResolvedIPs are the addresses resolved for this request. They are what the
	// human reads and what an approval pins.
	ResolvedIPs []string
	Resolver    string
	ResolvedAt  time.Time
	Reason      string        // no_pin | new_ip | revoked
	Pin         *db.TargetPin // the active pin an approval would extend (new_ip); nil otherwise
	ExemptVoid  bool          // a stored exemption names the target and was void for this call
	// RedirectFrom is the origin (host:port) of the redirect that leads to the
	// target; empty when the call names the target itself.
	RedirectFrom string
}

// TargetResult is the outcome of RequestTargets. Code is empty when every
// request the call waited on was approved (or was decided in between): the
// caller then re-runs the pin lookup and executes only if every target is
// covered. Otherwise Code is the block code and Host, Port and PendingID name
// the request that stopped the call.
type TargetResult struct {
	Code      string
	Host      string
	Port      int
	PendingID int64
	Reason    string
	// AskMerged reports that the ask passed in was carried by a request this call
	// created, so its decision answered both. When false the caller still has to
	// raise the ask on its own.
	AskMerged bool
}

func (s TargetScope) ref() (db.TargetScopeRef, error) {
	ref := db.TargetScopeRef{ConversationID: s.ConversationID}
	if s.TaskID != "" {
		id, err := strconv.ParseInt(s.TaskID, 10, 64)
		if err != nil {
			return ref, fmt.Errorf("target scope: task id %q: %w", s.TaskID, err)
		}
		ref.TaskID = id
	}
	return ref, nil
}

// scopeName is how a request text names what an approval is bound to.
func (s TargetScope) scopeName() string {
	if s.TaskID != "" {
		return "task " + s.TaskID
	}
	return "conversation " + strconv.FormatInt(s.ConversationID, 10)
}

// targetWaiter is one request row a call waits on.
type targetWaiter struct {
	target  TargetRequest
	id      int64 // 0 = the open request was decided in between: nothing to wait for
	created bool  // this call wrote the row
}

// RequestTargets asks a human to approve the targets of one gated call that no
// pin covers, and waits for the decisions up to the scope's wait bound.
//
// There is one open request per (scope, host, port). The first call writes the
// row and emits the approval card once; later calls for the same key attach to
// that row and wait on it. A request is durable and host-level: a call that
// stops waiting (bound elapsed, cancelled) leaves it open, and a later approval
// still creates the pin. Nothing here ever pins: only Decide does, on a click.
//
// ask is the pending ask of a rule or of the judge for the same call, nil when
// there is none. It is merged into the first row this call creates, so one
// click answers both. A merged row is bound to its creating call like a classic
// ask: when that call leaves, the system settles it, and a rule timeout never
// allows it, because a timeout cannot pin.
func (i *Interceptor) RequestTargets(ctx context.Context, scope TargetScope, toolName string, input []byte, targets []TargetRequest, ask *Decision) TargetResult {
	ref, err := scope.ref()
	if err != nil {
		return TargetResult{Code: TargetGateUnavailable, Reason: err.Error()}
	}
	// An approval pins the addresses the request displays, so a request without
	// any is never opened: approving it would pin nothing.
	for _, t := range targets {
		if len(t.ResolvedIPs) == 0 {
			return TargetResult{Code: TargetResolveFailed, Host: t.Host, Port: t.Port,
				Reason: "no address was resolved for " + targetName(t) + ", and an approval never pins an empty address list"}
		}
	}
	if scope.WaitBound <= 0 {
		// A call that never waits cannot own a call-bound row.
		ask = nil
	}

	var res TargetResult
	var merged *targetWaiter
	var mergedAsk Decision
	// Whatever the way out, a merged row never outlives its creating call. This
	// is a no-op once the row is decided.
	defer func() {
		if merged != nil {
			i.settleMerged(merged.id, "denied", "the call left before a decision")
		}
	}()

	waiters := make([]*targetWaiter, 0, len(targets))
	for _, t := range targets {
		w, err := i.openTargetRequest(ctx, ref, scope, toolName, input, t, ask)
		if err != nil {
			res.Code, res.Host, res.Port, res.Reason = TargetGateUnavailable, t.Host, t.Port, err.Error()
			return res
		}
		if w.created && ask != nil {
			merged, mergedAsk, res.AskMerged = w, *ask, true
			ask = nil
		}
		waiters = append(waiters, w)
	}
	if len(waiters) == 0 {
		return res
	}

	blocked := func(w *targetWaiter, code, reason string) TargetResult {
		res.Code, res.Host, res.Port, res.PendingID, res.Reason = code, w.target.Host, w.target.Port, w.id, reason
		return res
	}
	if scope.WaitBound <= 0 {
		return blocked(waiters[0], TargetApprovalPending, "this call does not wait for approvals; the request stays open")
	}
	bound := time.NewTimer(scope.WaitBound)
	defer bound.Stop()

	// The merged row first: its rule timeout runs from the creation of the row.
	if merged != nil {
		var ruleTimeout <-chan time.Time
		if mergedAsk.TimeoutEnabled {
			secs := mergedAsk.TimeoutSeconds
			if secs <= 0 {
				secs = 60
			}
			timer := time.NewTimer(time.Duration(secs) * time.Second)
			defer timer.Stop()
			ruleTimeout = timer.C
		}
		status, reason := "", ""
		switch st := i.awaitTarget(ctx, merged.id, bound.C, ruleTimeout); st {
		case "allowed":
		case waitRuleTimeout:
			status, reason = "timeout", "approval timed out"
			if mergedAsk.TimeoutAction == "allow" {
				reason += `; the timeout action "allow" was overridden, because a timeout cannot pin a target`
			}
		case waitElapsed:
			status, reason = "timeout", "no approval within the wait bound"
		case waitCancelled:
			status, reason = "denied", "work cancelled"
		case waitGone:
			return blocked(merged, TargetGateUnavailable, "the approval request no longer exists")
		default:
			return blocked(merged, TargetDenied, "the request was denied")
		}
		// A human decision that lands while the call is leaving still counts.
		if status != "" && (i.settleMerged(merged.id, status, reason) || !i.targetAllowed(merged.id)) {
			return blocked(merged, TargetDenied, reason)
		}
	}

	for _, w := range waiters {
		if w == merged || w.id == 0 {
			continue
		}
		st := i.awaitTarget(ctx, w.id, bound.C, nil)
		if (st == "denied" || st == "timeout") && !w.created && i.wasMerged(w.id) {
			// The row this call attached to was bound to another call and closed
			// with it. That says nothing about the host: ask once more, with a
			// plain request.
			retry, err := i.openTargetRequest(ctx, ref, scope, toolName, input, w.target, nil)
			if err != nil {
				return blocked(w, TargetGateUnavailable, err.Error())
			}
			if retry.id == 0 {
				continue
			}
			w = retry
			st = i.awaitTarget(ctx, w.id, bound.C, nil)
		}
		switch st {
		case "allowed":
		case waitElapsed:
			return blocked(w, TargetApprovalPending, "no approval within the wait bound; the request stays open")
		case waitCancelled:
			return blocked(w, TargetApprovalPending, "work cancelled; the request stays open")
		case waitGone:
			return blocked(w, TargetGateUnavailable, "the approval request no longer exists")
		default:
			return blocked(w, TargetDenied, "the request was denied")
		}
	}
	return res
}

// openTargetRequest finds or creates the request row for one target. When this
// call writes the row it emits the approval card; an attaching call writes and
// emits nothing, and never rewrites the addresses a human may be reading.
func (i *Interceptor) openTargetRequest(ctx context.Context, ref db.TargetScopeRef, scope TargetScope, toolName string, input []byte, t TargetRequest, ask *Decision) (*targetWaiter, error) {
	i.mu.RLock()
	proxied := i.upstreamProxy
	i.mu.RUnlock()
	// Behind the upstream proxy the proxy chooses the address: the approval is
	// for the name, and the pin created from this row says so.
	nameOnly := proxied != nil && proxied()

	dec := Decision{Action: "ask"}
	if ask != nil {
		dec = *ask
	}
	dec.Message = targetReason(scope, t, ask, nameOnly)
	audit := auditFor(ctx, dec, input, "pending")
	audit.MergedAsk = ask != nil
	target := db.InterceptTarget{
		Host: t.Host, Port: t.Port, Kind: t.Kind,
		ResolvedIPs: t.ResolvedIPs, Resolver: t.Resolver, ResolvedAt: t.ResolvedAt,
		Reason: t.Reason, Outcome: "requested", NameOnlyEffective: nameOnly, ExemptVoid: t.ExemptVoid,
		RedirectFrom: t.RedirectFrom,
	}
	if t.Pin != nil {
		target.PinID, target.PinVersion, target.PinnedIPs = t.Pin.ID, t.Pin.Version, t.Pin.PinnedIPs
	}
	audit.Targets = []db.InterceptTarget{target}

	_, agentName := taskInfoFromCtx(ctx)
	id, created, err := i.db.FindOrCreateTargetRequest(db.TargetRequest{
		Scope: ref, Host: t.Host, Port: t.Port, RuleID: dec.RuleID,
		AgentName: agentName, ToolName: toolName, ToolInput: input, Reason: dec.Message, Audit: audit,
	})
	if err != nil {
		return nil, err
	}
	w := &targetWaiter{target: t, id: id, created: created}
	if !created {
		return w, nil
	}
	if ask != nil {
		// Call-bound like a classic ask: the result of this call belongs to the row.
		i.bindResult(ctx, id, audit)
	}
	detail, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
		"pending_id": id,
		"tool":       toolName,
		"input":      json.RawMessage(input),
	})
	activity := db.Activity{
		Kind:    "intercept_request",
		Summary: fmt.Sprintf("tool %s requests approval for target %s (#%d)", toolName, targetName(t), id),
		Detail:  string(detail),
	}
	if scope.ConversationID != 0 {
		_, _ = i.db.AppendConvActivity(scope.ConversationID, activity)
	} else if emit := taskEmitFromCtx(ctx); emit != nil {
		emit(activity)
	}
	return w, nil
}

// Ways a wait ends without a decision on the row.
const (
	waitElapsed     = "wait_elapsed"      // the scope's wait bound
	waitRuleTimeout = "wait_rule_timeout" // the timeout of a merged ask
	waitCancelled   = "wait_cancelled"    // the call's context
	waitGone        = "wait_gone"         // the row no longer exists (its conversation was deleted)
)

// awaitTarget waits for the decision on one request row and returns its status
// (allowed | denied | timeout) or the way the wait ended. It never settles the
// row. The row is re-read before each wait: that covers a decision taken before
// the waiter registered, and one taken on another instance.
func (i *Interceptor) awaitTarget(ctx context.Context, id int64, bound, ruleTimeout <-chan time.Time) string {
	ch := i.pending.add(id)
	defer i.pending.remove(id, ch)
	poll := time.NewTicker(targetPollInterval)
	defer poll.Stop()
	for {
		row, err := i.db.GetInterceptPending(id)
		if err == nil && row == nil {
			return waitGone
		}
		if err == nil && row.Status != "pending" {
			return row.Status
		}
		select {
		case <-ch:
		case <-poll.C:
		case <-bound:
			return waitElapsed
		case <-ruleTimeout:
			return waitRuleTimeout
		case <-ctx.Done():
			return waitCancelled
		}
	}
}

// settleMerged closes a merged row on behalf of its creating call, which is
// leaving, and wakes the calls attached to it. It reports whether the row was
// still open; a merged row closed this way never pins.
func (i *Interceptor) settleMerged(id int64, status, reason string) bool {
	resolved, err := i.db.ResolveIntercept(id, status, "deny", reason, "system")
	if err != nil || !resolved {
		return false
	}
	i.pending.resolve(id, false)
	return true
}

func (i *Interceptor) targetAllowed(id int64) bool {
	row, err := i.db.GetInterceptPending(id)
	return err == nil && row != nil && row.Status == "allowed"
}

func (i *Interceptor) wasMerged(id int64) bool {
	detail, err := i.db.GetInterceptDetail(id)
	return err == nil && detail != nil && detail.Audit != nil && detail.Audit.MergedAsk
}

func targetName(t TargetRequest) string {
	if t.Port == 0 {
		return t.Host
	}
	return net.JoinHostPort(t.Host, strconv.Itoa(t.Port))
}

// targetReason is the text a human reads before deciding: host, port, the
// addresses an approval pins, and what the approval is bound to.
func targetReason(scope TargetScope, t TargetRequest, ask *Decision, nameOnly bool) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	if ask != nil && ask.Message != "" {
		b.WriteString(ask.Message)
		b.WriteString("\nThis call also names a target that needs approval. ")
	}
	if t.RedirectFrom != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "A redirect from %s leads to this target; the redirect was not followed. ", t.RedirectFrom)
	}
	name, bound := targetName(t), scope.scopeName()
	if t.Port == 0 {
		name += " (port not declared: every port)"
	}
	ips := strings.Join(t.ResolvedIPs, ", ")
	if t.Pin != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Target %s is pinned for %s (pin v%d: %s) and now resolves to %s (resolver: %s).",
			name, bound, t.Pin.Version, strings.Join(t.Pin.PinnedIPs, ", "), ips, t.Resolver)
	} else {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "Target %s is not approved for %s. It resolves to %s (resolver: %s).", name, bound, ips, t.Resolver)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, " Approving pins these addresses for %s until revoked.", bound)
	if nameOnly {
		b.WriteString(" Egress goes through the upstream proxy, which chooses the address it connects to." +
			" The addresses listed are what the platform resolved. This approval is name-only." +
			" The platform does not bind the connection to these addresses.")
	}
	return b.String()
}

package intercept

import (
	"context"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"sync/atomic"
	"testing"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

func TestPendingWakesAllWaiters(t *testing.T) {
	p := newPendingManager()
	a, b, gone := p.add(1), p.add(1), p.add(1)
	other := p.add(2)
	p.remove(1, gone)
	p.resolve(1, true)
	for name, ch := range map[string]chan bool{"first": a, "second": b} {
		select {
		case allowed := <-ch:
			if !allowed {
				t.Fatalf("%s waiter got a denial", name)
			}
		default:
			t.Fatalf("%s waiter of the request was not woken", name)
		}
	}
	select {
	case <-gone:
		t.Fatal("a removed waiter was woken")
	case <-other:
		t.Fatal("a waiter of another request was woken")
	default:
	}
	if len(p.ch) != 1 || len(p.ch[2]) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("waiters left = %v, want only the one of request 2", p.ch)
	}
	// Resolving a request nobody waits on, twice, blocks nobody.
	p.resolve(1, true)
	p.resolve(2, false)
	if allowed := <-other; allowed {
		t.Fatal("the waiter of request 2 got an approval")
	}
	p.remove(2, other)
	if len(p.ch) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("waiters left = %v, want none", p.ch)
	}
}

func targetTestDB(t *testing.T) *db.DB {
	t.Helper()
	dsn, _, err := db.DSN()
	if err != nil {
		t.Skipf("no database config (%v) - skipping", err)
	}
	d, err := db.Open(dsn)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { d.Close() })
	return d
}

// taskScope creates a task and returns its target scope on ic, with the gate
// on and the given wait bound.
func taskScope(t *testing.T, d *db.DB, ic *Interceptor, wait time.Duration) TargetScope {
	t.Helper()
	task, err := d.CreateTaskWithOptions("target requests", "request, wait, decide", db.TaskCreateOptions{})
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	id := strconv.FormatInt(task.ID, 10)
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = d.DeleteTask(task.ID)
		_, _ = d.Exec(`DELETE FROM target_pins WHERE task_id=$1`, task.ID)
		_, _ = d.Exec(`DELETE FROM intercept_pending WHERE task_id=$1`, id)
	})
	return TargetScope{TaskID: id, Enabled: func() bool { return true }, WaitBound: wait, Interceptor: ic}
}

func (s TargetScope) dbRef(t *testing.T) db.TargetScopeRef {
	t.Helper()
	ref, err := s.ref()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return ref
}

func target(host string, port int, ips ...string) TargetRequest {
	return TargetRequest{Host: host, Port: port, Kind: "domain", ResolvedIPs: ips, Resolver: "system", ResolvedAt: time.Now().UTC(), Reason: "no_pin"}
}

var webFetchInput = []byte(`{"url":"https://app.example.com/"}`)

// request runs RequestTargets in the background and returns the channel its
// result arrives on.
func request(ctx context.Context, ic *Interceptor, scope TargetScope, ask *Decision, targets ...TargetRequest) <-chan TargetResult {
	out := make(chan TargetResult, 1)
	go func() { out <- ic.RequestTargets(ctx, scope, "WebFetch", webFetchInput, targets, ask) }()
	return out
}

func result(t *testing.T, ch <-chan TargetResult) TargetResult {
	t.Helper()
	select {
	case res := <-ch:
		return res
	case <-time.After(20 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the call is still waiting")
		return TargetResult{}
	}
}

func stillWaiting(t *testing.T, ch <-chan TargetResult) {
	t.Helper()
	select {
	case res := <-ch:
		t.Fatalf("the call returned %+v, want it still waiting", res)
	case <-time.After(4 * targetPollInterval):
	}
}

func eventually(t *testing.T, what string, cond func() bool) {
	t.Helper()
	deadline := time.Now().Add(20 * time.Second)
	for !cond() {
		if time.Now().After(deadline) {
			t.Fatalf("timed out waiting for %s", what)
		}
		time.Sleep(5 * time.Millisecond)
	}
}

// openRows returns the ids of the open target requests of scope, oldest first.
func openRows(t *testing.T, d *db.DB, scope TargetScope) []int64 {
	t.Helper()
	rows, err := d.Query(`SELECT id FROM intercept_pending
WHERE COALESCE(task_id,'')=$1 AND COALESCE(conversation_id,0)=$2 AND status='pending' AND target_key IS NOT NULL ORDER BY id`,
		scope.TaskID, scope.ConversationID)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	defer rows.Close()
	var ids []int64
	for rows.Next() {
		var id int64
		if err := rows.Scan(&id); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		ids = append(ids, id)
	}
	return ids
}

func allRows(t *testing.T, d *db.DB, scope TargetScope) int {
	t.Helper()
	var n int
	if err := d.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM intercept_pending
WHERE COALESCE(task_id,'')=$1 AND COALESCE(conversation_id,0)=$2 AND target_key IS NOT NULL`, scope.TaskID, scope.ConversationID).Scan(&n); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return n
}

// waiters is how many calls wait on request id through ic.
func waiters(ic *Interceptor, id int64) int {
	ic.pending.mu.Lock()
	defer ic.pending.mu.Unlock()
	return len(ic.pending.ch[id])
}

// oneOpenRow waits for the scope's single open request and returns its id.
func oneOpenRow(t *testing.T, d *db.DB, scope TargetScope) int64 {
	t.Helper()
	var ids []int64
	eventually(t, "one open target request", func() bool {
		ids = openRows(t, d, scope)
		return len(ids) == 1
	})
	return ids[0]
}

func pins(t *testing.T, d *db.DB, scope TargetScope) []*db.TargetPin {
	t.Helper()
	out, err := d.ListTargetPins(scope.dbRef(t))
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return out
}

// Calls for one host share one request, in one process and across two
// instances on one database: one row, one card, one decision wakes them all,
// one pin.
func TestConcurrentCallsSameHostShareOneRequest(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	first, second := New(d), New(targetTestDB(t))
	scope := taskScope(t, d, first, time.Minute)
	var cards atomic.Int32
	ctx := WithTaskContext(context.Background(), scope.TaskID, "work#1", func(a db.Activity) {
		if a.Kind == "intercept_request" {
			cards.Add(1)
		}
	})
	tgt := target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7")
	a := request(ctx, first, scope, nil, tgt)
	id := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
	b := request(ctx, first, scope, nil, tgt)
	c := request(ctx, second, scope, nil, tgt)
	eventually(t, "every call to wait on the request", func() bool { return waiters(first, id) == 2 && waiters(second, id) == 1 })
	if ids := openRows(t, d, scope); len(ids) != 1 || allRows(t, d, scope) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("open requests = %v, want the one row %d", ids, id)
	}
	if n := cards.Load(); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d approval cards emitted, want 1", n)
	}
	stillWaiting(t, a)

	// Decided on the second instance: its own waiter is woken by the channel,
	// the waiters of the first instance by their poll.
	if err := second.Decide(id, true, "HIVE", "198.51.100.9"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	for name, ch := range map[string]<-chan TargetResult{"creator": a, "attached": b, "other instance": c} {
		if res := result(t, ch); res.Code != "" {
			t.Fatalf("%s call: %+v, want approved", name, res)
		}
	}
	got := pins(t, d, scope)
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0].Status != db.TargetPinActive || got[0].Host != "app.example.com" || got[0].Port != 443 ||
		!slices.Equal(got[0].PinnedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.7"}) {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %+v, want one active pin", got)
	}
	if allRows(t, d, scope) != 1 || cards.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("rows=%d cards=%d after the decision, want 1 and 1", allRows(t, d, scope), cards.Load())
	}
	if err := first.Decide(id, false, "HIVE", ""); err != ErrAlreadyDecided {
		t.Fatalf("second decision: %v, want ErrAlreadyDecided", err)
	}
}

// A call that stops waiting leaves the request alone: it stays open, the next
// call attaches to it, and a later approval still pins.
func TestWaiterLeavingKeepsRequestOpen(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	tgt := target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7")
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	call := request(ctx, ic, scope, nil, tgt)
	id := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
	eventually(t, "the call to wait", func() bool { return waiters(ic, id) == 1 })
	cancel()
	res := result(t, call)
	if res.Code != TargetApprovalPending || res.PendingID != id || res.Host != "app.example.com" || res.Port != 443 {
		t.Fatalf("cancelled call: %+v, want %s on request %d", res, TargetApprovalPending, id)
	}
	row, err := d.GetInterceptPending(id)
	if err != nil || row == nil || row.Status != "pending" || row.DecidedBy != "" {
		t.Fatalf("request after its waiter left = %+v, %v; want untouched", row, err)
	}
	if waiters(ic, id) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("the waiter that left is still registered")
	}

	again := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, tgt)
	eventually(t, "the next call to attach", func() bool { return waiters(ic, id) == 1 })
	if ids := openRows(t, d, scope); !slices.Equal(ids, []int64{id}) {
		t.Fatalf("open requests = %v, want the same row %d", ids, id)
	}
	if err := ic.Decide(id, true, "HIVE", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res := result(t, again); res.Code != "" {
		t.Fatalf("attached call: %+v, want approved", res)
	}
	if got := pins(t, d, scope); len(got) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %+v, want the late approval to pin", got)
	}
}

func TestWaitBoundReturnsPendingCode(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, 150*time.Millisecond)
	tgt := target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7")
	start := time.Now()
	res := result(t, request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, tgt))
	if res.Code != TargetApprovalPending || res.PendingID == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("bounded call: %+v, want %s", res, TargetApprovalPending)
	}
	if waited := time.Since(start); waited < 150*time.Millisecond {
		t.Fatalf("the call returned after %v, before its wait bound", waited)
	}
	if ids := openRows(t, d, scope); !slices.Equal(ids, []int64{res.PendingID}) {
		t.Fatalf("open requests = %v, want the request %d left open", ids, res.PendingID)
	}

	// Bound 0 (the final settlement round): never wait, but still ask.
	never := scope
	never.WaitBound = 0
	other := target("other.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.8")
	res = result(t, request(context.Background(), ic, never, nil, other))
	if res.Code != TargetApprovalPending || res.Host != "other.example.com" || res.PendingID == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("zero-bound call: %+v, want an immediate %s", res, TargetApprovalPending)
	}
	if len(openRows(t, d, scope)) != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("open requests = %v, want the zero-bound call to have created its request", openRows(t, d, scope))
	}
	// An ask is never merged into a row the call does not wait on.
	asked := ic.RequestTargets(context.Background(), never, "WebFetch", webFetchInput,
		[]TargetRequest{target("third.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.9")}, &Decision{Action: "ask", Message: "rule asks"})
	if asked.Code != TargetApprovalPending || asked.AskMerged {
		t.Fatalf("zero-bound call with an ask: %+v, want a plain open request", asked)
	}
	if row, err := d.GetInterceptPending(asked.PendingID); err != nil || row == nil || row.Status != "pending" {
		t.Fatalf("request of the zero-bound call = %+v, %v; want left open", row, err)
	}
}

func askRule(t *testing.T, d *db.DB, timeoutEnabled bool, seconds int, action string) Decision {
	t.Helper()
	rule, err := d.CreateInterceptRule(fmt.Sprintf("target merge %d", time.Now().UnixNano()), "tool_name", "string",
		"NoSuchToolForTargetMerge", "ask", "", 0, false, timeoutEnabled, seconds, action)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = d.DeleteInterceptRule(rule.ID) })
	return Decision{Action: "ask", Message: "rule requires approval", RuleID: rule.ID, RuleName: rule.Name,
		TimeoutEnabled: timeoutEnabled, TimeoutSeconds: seconds, TimeoutAction: action}
}

// A merged row is bound to the call that created it: when that call leaves, the
// system closes the row, and nothing is pinned.
func TestMergedRequestSettledWhenCreatorLeaves(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	ask := askRule(t, d, false, 0, "deny")
	ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
	call := request(ctx, ic, scope, &ask, target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7"))
	id := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
	detail, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(id)
	if err != nil || detail == nil || detail.RuleID == nil || *detail.RuleID != ask.RuleID || detail.DecisionSource != "target" ||
		detail.Audit == nil || !detail.Audit.MergedAsk || detail.Audit.RuleName != ask.RuleName || len(detail.Audit.Targets) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("merged row = %+v, %v; want the rule and the target on one row", detail, err)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(detail.Reason, "rule requires approval") || !strings.Contains(detail.Reason, "app.example.com:443") ||
		!strings.Contains(detail.Reason, "203.0.113.7") || !strings.Contains(detail.Reason, "Approving pins these addresses for task "+scope.TaskID+" until revoked.") {
		t.Fatalf("merged reason does not name both the ask and the target: %q", detail.Reason)
	}
	eventually(t, "the creating call to wait", func() bool { return waiters(ic, id) == 1 })
	cancel()
	res := result(t, call)
	if res.Code != TargetDenied || !res.AskMerged || res.PendingID != id {
		t.Fatalf("creating call after cancel: %+v, want %s with the ask merged", res, TargetDenied)
	}
	row, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(id)
	if err != nil || row == nil || row.Status != "denied" || row.DecidedBy != "system" || row.Audit.EffectiveAction != "deny" ||
		row.Audit.DecisionReason != "work cancelled" {
		t.Fatalf("merged row after its creator left = %+v, %v; want denied by the system", row, err)
	}
	if got := pins(t, d, scope); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("a row closed by the system pinned: %+v", got)
	}
}

// A timeout never pins, whatever the rule says: timeout_action = allow is
// overridden on a merged row and the override is recorded.
func TestTimeoutNeverPins(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	ask := askRule(t, d, true, 1, "allow")
	res := result(t, request(context.Background(), ic, scope, &ask, target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7")))
	if res.Code != TargetDenied || !res.AskMerged {
		t.Fatalf("call after the rule timeout: %+v, want %s", res, TargetDenied)
	}
	row, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(res.PendingID)
	if err != nil || row == nil || row.Status != "timeout" || row.DecidedBy != "system" || row.Audit.EffectiveAction != "deny" ||
		row.Audit.ExecutionStatus != "not_executed" || !strings.Contains(row.Audit.DecisionReason, `timeout action "allow" was overridden`) {
		t.Fatalf("timed-out merged row = %+v, %v; want a timeout that denies and records the override", row, err)
	}
	if got := pins(t, d, scope); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("a timeout pinned: %+v", got)
	}
	if len(openRows(t, d, scope)) != 0 {
		t.Fatal("the merged row is still open after its creator left")
	}
}

// What is displayed is what is pinned: the addresses stored when the row was
// created. A call that attaches with other addresses never rewrites them.
func TestDecidePinsDisplayedIPs(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	creator := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.8", "203.0.113.7"))
	id := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
	attached := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, target("app.example.com", 443, "198.51.100.66"))
	eventually(t, "both calls to wait", func() bool { return waiters(ic, id) == 2 })
	shown, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(id)
	if err != nil || shown == nil || len(shown.Audit.Targets) != 1 ||
		!slices.Equal(shown.Audit.Targets[0].ResolvedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.8", "203.0.113.7"}) || strings.Contains(shown.Reason, "198.51.100.66") {
		t.Fatalf("displayed request = %+v, %v; want the creator's addresses only", shown, err)
	}
	if err := ic.Decide(id, true, "HIVE", "198.51.100.9"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res := result(t, creator); res.Code != "" {
		t.Fatalf("creator: %+v", res)
	}
	if res := result(t, attached); res.Code != "" {
		t.Fatalf("attached: %+v", res)
	}
	got := pins(t, d, scope)
	if len(got) != 1 || !slices.Equal(got[0].PinnedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.7", "203.0.113.8"}) || got[0].InterceptID == nil || *got[0].InterceptID != id {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %+v, want exactly the displayed addresses", got)
	}
}

func TestDeniedRequestPinsNothing(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	tgt := target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7")
	call := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, tgt)
	id := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
	if err := ic.Decide(id, false, "HIVE", "198.51.100.9"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res := result(t, call); res.Code != TargetDenied || res.PendingID != id {
		t.Fatalf("denied call: %+v, want %s", res, TargetDenied)
	}
	if got := pins(t, d, scope); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("a denial pinned: %+v", got)
	}
	row, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(id)
	if err != nil || row == nil || row.Status != "denied" || row.DecidedBy != "human" || row.Audit.Targets[0].Outcome != "denied" ||
		row.Audit.Approver != "HIVE" || row.Audit.ApproverAddr != "198.51.100.9" {
		t.Fatalf("denied row = %+v, %v", row, err)
	}
	// No sticky denial: the next call asks again, on a new row.
	next := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, tgt)
	if fresh := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope); fresh == id {
		t.Fatal("the next call reused the denied row")
	} else if err := ic.Decide(fresh, true, "HIVE", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res := result(t, next); res.Code != "" {
		t.Fatalf("call after the denial: %+v, want approved", res)
	}
}

// A call attached to a merged row that closes without an approval is not
// blocked for the host: the row was about another call. It asks once more with
// a plain request, then blocks.
func TestAttachedWaiterRequeuesAfterMergedDenial(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	for _, approveRetry := range []bool{true, false} {
		t.Run(fmt.Sprintf("retry approved=%v", approveRetry), func(t *testing.T) {
			ic := New(d)
			scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
			ask := askRule(t, d, false, 0, "deny")
			tgt := target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7")
			creator := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, &ask, tgt)
			merged := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
			attached := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, tgt)
			eventually(t, "both calls to wait", func() bool { return waiters(ic, merged) == 2 })
			if err := ic.Decide(merged, false, "HIVE", ""); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			if res := result(t, creator); res.Code != TargetDenied || !res.AskMerged {
				t.Fatalf("creator of the merged row: %+v, want %s", res, TargetDenied)
			}
			var retry int64
			eventually(t, "the attached call to ask again", func() bool {
				ids := openRows(t, d, scope)
				if len(ids) == 1 && ids[0] != merged {
					retry = ids[0]
				}
				return retry != 0
			})
			plain, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(retry)
			if err != nil || plain == nil || plain.RuleID != nil || plain.Audit.MergedAsk {
				t.Fatalf("retry row = %+v, %v; want a plain target request", plain, err)
			}
			stillWaiting(t, attached)
			if err := ic.Decide(retry, approveRetry, "HIVE", ""); err != nil {
				t.Fatal(err)
			}
			res := result(t, attached)
			if approveRetry && (res.Code != "" || len(pins(t, d, scope)) != 1) {
				t.Fatalf("attached call after its retry was approved: %+v pins=%+v", res, pins(t, d, scope))
			}
			if !approveRetry && (res.Code != TargetDenied || res.PendingID != retry || len(pins(t, d, scope)) != 0) {
				t.Fatalf("attached call after its retry was denied: %+v, want %s", res, TargetDenied)
			}
			// One retry, then block: never a third request.
			if n := allRows(t, d, scope); n != 2 {
				t.Fatalf("%d request rows, want the merged one and one retry", n)
			}
		})
	}
}

// The request rows of a conversation go with it (cascade). A waiter that finds
// its row gone stops with a block.
func TestWaiterStopsWhenRowDeleted(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	conv, err := d.CreateConversation("assistant", fmt.Sprintf("target wait %d", time.Now().UnixNano()), nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = d.DeleteConversation(conv.ID)
		_, _ = d.Exec(`DELETE FROM target_pins WHERE conversation_id=$1`, conv.ID)
	})
	scope := TargetScope{ConversationID: conv.ID, Enabled: func() bool { return true }, WaitBound: time.Minute, Interceptor: ic}
	call := request(WithConvID(context.Background(), conv.ID), ic, scope, nil, target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7"))
	id := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
	eventually(t, "the call to wait", func() bool { return waiters(ic, id) == 1 })
	// The card went to the conversation stream.
	var cards int
	if err := d.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM conversation_activities WHERE conversation_id=$1 AND kind='intercept_request'`, conv.ID).Scan(&cards); err != nil || cards != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d approval cards in the conversation (%v), want 1", cards, err)
	}
	if err := d.DeleteConversation(conv.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res := result(t, call); res.Code != TargetGateUnavailable || res.PendingID != id {
		t.Fatalf("call whose request was deleted: %+v, want %s", res, TargetGateUnavailable)
	}
}

// Every human decision records who took it and from where: on the pin and in
// the audit of a target row, in the audit of a classic ask. decided_by on the
// row stays the actor class.
func TestDecideRecordsApproverAndAddress(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	call := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7"))
	id := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
	if err := ic.Decide(id, true, "HIVE", "198.51.100.9"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res := result(t, call); res.Code != "" {
		t.Fatalf("approved call: %+v", res)
	}
	got := pins(t, d, scope)
	if len(got) != 1 || got[0].DecidedBy != "HIVE" || got[0].DecidedFrom != "198.51.100.9" {
		t.Fatalf("pin = %+v, want the approver and the address", got)
	}
	row, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(id)
	if err != nil || row == nil || row.DecidedBy != "human" || row.Audit.Approver != "HIVE" || row.Audit.ApproverAddr != "198.51.100.9" {
		t.Fatalf("target row = %+v, %v", row, err)
	}

	// A classic ask goes through the same Decide and records the same.
	ctx := WithTaskContext(context.Background(), scope.TaskID, "work#1", nil)
	allowed := make(chan bool, 1)
	go func() {
		allowed <- ic.HandleAsk(ctx, 0, Decision{Action: "ask", Message: "classic ask"}, "Bash", []byte(`{"command":"id"}`))
	}()
	var classic int64
	eventually(t, "the classic ask", func() bool {
		return d.QueryRow(`SELECT id FROM intercept_pending WHERE task_id=$1 AND status='pending' AND target_key IS NULL`, scope.TaskID).Scan(&classic) == nil
	})
	eventually(t, "the classic ask to wait", func() bool { return waiters(ic, classic) == 1 })
	if err := ic.Decide(classic, true, "HIVE", "198.51.100.10"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	select {
	case ok := <-allowed:
		if !ok {
			t.Fatal("the approved classic ask was refused")
		}
	case <-time.After(20 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the classic ask is still waiting")
	}
	row, err = d.GetInterceptDetail(classic)
	if err != nil || row == nil || row.Status != "allowed" || row.DecidedBy != "human" || row.Audit == nil ||
		row.Audit.Approver != "HIVE" || row.Audit.ApproverAddr != "198.51.100.10" || len(row.Audit.Targets) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("classic row = %+v, %v; want the approver and the address in its audit", row, err)
	}
	if len(pins(t, d, scope)) != 1 {
		t.Fatal("approving a classic ask pinned something")
	}
}

// Behind the upstream proxy the proxy chooses the address: the request says the
// approval is name-only and the pin carries the mark. The mark stays when the
// proxy is removed; addresses are enforced again only after a new approval.
func TestPinUnderGlobalProxyIsNameOnly(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	var proxied atomic.Bool
	ic.SetUpstreamProxyCheck(proxied.Load)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	const sentence = "This approval is name-only."
	approve := func(host string) (*db.TargetPin, string) {
		t.Helper()
		call := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, target(host, 443, "203.0.113.7"))
		id := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
		row, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(id)
		if err != nil || row == nil {
			t.Fatalf("request row: %+v, %v", row, err)
		}
		if err := ic.Decide(id, true, "HIVE", ""); err != nil {
			t.Fatal(err)
		}
		if res := result(t, call); res.Code != "" {
			t.Fatalf("approved call: %+v", res)
		}
		active, err := d.ActiveTargetPins(scope.dbRef(t), host, 443)
		if err != nil || len(active) != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("active pins of %s = %+v, %v", host, active, err)
		}
		return active[0], row.Reason
	}

	direct, reason := approve("direct.example.com")
	if direct.NameOnlyEffective || strings.Contains(reason, sentence) {
		t.Fatalf("without a proxy: pin=%+v reason=%q, want an address pin", direct, reason)
	}

	proxied.Store(true)
	named, reason := approve("proxied.example.com")
	if !named.NameOnlyEffective || !strings.Contains(reason, sentence) || !strings.Contains(reason, "upstream proxy") {
		t.Fatalf("behind the proxy: pin=%+v reason=%q, want a name-only pin and a request that says so", named, reason)
	}
	if !slices.Equal(named.PinnedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.7"}) {
		t.Fatalf("name-only pin addresses = %v, want what the platform resolved", named.PinnedIPs)
	}

	// The proxy is removed: the pin stays name-only, the address pin stays one.
	proxied.Store(false)
	ref := scope.dbRef(t)
	if still, err := d.ActiveTargetPins(ref, "proxied.example.com", 443); err != nil || len(still) != 1 || !still[0].NameOnlyEffective {
		t.Fatalf("name-only pin after the proxy was removed = %+v, %v; want still name-only", still, err)
	}
	if still, err := d.ActiveTargetPins(ref, "direct.example.com", 443); err != nil || len(still) != 1 || still[0].NameOnlyEffective {
		t.Fatalf("address pin = %+v, %v", still, err)
	}
	// Enforcing addresses again takes a revocation and a new approval.
	if _, err := d.RevokeTargetPin(ref, named.ID); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if again, _ := approve("proxied.example.com"); again.NameOnlyEffective || again.Version != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("pin approved after the proxy was removed = %+v, want an address pin, version 2", again)
	}
}

// A new_ip request shows the old version, the pinned addresses and the new
// ones, and its approval extends the pin.
func TestNewIPRequestShowsOldAndNewAddresses(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	first := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, target("app.example.com", 0, "203.0.113.7"))
	id := oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
	if row, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(id); err != nil || row == nil || !strings.Contains(row.Reason, "app.example.com (port not declared: every port)") {
		t.Fatalf("port-0 request = %+v, %v; want the reason to say the port is not declared", row, err)
	}
	if err := ic.Decide(id, true, "HIVE", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res := result(t, first); res.Code != "" {
		t.Fatalf("first call: %+v", res)
	}
	v1 := pins(t, d, scope)[0]

	moved := target("app.example.com", 0, "203.0.113.99")
	moved.Reason, moved.Pin = "new_ip", v1
	second := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, nil, moved)
	id = oneOpenRow(t, d, scope)
	row, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(id)
	if err != nil || row == nil || !strings.Contains(row.Reason, "pin v1: 203.0.113.7") || !strings.Contains(row.Reason, "now resolves to 203.0.113.99") {
		t.Fatalf("new_ip request = %+v, %v; want the old version, the pinned and the new addresses", row, err)
	}
	if got := row.Audit.Targets[0]; got.Reason != "new_ip" || got.PinID != v1.ID || got.PinVersion != 1 || !slices.Equal(got.PinnedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.7"}) {
		t.Fatalf("recorded target = %+v", got)
	}
	if err := ic.Decide(id, true, "HIVE", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if res := result(t, second); res.Code != "" {
		t.Fatalf("second call: %+v", res)
	}
	active, err := d.ActiveTargetPins(scope.dbRef(t), "app.example.com", 0)
	if err != nil || len(active) != 1 || active[0].Version != 2 || !slices.Equal(active[0].PinnedIPs, []string{"203.0.113.7", "203.0.113.99"}) {
		t.Fatalf("pin after the new_ip approval = %+v, %v; want v2 with both addresses", active, err)
	}
}

// One call, several targets: one request per host and port, and the call
// passes only when all of them are approved.
func TestSeveralTargetsNeedEveryApproval(t *testing.T) {
	d := targetTestDB(t)
	ic := New(d)
	scope := taskScope(t, d, ic, time.Minute)
	ask := askRule(t, d, false, 0, "deny")
	call := request(context.Background(), ic, scope, &ask,
		target("a.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.1"), target("b.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.2"))
	var ids []int64
	eventually(t, "two open requests", func() bool {
		ids = openRows(t, d, scope)
		return len(ids) == 2
	})
	// The ask is merged into the first row the call created; the other is plain.
	for n, id := range ids {
		row, err := d.GetInterceptDetail(id)
		if err != nil || row == nil || row.Audit.MergedAsk != (n == 0) || (row.RuleID != nil) != (n == 0) {
			t.Fatalf("row %d = %+v, %v; want the ask merged into the first row only", n, row, err)
		}
	}
	if err := ic.Decide(ids[0], true, "HIVE", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	stillWaiting(t, call)
	if err := ic.Decide(ids[1], false, "HIVE", ""); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	res := result(t, call)
	if res.Code != TargetDenied || res.Host != "b.example.com" || !res.AskMerged {
		t.Fatalf("call with one target denied: %+v, want %s on b.example.com", res, TargetDenied)
	}
	if got := pins(t, d, scope); len(got) != 1 || got[0].Host != "a.example.com" {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %+v, want only the approved host", got)
	}
}

// A scope that names no task and no conversation, or a task id that is not a
// number, never reaches the store.
func TestRequestTargetsRejectsBadScope(t *testing.T) {
	ic := New(nil)
	for name, scope := range map[string]TargetScope{
		"empty":        {WaitBound: time.Minute},
		"both":         {TaskID: "7", ConversationID: 9, WaitBound: time.Minute},
		"task not int": {TaskID: "seven", WaitBound: time.Minute},
	} {
		res := ic.RequestTargets(context.Background(), scope, "WebFetch", webFetchInput, []TargetRequest{target("app.example.com", 443, "203.0.113.7")}, nil)
		if res.Code != TargetGateUnavailable {
			t.Errorf("%s scope: %+v, want %s", name, res, TargetGateUnavailable)
		}
	}
}

=====================================================================
FILE: intercept/target_resolve.go
=====================================================================
package intercept

import (
	"context"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net"
	"net/netip"
	"slices"
	"sync"
	"time"
)

// Resolver turns a host name into its addresses. The gate compares what it
// returns with the addresses a human pinned.
type Resolver interface {
	// Name identifies the resolver in pins and in audit rows.
	Name() string
	// LookupIPs returns the A and AAAA answers for host.
	LookupIPs(ctx context.Context, host string) ([]netip.Addr, error)
}

// SetResolver replaces the resolver of the target gate, which is the system
// resolver unless one is set.
func (i *Interceptor) SetResolver(r Resolver) { i.resolve.use(r) }

// SetBaseDialer replaces the dialer that opens the connections PinnedDialer
// lets through, which is a net.Dialer with the settings of
// http.DefaultTransport unless one is set. Tests use it to map addresses to
// local listeners and to see what was dialled.
func (i *Interceptor) SetBaseDialer(f func(ctx context.Context, network, addr string) (net.Conn, error)) {
	i.mu.Lock()
	i.dial = f
	i.mu.Unlock()
}

// systemResolver is the resolver of the HIVE process. It reads the same
// resolver configuration as the tools that run in the same container.
type systemResolver struct{}

func (systemResolver) Name() string { return "system" }

func (systemResolver) LookupIPs(ctx context.Context, host string) ([]netip.Addr, error) {
	return net.DefaultResolver.LookupNetIP(ctx, "ip", host)
}

const (
	// resolveTimeout bounds one lookup.
	resolveTimeout = 3 * time.Second
	// resolveCacheTTL is how long a positive answer is reused. It bounds latency
	// and resolver load when several calls name one host, and adds at most this
	// much to the time a changed address goes unnoticed.
	resolveCacheTTL = 10 * time.Second
)

// resolution is one positive answer: canonical addresses, sorted, never empty.
type resolution struct {
	ips []string
	at  time.Time
}

type resolveFlight struct {
	done chan struct{}
	res  resolution
	err  error
}

// resolveCache resolves names through one Resolver. Positive answers are kept
// per host for resolveCacheTTL, concurrent lookups for one host collapse into
// one, and a failure or an empty answer is never kept: the next call tries
// again.
type resolveCache struct {
	now func() time.Time

	mu       sync.Mutex
	resolver Resolver
	entries  map[string]resolution
	flights  map[string]*resolveFlight
}

func newResolveCache(r Resolver) *resolveCache {
	return &resolveCache{resolver: r, now: time.Now, entries: map[string]resolution{}, flights: map[string]*resolveFlight{}}
}

// use replaces the resolver and drops the answers of the previous one.
func (c *resolveCache) use(r Resolver) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	c.resolver, c.entries = r, map[string]resolution{}
	c.mu.Unlock()
}

func (c *resolveCache) name() string {
	c.mu.Lock()
	defer c.mu.Unlock()
	return c.resolver.Name()
}

// lookup resolves host. fresh skips the cached answer: it is what a new
// approval request uses, because a human reads and pins those addresses.
func (c *resolveCache) lookup(ctx context.Context, host string, fresh bool) (resolution, error) {
	c.mu.Lock()
	if e, ok := c.entries[host]; ok && !fresh && c.now().Sub(e.at) < resolveCacheTTL {
		c.mu.Unlock()
		return e, nil
	}
	f := c.flights[host]
	if f == nil {
		f = &resolveFlight{done: make(chan struct{})}
		c.flights[host] = f
		go c.fly(c.resolver, host, f)
	}
	c.mu.Unlock()
	select {
	case <-f.done:
		return f.res, f.err
	case <-ctx.Done():
		return resolution{}, ctx.Err()
	}
}

// fly runs the one lookup the waiters of host share. It is not bound to the
// context of the call that started it: that call leaving must not fail the others.
func (c *resolveCache) fly(r Resolver, host string, f *resolveFlight) {
	ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), resolveTimeout)
	defer cancel()
	addrs, err := r.LookupIPs(ctx, host)
	switch {
	case ctx.Err() != nil:
		f.err = fmt.Errorf("lookup timed out after %s", resolveTimeout)
	case err != nil:
		f.err = lookupError(err)
	case len(addrs) == 0:
		f.err = errors.New("the lookup returned no address")
	default:
		f.res = resolution{ips: canonicalIPs(addrs), at: c.now()}
	}
	c.mu.Lock()
	delete(c.flights, host)
	if f.err == nil {
		c.entries[host] = f.res
	}
	c.mu.Unlock()
	close(f.done)
}

// lookupError keeps the part of a resolver error that says what went wrong.
func lookupError(err error) error {
	var dns *net.DNSError
	if errors.As(err, &dns) {
		if dns.IsTimeout {
			return fmt.Errorf("lookup timed out after %s", resolveTimeout)
		}
		if dns.IsNotFound {
			return errors.New("no such host")
		}
		return errors.New(dns.Err)
	}
	return err
}

// canonicalIPs returns the addresses as sorted, unique strings, IPv4-mapped
// addresses unmapped and zones dropped.
func canonicalIPs(addrs []netip.Addr) []string {
	out := make([]string, 0, len(addrs))
	for _, a := range addrs {
		out = append(out, a.Unmap().WithZone("").String())
	}
	slices.Sort(out)
	return slices.Compact(out)
}

// subset reports whether every resolved address is one of the pinned ones. An
// empty answer is never a subset: a lookup that returned nothing matches no pin.
func subset(resolved, pinned []string) bool {
	if len(resolved) == 0 {
		return false
	}
	for _, ip := range resolved {
		if !slices.Contains(pinned, ip) {
			return false
		}
	}
	return true
}

package intercept

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"slices"
	"testing"
)

func TestNormalizeTarget(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		raw  string
		want Target
	}{
		{"case", "HTTPS://App.Example.COM/Admin", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 443}},
		{"trailing dot", "https://app.example.com./", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 443}},
		{"userinfo", "https://user:p@ss@app.example.com/x", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 443}},
		{"userinfo that looks like a host", "http://pinned.example@evil.example/", Target{TargetDomain, "evil.example", 80}},
		{"ipv6 brackets", "http://[2001:DB8::1]/", Target{TargetIP, "2001:db8::1", 80}},
		{"ipv6 brackets and port", "http://[2001:db8::1]:8443/x", Target{TargetIP, "2001:db8::1", 8443}},
		{"ipv4-mapped ipv6", "http://[::ffff:203.0.113.7]/", Target{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 80}},
		{"decimal ipv4", "http://2130706433/", Target{TargetIP, "127.0.0.1", 80}},
		{"hex ipv4", "http://0x7f000001/", Target{TargetIP, "127.0.0.1", 80}},
		{"octal ipv4", "http://0177.0.0.1/", Target{TargetIP, "127.0.0.1", 80}},
		{"short ipv4", "http://127.1/", Target{TargetIP, "127.0.0.1", 80}},
		{"mixed ipv4 forms", "http://0xa9.254.0xa9fe/", Target{TargetIP, "169.254.169.254", 80}},
		{"punycode", "https://bücher.example/", Target{TargetDomain, "xn--bcher-kva.example", 443}},
		{"punycode kept", "https://xn--bcher-kva.example/", Target{TargetDomain, "xn--bcher-kva.example", 443}},
		{"default port http", "http://app.example.com", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 80}},
		{"default port https", "https://app.example.com?x=1", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 443}},
		{"default port ws", "ws://app.example.com/socket", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 80}},
		{"default port wss", "wss://app.example.com/socket", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 443}},
		{"default port ftp", "ftp://files.example.com/pub", Target{TargetDomain, "files.example.com", 21}},
		{"explicit port wins", "https://app.example.com:8443/", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 8443}},
		{"empty port is the default", "https://app.example.com:/", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 443}},
		{"port 0: scheme without a default", "ssh://git.example.com/repo", Target{TargetDomain, "git.example.com", 0}},
		{"port 0: bare host", "app.example.com", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 0}},
		{"host and port", "App.Example.com:8080", Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 8080}},
		{"ip and port", "203.0.113.7:22", Target{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 22}},
		{"bare ipv6", "2001:db8::1", Target{TargetIP, "2001:db8::1", 0}},
		{"ipv6 zone dropped", "fe80::1%eth0", Target{TargetIP, "fe80::1", 0}},
		{"cidr is masked", "10.1.2.3/8", Target{TargetCIDR, "10.0.0.0/8", 0}},
		{"ipv6 cidr", "FD00::/8", Target{TargetCIDR, "fd00::/8", 0}},
		{"underscore label", "http://my_host.internal/", Target{TargetDomain, "my_host.internal", 80}},
		{"percent-encoded host", "http://%65vil.example/", Target{TargetDomain, "evil.example", 80}},
		{"percent-encoded address", "http://127.0.0.1%2e/x", Target{TargetIP, "127.0.0.1", 80}},
		{"a host no profile accepts is kept", "https://-odd-.example/", Target{TargetDomain, "-odd-.example", 443}},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		got, ok := NormalizeTarget(c.raw)
		if !ok || got != c.want {
			t.Errorf("%s: NormalizeTarget(%q) = %+v, %v; want %+v", c.name, c.raw, got, ok, c.want)
		}
	}
	for _, raw := range []string{"", "file:///etc/passwd", "http:///path", "http://app.example.com:99999/", "http://app.example.com:http/", "http://[::1", "10.0.0.0/99"} {
		if got, ok := NormalizeTarget(raw); ok {
			t.Errorf("NormalizeTarget(%q) = %+v, want no target", raw, got)
		}
	}
}

func targetsOf(tool string, input any) []Target {
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(input)
	return ExtractTargets(tool, raw)
}

func command(cmd string) map[string]string { return map[string]string{"command": cmd} }

func wantTargets(t *testing.T, what string, got []Target, want ...Target) {
	t.Helper()
	if !slices.Equal(got, want) {
		t.Errorf("%s: targets = %+v, want %+v", what, got, want)
	}
}

func TestExtractTargets(t *testing.T) {
	app := Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 443}

	// WebFetch names its target exactly.
	wantTargets(t, "WebFetch", targetsOf("WebFetch", map[string]any{"url": "https://App.Example.com/login?next=http://other.example/", "extract": true}), app)
	wantTargets(t, "WebFetch numeric host", targetsOf("WebFetch", map[string]string{"url": "http://2130706433/"}), Target{TargetIP, "127.0.0.1", 80})
	wantTargets(t, "WebFetch without a url", targetsOf("WebFetch", map[string]string{}))

	// The command tools: Bash, shell_open, Monitor (command) and shell_send (text).
	commands := []struct {
		cmd  string
		want []Target
	}{
		{"curl -s https://app.example.com/api | jq .", []Target{app}},
		{"curl -sk 'https://app.example.com:8443/a?b=1&c=http://inner.example/' -o out", []Target{{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 8443}}},
		{"curl http://a.example/;curl http://b.example|sh", []Target{{TargetDomain, "a.example", 80}, {TargetDomain, "b.example", 80}}},
		{"curl -x http://127.0.0.1:8080 https://app.example.com/", []Target{{TargetIP, "127.0.0.1", 8080}, app}},
		{"nmap -sV 203.0.113.7", []Target{{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 0}}},
		{"nmap -p 443 203.0.113.0/24 198.51.100.9", []Target{{TargetCIDR, "203.0.113.0/24", 0}, {TargetIP, "198.51.100.9", 0}}},
		{"nc -v 203.0.113.7:4444", []Target{{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 4444}}},
		{"ssh root@203.0.113.7 -p 22", []Target{{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 0}}},
		{"mysql --host=203.0.113.7 -uroot", []Target{{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 0}}},
		{"openssl s_client -connect app.example.com:443 -servername x", []Target{app}},
		{"nc localhost:8080", []Target{{TargetDomain, "localhost", 8080}}},
		{"ping6 2001:db8::1", []Target{{TargetIP, "2001:db8::1", 0}}},
		{"curl 'http://[2001:db8::1]:8080/'; nc [2001:db8::2]:22", []Target{{TargetIP, "2001:db8::1", 8080}, {TargetIP, "2001:db8::2", 22}}},
		{"nmap fd00::/8 ::ffff:203.0.113.7", []Target{{TargetCIDR, "fd00::/8", 0}, {TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 0}}},
		{"curl https://app.example.com/a https://APP.example.com/b", []Target{app}},
		{"git clone git+ssh://git@code.example.com/x.git", []Target{{TargetDomain, "code.example.com", 0}}},
		{"scp f 203.0.113.7:/tmp/f", []Target{{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 0}}},
		{"docker run -p 203.0.113.7:8080:80 img", []Target{{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 8080}}},
		{"curl 203.0.113.7/2024/report", []Target{{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 0}}},
		{"dig @198.51.100.53 x", []Target{{TargetIP, "198.51.100.53", 0}}},
		// The authority of a URL reads differently quoted and unquoted: both readings are targets.
		{`curl 'http://pinned.example;@evil.example/'`, []Target{{TargetDomain, "evil.example", 80}, {TargetDomain, "pinned.example", 80}}},
		{`curl http://pinned.example\@evil.example/`, []Target{{TargetDomain, "evil.example", 80}, {TargetDomain, "pinned.example", 80}}},
		{`curl "http://pinned.example,x@evil.example:8443/"`, []Target{{TargetDomain, "evil.example", 8443}, {TargetDomain, "pinned.example", 80}}},
		{"curl http://a.example;curl http://b.example&&id", []Target{{TargetDomain, "a.example", 80}, {TargetDomain, "b.example", 80}}},
		{"curl http://user:pw@app.example.com:8443/ http://%65vil.example/", []Target{{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 8443}, {TargetDomain, "evil.example", 80}}},
		// A port the gate cannot read leaves the address a target.
		{"for p in 80 443; do curl http://203.0.113.7:$p/; done", []Target{{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 0}}},
	}
	for _, c := range commands {
		wantTargets(t, "Bash "+c.cmd, targetsOf("Bash", command(c.cmd)), c.want...)
		wantTargets(t, "shell_open "+c.cmd, targetsOf("shell_open", command(c.cmd)), c.want...)
		wantTargets(t, "Monitor "+c.cmd, targetsOf("Monitor", command(c.cmd)), c.want...)
		wantTargets(t, "shell_send "+c.cmd, targetsOf("shell_send", map[string]string{"text": c.cmd + "\n"}), c.want...)
	}
	// Only the command field is read.
	wantTargets(t, "Bash description", targetsOf("Bash", map[string]string{"command": "ls", "description": "see https://app.example.com/"}))
	wantTargets(t, "shell_send session", targetsOf("shell_send", map[string]string{"text": "id\n", "session_id": "203.0.113.7"}))

	// The field is read the way the tool decodes it: a key matches whatever its
	// case, and the last duplicate wins. The gate reads the value that runs.
	for _, c := range []struct{ tool, input string }{
		{"Bash", `{"command":"ls","Command":"curl https://app.example.com/"}`},
		{"Bash", `{"command":"ls","command":"curl https://app.example.com/"}`},
		{"Bash", `{"COMMAND":"curl https://app.example.com/"}`},
		{"Bash", `{"command":"curl https://app.example.com/","timeout":"not a number","text":5}`},
		{"Monitor", `{"command":"ls","cOmMaNd":"curl https://app.example.com/"}`},
		{"shell_send", `{"text":"id","Text":"curl https://app.example.com/\n"}`},
		{"WebFetch", `{"url":"https://pinned.example/","URL":"https://app.example.com/"}`},
		{"WebFetch", `{"url":"https://pinned.example/","url":"https://app.example.com/"}`},
		{"ExecuteExtraTool", `{"tool_name":"list_assets","Tool_Name":"mcp__x__y","params":{"u":"https://pinned.example/"},"PARAMS":{"u":"https://app.example.com/"}}`},
	} {
		wantTargets(t, c.tool+" "+c.input, ExtractTargets(c.tool, []byte(c.input)), app)
	}
	wantTargets(t, "first duplicate does not run", ExtractTargets("Bash", []byte(`{"command":"curl https://app.example.com/","Command":"ls"}`)))
	// A tool the gate does not know may keep either value of a duplicated key: both are read.
	wantTargets(t, "duplicate key, unknown tool", ExtractTargets("mcp__scan__run", []byte(`{"url":"https://app.example.com/","url":"https://other.example.com/"}`)),
		app, Target{TargetDomain, "other.example.com", 443})

	// Things that look close to a target and are not one.
	for _, cmd := range []string{
		"sleep 300; echo 2130706433",
		"pip install requests==2.31.0 && python3 --version",
		"echo v1.2.3.4 > version; tar xf app-1.2.3.4.tgz",
		"date +%H:%M:%S; echo 12:30:45",
		"curl -u admin:1234 -H 'X-Id: 7' file:///etc/hosts",
		"docker run redis:7 && docker pull python:3.12",
		"chown user:1000 f; chmod 600 key.pem",
		"ip link show; echo 00:11:22:33:44:55",
		"echo 999.1.1.1 1.2.3 1.2.3.4.5",
		"python3 -c 'print(a[::-1])'; g++ -std=c++17 x.cc && echo std::cout",
		"cat ./src/main.go:42",
	} {
		wantTargets(t, "Bash "+cmd, targetsOf("Bash", command(cmd)))
	}
}

// Every MCP tool and every deferred custom tool is called through
// ExecuteExtraTool: the gate reads the inner tool name and its parameters.
func TestExtractUnwrapsExecuteExtraTool(t *testing.T) {
	app := Target{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 443}
	call := func(tool string, params any) []Target {
		return targetsOf("ExecuteExtraTool", map[string]any{"tool_name": tool, "params": params})
	}
	wantTargets(t, "mcp tool", call("mcp__browser__navigate", map[string]string{"url": "https://app.example.com/"}), app)
	wantTargets(t, "inner WebFetch", call("WebFetch", map[string]string{"url": "https://app.example.com/x"}), app)
	wantTargets(t, "inner Bash", call("Bash", map[string]string{"command": "nmap 203.0.113.7", "description": "https://app.example.com/"}),
		Target{TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 0})
	wantTargets(t, "inner tool without a target", call("list_assets", map[string]string{"q": "https://app.example.com/"}))
	wantTargets(t, "no params", targetsOf("ExecuteExtraTool", map[string]any{"tool_name": "mcp__scan__run"}))
	// A call that does not name its inner tool is read as a whole.
	wantTargets(t, "no tool name", targetsOf("ExecuteExtraTool", map[string]any{"params": map[string]string{"url": "https://app.example.com/"}}), app)
	// The wrapper is unwrapped once: a nested wrapper is read as an unknown tool.
	wantTargets(t, "nested", call("ExecuteExtraTool", map[string]any{"tool_name": "list_assets", "params": map[string]string{"q": "https://app.example.com/"}}), app)
}

func TestExtractSkipsNoTargetTools(t *testing.T) {
	input := map[string]any{
		"query": "site:app.example.com 203.0.113.7", "file_path": "/tmp/203.0.113.7.txt", "content": "curl https://app.example.com/",
		"url": "https://app.example.com/", "command": "nmap 203.0.113.7", "items": []any{map[string]any{"url": "https://app.example.com:8443/"}},
	}
	for _, tool := range []string{
		"web_search", "Read", "Write", "Edit", "MultiEdit", "LS", "Glob", "Grep", "TodoWrite", "sleep",
		"TaskOutput", "TaskStop", "TaskList",
		"add_intent", "insert_assets", "report_finding", "record_fact", "add_task_scope", "graph_overview",
		"spawn_task", "ask_operator", "traffic_search", "traffic_get", "traffic_blob",
	} {
		wantTargets(t, tool, targetsOf(tool, input))
	}
}

// A tool the gate does not know is scanned, not skipped: a tool added later is
// gated by default.
func TestExtractUnknownToolScansStringLeaves(t *testing.T) {
	input := map[string]any{
		"target":  "203.0.113.7",
		"options": map[string]any{"proxy": "http://127.0.0.1:8080", "ports": []any{"443", 8443}, "deep": true},
		"urls":    []any{"https://app.example.com/a", map[string]any{"u": "https://app.example.com/b"}, "ftp://files.example.com"},
		"note":    "x.py and README.md are files",
	}
	// In the order of the sorted keys: options, target, urls.
	want := []Target{
		{TargetIP, "127.0.0.1", 8080}, {TargetIP, "203.0.113.7", 0},
		{TargetDomain, "app.example.com", 443}, {TargetDomain, "files.example.com", 21},
	}
	for _, tool := range []string{"mcp__scan__run", "my_custom_http_tool", "SomeToolAddedLater", "create_mcp", "create_custom_tool"} {
		wantTargets(t, tool, targetsOf(tool, input), want...)
	}
	wantTargets(t, "input that is not JSON", ExtractTargets("mcp__scan__run", []byte("https://app.example.com/")))
}

// A bare name is not a target in a command: a file name is a valid host name,
// so reading bare names would ask on every script run.
func TestExtractDoesNotTreatFileNamesAsHosts(t *testing.T) {
	for _, cmd := range []string{
		"python3 x.py", "node server.js --watch", "cat notes.txt README.md", "bash ./run.sh && go test ./...",
		"tar czf out.tar.gz data.json", "ls app.example.com.har", "vim config.yaml", "./exploit.py --out result.io",
	} {
		wantTargets(t, cmd, targetsOf("Bash", command(cmd)))
	}
}

// The tests below document what the gate does NOT see. A subprocess path is
// advisory: the gate detects a declared target and cannot prevent an undeclared
// connection. Each asserts that no target is extracted, which is the gap. They
// change only if that decision changes.

func TestBypass_BareHostnameNotExtracted(t *testing.T) {
	for _, cmd := range []string{"nmap app.example.com", "ping -c1 app.example.com", "curl app.example.com/login", "ssh root@app.example.com", "nc db 5432"} {
		wantTargets(t, cmd, targetsOf("Bash", command(cmd)))
	}
}

func TestBypass_EncodedCommandHidesTarget(t *testing.T) {
	for _, cmd := range []string{

		`python3 -c "import urllib.request as u; u.urlopen('https:/'+'/app.example'+'.com/')"`,
		"H=app.example; curl $H.com",
		"curl http://$TARGET/login https://${HOST}:8443/",
		"curl 'http://{app.example.com}/'",
	} {
		wantTargets(t, cmd, targetsOf("Bash", command(cmd)))
	}
}

	}
}

=====================================================================
FILE: intercept/trace.go
=====================================================================
package intercept

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"crypto/rand"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/hex"
	"encoding/json"
	"sync"
	"time"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

const (
	contextLimit = 24
	entryLimit   = 8 * 1024
	promptLimit  = 32 * 1024
	outputLimit  = 64 * 1024
)

type traceKey struct{}
type callKey struct{}
type completion func(status, output string, truncated bool)

type tracedCall struct {
	key       string
	audit     db.InterceptAudit
	claimed   bool
	ambiguous bool
	complete  completion
}

// Trace belongs to ONE Prompt invocation. SDK v0.3.6 hooks omit the tool ID;
// correlate only when exactly one outstanding event has matching input. Never
// guess between simultaneous identical requests, even when results arrive FIFO.
type Trace struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	runID   string
	user    string
	userCut bool
	entries []db.InterceptContextEntry
	cut     bool
	calls   map[string]*tracedCall
}

func WithTrace(ctx context.Context, user string, prior []db.InterceptContextEntry) (context.Context, *Trace) {
	t := &Trace{runID: rand.Text(), calls: make(map[string]*tracedCall)}
	t.user, t.userCut = bounded(user, promptLimit)
	for _, e := range prior {
		t.append(e)
	}
	return context.WithValue(ctx, traceKey{}, t), t
}

func (t *Trace) append(e db.InterceptContextEntry) {
	var cut bool
	e.Text, cut = bounded(e.Text, entryLimit)
	e.Truncated = e.Truncated || cut
	t.cut = t.cut || e.Truncated
	t.entries = append(t.entries, e)
	if len(t.entries) > contextLimit {
		t.entries = append([]db.InterceptContextEntry(nil), t.entries[len(t.entries)-contextLimit:]...)
		t.cut = true
	}
}

func (t *Trace) Append(e db.InterceptContextEntry) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.append(e)
}

func (t *Trace) Start(id, tool string, input []byte) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	t.calls[id] = &tracedCall{key: tool + ":" + digestInput(input), audit: db.InterceptAudit{
		RunID: t.runID, ToolUseID: id, Correlation: "exact", InputDigest: digestInput(input),
		UserMessage: t.user, UserTruncated: t.userCut, CapturedAt: time.Now().UTC(),
		Context: append([]db.InterceptContextEntry{}, t.entries...), ContextTruncated: t.cut,
	}}
	t.append(db.InterceptContextEntry{Kind: "tool_use", Tool: tool, ToolUseID: id, Text: string(input)})
}

// WithCall claims the event before model review starts, so subsequent tools
// cannot change this approval's context while the judge is running.
func WithCall(ctx context.Context, tool string, input []byte) context.Context {
	t, _ := ctx.Value(traceKey{}).(*Trace)
	a := db.InterceptAudit{Correlation: "unavailable", InputDigest: digestInput(input), CapturedAt: time.Now().UTC()}
	if t != nil {
		t.mu.Lock()
		var candidates []*tracedCall
		for _, c := range t.calls {
			if !c.claimed && c.key == tool+":"+a.InputDigest {
				candidates = append(candidates, c)
			}
		}
		if len(candidates) == 1 && !candidates[0].ambiguous {
			candidates[0].claimed = true
			a = candidates[0].audit
		} else {
			a.RunID, a.UserMessage, a.UserTruncated = t.runID, t.user, t.userCut
			if len(candidates) > 0 {
				a.Correlation = "ambiguous"
				for _, c := range candidates {
					c.ambiguous = true
				}
			}
		}
		t.mu.Unlock()
	}
	return context.WithValue(ctx, callKey{}, a)
}

func (t *Trace) bind(id string, f completion) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	defer t.mu.Unlock()
	if c := t.calls[id]; c != nil {
		c.complete = f
	}
}

func (t *Trace) Complete(id, output string, isError bool) {
	t.mu.Lock()
	c := t.calls[id]
	delete(t.calls, id)
	t.mu.Unlock()
	if c == nil || c.complete == nil {
		return
	}
	status := "succeeded"
	if isError {
		status = "failed"
	}
	out, cut := bounded(output, outputLimit)
	c.complete(status, out, cut)
}

// Finish marks missing results unknown, never successful. The tool may have
// been interrupted or its final event lost; this is distinct from a tool error.
func (t *Trace) Finish() {
	t.mu.Lock()
	calls := t.calls
	t.calls = make(map[string]*tracedCall)
	t.mu.Unlock()
	for _, c := range calls {
		if c.complete != nil {
			c.complete("unknown", "execution ended but no tool result was received", false)
		}
	}
}

func auditFor(ctx context.Context, dec Decision, input []byte, status string) *db.InterceptAudit {
	a, ok := ctx.Value(callKey{}).(db.InterceptAudit)
	if !ok {
		a = db.InterceptAudit{Correlation: "unavailable", InputDigest: digestInput(input), CapturedAt: time.Now().UTC()}
	}
	a.InitialAction, a.InitialReason = dec.Action, dec.Message
	a.ModelFallback = dec.ModelFallback
	a.ModelInput, a.ModelInputDigest = dec.ModelInput, dec.ModelInputDigest
	a.RuleName, a.ConfigDigest, a.ProfileID = dec.RuleName, dec.ConfigDigest, dec.ProfileID
	a.JudgeAnswers = dec.JudgeAnswers
	a.ExecutionStatus = "not_started"
	if status == "allowed" {
		a.EffectiveAction, a.ExecutionStatus = "allow", "awaiting_result"
		if a.Correlation != "exact" {
			a.ExecutionStatus = "unknown"
		}
		// Keep the exact model input for EVERY model verdict, including automatic
		// allows. Raw audit history is not model input. Preserve the existing
		// lightweight allow-retention policy; render the saved input directly.
		a.UserMessage, a.UserTruncated = "", false
		a.Context, a.ContextTruncated = nil, false
	}
	if status == "denied" {
		a.EffectiveAction, a.ExecutionStatus = "deny", "not_executed"
	}
	return &a
}

func (i *Interceptor) bindResult(ctx context.Context, id int64, audit *db.InterceptAudit) {
	t, _ := ctx.Value(traceKey{}).(*Trace)
	if t == nil || audit.Correlation != "exact" || audit.ToolUseID == "" {
		return
	}
	t.bind(audit.ToolUseID, func(status, output string, cut bool) {
		_ = i.db.CompleteIntercept(id, audit.RunID, audit.ToolUseID, status, output, cut)
	})
}

func digestInput(input []byte) string {
	var value any
	d := json.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(input))
	d.UseNumber()
	if d.Decode(&value) == nil {
		if canonical, err := json.Marshal(value); err == nil {
			input = canonical
		}
	}
	h := sha256.Sum256(input)
	return hex.EncodeToString(h[:])
}

func bounded(s string, limit int) (string, bool) {
	if len(s) <= limit {
		return s, false
	}
	end := limit
	for end > 0 && !utf8.RuneStart(s[end]) {
		end--
	}
	return s[:end], true
}

FILE: intercept/trace_test.go

package intercept

import (
	"context"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
	"unicode/utf8"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

func TestTraceExactCorrelationAndSnapshot(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, trace := WithTrace(context.Background(), "save report", []db.InterceptContextEntry{{Kind: "user", Text: "prior message"}})
	trace.Start("call-a", "Write", []byte(`{"path":"a","n":12345678901234567890}`))
	trace.Append(db.InterceptContextEntry{Kind: "text", Text: "later context"})
	callCtx := WithCall(ctx, "Write", []byte(`{ "n":12345678901234567890, "path":"a" }`))
	// "pending" (the ask path) keeps the full snapshot; see TestAuditAllowDropsSnapshot
	// for why a routine allow does not.
	a := auditFor(callCtx, Decision{Action: "ask"}, nil, "pending")
	if a.Correlation != "exact" || a.ToolUseID != "call-a" || len(a.Context) != 1 || a.Context[0].Text != "prior message" {
		t.Fatalf("wrong snapshot: %+v", a)
	}
	var got string
	trace.bind("call-a", func(status, output string, cut bool) { got = status + ":" + output })
	trace.Complete("different-call", "wrong", false)
	if got != "" {
		t.Fatal("unrelated result attached")
	}
	trace.Complete("call-a", "written", false)
	trace.Finish()
	if got != "succeeded:written" {
		t.Fatalf("result %q", got)
	}
}

// A rule allow is logged for auditability but must not carry the replay
// snapshot: with the fallback judge on those rows are emitted per tool call, and
// keeping 24×8KiB of context plus a 32KiB prompt each would put hundreds of MB
// into intercept_pending (and from there into the task archive). Decision
// metadata and correlation must survive so the execution result still binds.
func TestAuditAllowDropsSnapshot(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, trace := WithTrace(context.Background(), "a long user prompt", []db.InterceptContextEntry{{Kind: "user", Text: "prior message"}})
	input := []byte(`{"path":"a"}`)
	trace.Start("call-a", "Write", input)
	a := auditFor(WithCall(ctx, "Write", input), Decision{Action: "allow", RuleName: "auto"}, input, "allowed")
	if a.UserMessage != "" || a.UserTruncated || a.Context != nil || a.ContextTruncated {
		t.Fatalf("allow kept the replay snapshot: %+v", a)
	}
	if a.Correlation != "exact" || a.ToolUseID != "call-a" || a.EffectiveAction != "allow" ||
		a.ExecutionStatus != "awaiting_result" || a.RuleName != "auto" || a.InputDigest == "" {
		t.Fatalf("allow lost decision metadata: %+v", a)
	}

	// A denial is rare and worth the full context, so it keeps its snapshot.
	denied := []byte(`{"path":"b"}`)
	trace.Start("call-b", "Write", denied)
	d := auditFor(WithCall(ctx, "Write", denied), Decision{Action: "deny"}, denied, "denied")
	if len(d.Context) == 0 || d.Context[0].Text != "prior message" || d.UserMessage == "" {
		t.Fatalf("deny lost the snapshot: %+v", d)
	}
}

func TestTraceIdenticalParallelCallsAreNeverGuessed(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, trace := WithTrace(context.Background(), "test", nil)
	input := []byte(`{"command":"pwd"}`)
	trace.Start("first", "Bash", input)
	trace.Start("second", "Bash", input)
	for range 2 {
		a := auditFor(WithCall(ctx, "Bash", input), Decision{}, input, "pending")
		if a.Correlation != "ambiguous" || a.ToolUseID != "" {
			t.Fatalf("guessed identity: %+v", a)
		}
	}
	trace.Complete("first", "first-result", false)
	a := auditFor(WithCall(ctx, "Bash", input), Decision{}, input, "pending")
	if a.Correlation != "ambiguous" {
		t.Fatal("ambiguity must survive the other call completing")
	}
}

func TestTraceSequentialIdenticalCallsAndRunIsolation(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, trace := WithTrace(context.Background(), "test", nil)
	input := []byte(`{}`)
	trace.Start("a", "Read", input)
	a := auditFor(WithCall(ctx, "Read", input), Decision{}, input, "pending")
	trace.Start("b", "Read", input)
	b := auditFor(WithCall(ctx, "Read", input), Decision{}, input, "pending")
	other, next := WithTrace(context.Background(), "next run", nil)
	next.Start("a", "Read", input)
	c := auditFor(WithCall(other, "Read", input), Decision{}, input, "pending")
	if a.ToolUseID != "a" || b.ToolUseID != "b" || a.RunID == c.RunID {
		t.Fatal("run or call identities overlap")
	}
}

func TestTraceBoundsAndMissingResult(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, trace := WithTrace(context.Background(), strings.Repeat("ab", promptLimit), nil)
	for range contextLimit + 5 {
		trace.Append(db.InterceptContextEntry{Kind: "text", Text: strings.Repeat("xy", entryLimit)})
	}
	trace.Start("a", "Read", []byte(`{}`))
	a := auditFor(WithCall(ctx, "Read", []byte(`{}`)), Decision{}, nil, "pending")
	if !a.UserTruncated || !a.ContextTruncated || len(a.Context) != contextLimit || !utf8.ValidString(a.UserMessage) {
		t.Fatal("unbounded/invalid snapshot")
	}
	for _, e := range a.Context {
		if len(e.Text) > entryLimit || !utf8.ValidString(e.Text) {
			t.Fatal("invalid entry bound")
		}
	}
	got := ""
	trace.bind("a", func(status, _ string, _ bool) { got = status })
	trace.Finish()
	if got != "unknown" {
		t.Fatalf("missing result presented as %q", got)
	}
}

func TestTraceConcurrentDistinctCalls(t *testing.T) {
	ctx, trace := WithTrace(context.Background(), "test", nil)
	var wg sync.WaitGroup
	for _, id := range []string{"a", "b", "c", "d"} {
		wg.Go(func() {
			input := []byte(`{"path":"` + id + `"}`)
			trace.Start(id, "Read", input)
			a := auditFor(WithCall(ctx, "Read", input), Decision{}, input, "allowed")
			if a.ToolUseID != id {
				t.Errorf("got %s for %s", a.ToolUseID, id)
			}
			trace.Complete(id, "ok", false)
		})
	}
	wg.Wait()
}

=====================================================================
FILE: llmpool/catalog.go
