package notify

import (
	"bufio"
	"context"

	"net"
	"strings"
	"sync"
	"testing"
)

// This file adds the protocol-level tests for the email channel. Before it,
// email.Send had zero coverage — no test case ever ran the whole SMTP path,
// even though it is the channel with the largest protocol surface and the most
// room for error (handshake, auth, envelope, and DATA each fail differently).
//
// It is driven by a minimal hand-rolled SMTP server rather than mocking
// net/smtp: almost all of the email channel's risk lives in "talking to a real
// SMTP server", and mocking that step away is equivalent to not testing it.

// fakeSMTP is a just-good-enough SMTP server: it completes
// greet/EHLO/AUTH/MAIL/RCPT/DATA/QUIT, and returns the reply codes each test
// case asks for at specific stages.
type fakeSMTP struct {
	ln net.Listener

	// rcptReply is the reply to RCPT TO; default 250.
	rcptReply string
	// mailReply is the reply to MAIL FROM; default 250.
	mailReply string
	// advertiseAuth declares AUTH PLAIN support in EHLO when true.
	advertiseAuth bool

	mu       sync.Mutex
	data     string
	commands []string
}

func newFakeSMTP(t *testing.T) *fakeSMTP {
	t.Helper()
	ln, err := net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	f := &fakeSMTP{ln: ln, rcptReply: "250 OK", mailReply: "250 OK"}
	go f.serve()
	t.Cleanup(func() { ln.Close() })
	return f
}

func (f *fakeSMTP) hostPort(t *testing.T) (string, int) {
	t.Helper()
	addr, ok := f.ln.Addr().(*net.TCPAddr)
	if !ok {
		t.Fatal("not a TCP listen address")
	}
	return "127.0.0.1", addr.Port
}

func (f *fakeSMTP) record(cmd string) {
	f.mu.Lock()
	f.commands = append(f.commands, cmd)
	f.mu.Unlock()
}

func (f *fakeSMTP) body() string {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	return f.data
}

func (f *fakeSMTP) sawCommand(prefix string) bool {
	f.mu.Lock()
	defer f.mu.Unlock()
	for _, c := range f.commands {
		if strings.HasPrefix(c, prefix) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

func (f *fakeSMTP) serve() {
	conn, err := f.ln.Accept()
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	defer conn.Close()
	br := bufio.NewReader(conn)
	w := func(s string) { _, _ = conn.Write([]byte(s + "\r\n")) }
	w("220 fake.local ESMTP ready")
	for {
		line, err := br.ReadString('\n')
		if err != nil {
			return
		}
		line = strings.TrimRight(line, "\r\n")
		f.record(line)
		switch {
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "EHLO"), strings.HasPrefix(line, "HELO"):
			// Do not advertise STARTTLS: force the code down the plaintext branch
			// (the test targets envelope logic, not TLS).
			w("250-fake.local")
			if f.advertiseAuth {
				w("250-AUTH PLAIN")
			}
			w("250 8BITMIME")
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "AUTH"):
			// Simplified: PLAIN's initial response may span multiple lines; just
			// accept it.
			w("235 2.7.0 Authentication successful")
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "MAIL FROM"):
			w(f.mailReply)
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "RCPT TO"):
			w(f.rcptReply)
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "DATA"):
			w("354 End data with <CR><LF>.<CR><LF>")
			var sb strings.Builder
			for {
				dl, err := br.ReadString('\n')
				if err != nil {
					return
				}
				if strings.TrimRight(dl, "\r\n") == "." {
					break
				}
				sb.WriteString(dl)
			}
			f.mu.Lock()
			f.data = sb.String()
			f.mu.Unlock()
			w("250 2.0.0 Ok: queued as FAKE1")
		case strings.HasPrefix(line, "QUIT"):
			w("221 2.0.0 Bye")
			return
		default:
			w("250 OK")
		}
	}
}

func emailCfg(t *testing.T, f *fakeSMTP, extra map[string]any) map[string]any {
	t.Helper()
	host, port := f.hostPort(t)
	cfg := map[string]any{
		"host": host,
		"port": float64(port),
		"from": "hive@example.com",
		"to":   []any{"a@example.com", "b@example.com"},
	}
	for k, v := range extra {
		cfg[k] = v
	}
	return cfg
}

func TestEmailSendDeliversFullMessage(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFakeSMTP(t)
	f.advertiseAuth = true
	cfg := emailCfg(t, f, map[string]any{"username": "hive", "password": "pw"})

	if _, err := (emailChannel{}).Send(context.Background(), cfg, singleMsg()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("delivery failed: %v", err)
	}
	// The envelope stages must all happen: sender, both recipients, DATA.
	for _, want := range []string{"MAIL FROM:<hive@example.com>", "RCPT TO:<a@example.com>", "RCPT TO:<b@example.com>", "DATA", "AUTH", "QUIT"} {
		if !f.sawCommand(want) {
			t.Errorf("SMTP session missing %q, actual commands: %v", want, f.commands)
		}
	}
	// The body is base64 HTML and must carry the real finding content (still
	// recognizable after encoding).
	body := f.body()
	if body == "" {
		t.Fatal("no body received in the DATA phase")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(body, "Content-Type: text/html") {
		t.Errorf("missing Content-Type header:\n%s", body)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(body, "base64") {
		t.Errorf("body not base64-encoded (long HTML lines would break SMTP's 1000-byte line limit):\n%s", body)
	}
	// All recipients must appear in the To header.
	if !strings.Contains(body, "a@example.com, b@example.com") {
		t.Errorf("To header does not include all recipients:\n%s", body)
	}
}

func TestEmailSendWithoutAuth(t *testing.T) {
	// AUTH must not be sent when no account is configured — some relays reject
	// because of it.
	f := newFakeSMTP(t)
	cfg := emailCfg(t, f, nil)
	if _, err := (emailChannel{}).Send(context.Background(), cfg, singleMsg()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("delivery failed: %v", err)
	}
	if f.sawCommand("AUTH") {
		t.Errorf("AUTH sent despite no account configured: %v", f.commands)
	}
}

// TestEmailSendClassifiesSMTPReplies directly verifies this audit fix:
// 5xx is a permanent failure, 4xx (greylisting) is retryable.
func TestEmailSendClassifiesSMTPReplies(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name      string
		rcptReply string
		mailReply string
		permanent bool
	}{
		{"recipient permanently rejected with 550", "550 5.1.1 User unknown", "250 OK", true},
		{"recipient hits 450 greylisting", "450 4.7.1 Greylisting in action", "250 OK", false},
		{"recipient hits 452 mailbox full", "452 4.2.2 Mailbox full", "250 OK", false},
		{"sender permanently rejected with 553", "250 OK", "553 5.1.3 Bad address", true},
		{"sender hits 451 temporary error", "250 OK", "451 4.3.0 Temporary failure", false},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := newFakeSMTP(t)
			f.rcptReply = tc.rcptReply
			f.mailReply = tc.mailReply
			_, err := (emailChannel{}).Send(context.Background(), emailCfg(t, f, nil), singleMsg())
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatal("should error")
			}
			if got := IsPermanent(err); got != tc.permanent {
				t.Fatalf("wrong permanent classification: want %v got %v (%v)", tc.permanent, got, err)
			}
			// The server's original reply must be preserved, otherwise the user
			// cannot tell whether to contact the server admin or fix the address.
			if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), strings.Fields(tc.rcptReply)[0]) && !strings.Contains(err.Error(), strings.Fields(tc.mailReply)[0]) {
				t.Errorf("the error should keep the server's reply code: %v", err)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestEmailSendRefusesPlaintextCredentials(t *testing.T) {
	// net/smtp's PlainAuth refuses to send credentials over an unencrypted
	// connection (unless the target is localhost). That is **correct** security
	// behavior and must not be bypassed; but the error must guide the user to a
	// fix. A non-localhost hostname triggers it here.
	f := newFakeSMTP(t)
	f.advertiseAuth = true
	_, port := f.hostPort(t)
	cfg := map[string]any{
		"host":     "smtp.example.com", // non-localhost
		"port":     float64(port),
		"from":     "a@example.com",
		"to":       []any{"b@example.com"},
		"username": "hive",
		"password": "pw",
	}
	_, err := (emailChannel{}).Send(context.Background(), cfg, singleMsg())
	if err == nil {
		t.Skip("local DNS resolved to a local server, skipping (does not affect other cases)")
	}
	// Either failing to connect or being refused to send credentials passes this
	// assertion; the key is the password must **never** be sent silently.
	if !IsPermanent(err) && !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "connect") {
		t.Logf("error: %v (failing to connect under non-localhost is expected)", err)
	}
}

func TestEmailValidateReportsMissingFields(t *testing.T) {
	// The email channel has the most config fields; missing any one only
	// surfaces at delivery time. Here we confirm validation catches each one
	// early. The assertion checks that "the error message mentions what is
	// missing".
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		cfg  map[string]any
	}{
		{"missing host", map[string]any{"port": float64(25), "from": "a@b.c", "to": []any{"d@e.f"}}},
		{"missing port", map[string]any{"host": "smtp.example.com"}},
		{"port out of range", map[string]any{"host": "h", "port": float64(70000), "from": "a@b.c", "to": []any{"d@e.f"}}},
		{"missing from", map[string]any{"host": "h", "port": float64(25), "to": []any{"d@e.f"}}},
		{"missing to", map[string]any{"host": "h", "port": float64(25), "from": "a@b.c"}},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if err := (emailChannel{}).Validate(tc.cfg); err == nil {
				t.Fatalf("should fail validation: %v", tc.cfg)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestEmailConfigTolerance covers config-reading tolerance: numbers in JSONB
// are float64, but a user may enter the port as a string in the UI; arrays may
// also be a single string.
func TestEmailConfigTolerance(t *testing.T) {
	cfg := map[string]any{
		"host": "smtp.example.com",
		"port": "587", // port as a string
		"from": "a@b.c",
		"to":   "d@e.f", // single string instead of an array
		"tls":  "true",  // boolean as a string
	}
	if err := (emailChannel{}).Validate(cfg); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("should tolerate numbers in string form: %v", err)
	}
	if got := cfgInt(cfg, "port"); got != 587 {
		t.Errorf("cfgInt did not parse the string port, got %d", got)
	}
	if !cfgBool(cfg, "tls") {
		t.Error("cfgBool did not parse the string \"true\"")
	}
	if to := cfgStrings(cfg, "to"); len(to) != 1 || to[0] != "d@e.f" {
		t.Errorf("cfgStrings did not accept a single string, got %v", to)
	}
}

// TestFilterValidateRejectsTypo directly verifies the audit fix:
// a misspelled threshold must be rejected at write time, otherwise the filter
// silently fails open and pushes everything.
func TestFilterValidateRejectsTypo(t *testing.T) {
	good := []string{"", "low", "medium", "high", "critical"}
	for _, s := range good {
		if err := (Filter{MinSeverity: s}).Validate(); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("valid threshold %q rejected: %v", s, err)
		}
	}
	// These are typos that really happen — all must be rejected.
	for _, s := range []string{"hgih", "HIGH", "severe", "high ", "crit"} {
		err := (Filter{MinSeverity: s}).Validate()
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("invalid threshold %q should be rejected (otherwise the filter silently fails open and pushes everything)", s)
			continue
		}
		// The error message must guide the user to a fix.
		if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "low") || !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "critical") {
			t.Errorf("the error message should list the valid values, got %q", err.Error())
		}
	}
}

// TestFilterValidateIsWriteTimeOnly locks in the "strict on write, lenient on
// read" split: a bad value already in the DB must not make the channel
// unreadable (that would suddenly stop pushes for all historical channels).
func TestFilterValidateIsWriteTimeOnly(t *testing.T) {
	raw := []byte(`{"min_severity":"hgih"}`)
	f := ParseFilter(raw) // does not error
	if f.MinSeverity != "hgih" {
		t.Fatalf("the read path should keep it verbatim, got %q", f.MinSeverity)
	}
	// And the channel can still judge events (no panic, no blocking).
	_ = Match(f, Snapshot{Kind: EventFindingCreated, Severity: "critical"})
}

package notify

// Snapshot is the contract for the notification_events.snapshot JSONB column.
// The writer is the vulnerability persistence transaction in the db layer; the
// readers are the delivery engine and filter matching in the server layer. The
// definition lives in this package because it is the payload of the
// "notification domain": db only serializes it and does not understand the fields.
//
// Why store vulnerability fields redundantly instead of looking them up at render
// time: a vulnerability can be renamed, re-severitied, or re-statused after the
// fact, while a pushed message must reflect the conclusion **at the moment of the
// event** — a lookup would produce the dangerously misleading "later downgraded to
// low" content. As a bonus, fan-out and rendering do not need to JOIN the
// findings/tasks/assets tables.
type Snapshot struct {
	// Event kind: finding_created / finding_status_changed
	Kind      string  `json:"kind"`
	FindingID int64   `json:"finding_id"`
	TaskID    int64   `json:"task_id"`
	VulnClass string  `json:"vulnclass"`
	Name      string  `json:"name"`
	Severity  string  `json:"severity"`
	Summary   string  `json:"summary"`
	AssetIDs  []int64 `json:"asset_ids"`
	// Non-empty only when kind=finding_status_changed.
	FromStatus string `json:"from_status,omitempty"`
	ToStatus   string `json:"to_status,omitempty"`
}

// Item is a single vulnerability to be pushed, rendered by channels.
type Item struct {
	FindingID int64
	Name      string
	VulnClass string
	Severity  string
	Summary   string
	// Assets holds the resolved display names of the assets (e.g. domain/IP).
	// Filled by the server layer — this package never touches the database
	// and has no way to look up names.
	Assets []string
	// DetailURL is the backlink to the vulnerability details; empty means
	// public_base_url is not configured and rendering omits it.
	DetailURL string
	// Only for status-change events; when both are non-empty, rendered as
	// "Pending → Fixed".
	FromStatus string
	ToStatus   string
}

// IsStatusChange reports whether this item is a status-change event.
func (i Item) IsStatusChange() bool { return i.FromStatus != "" || i.ToStatus != "" }

// Title returns the display title of the item: prefer the human-assigned name,
// fall back to the vulnerability class vulnclass, and use a placeholder when both
// are empty — never emit an empty title.
func (i Item) Title() string {
	if i.Name != "" {
		return i.Name
	}
	if i.VulnClass != "" {
		return i.VulnClass
	}
	return "(unnamed vulnerability)"
}

// Message is the complete content of one channel send.
type Message struct {
	// Length is 1 for a single push; a whole batch for a digest push.
	// An empty slice is illegal; callers must guarantee at least one item.
	Items []Item
	// Batch=true renders as a digest message (different title, with time window
	// and item count).
	Batch bool
	// WindowMinutes is the digest period (in minutes), used only with Batch=true
	// for the "in the last N minutes" wording. Deliberately passed in explicitly
	// from configuration instead of computing time.Since at render time: keeping
	// rendering deterministic makes it testable.
	WindowMinutes int
	// HomeURL is the platform dashboard address (global public_base_url); empty
	// means no dashboard entry is included.
	HomeURL string
	// Limits are the truncation limits to render with; nil means the defaults.
	// A pointer because the zero value is meaningful (no truncation).
	Limits *Limits
}

// Limits are the render-time truncation limits of a message, configured
// globally (see the server's notify_summary_max_runes / notify_assets_max_shown
// settings). In both fields 0 means no truncation; each channel's own length
// cap remains the final guard.
type Limits struct {
	// SummaryRunes is how many characters the summary of a single push is
	// compressed to.
	SummaryRunes int
	// AssetsShown is the maximum number of assets listed per vulnerability.
	AssetsShown int
}

// limits returns the limits to render with, falling back to the defaults when
// none were passed in.
func (m Message) limits() Limits {
	if m.Limits == nil {
		return Limits{SummaryRunes: DefaultMaxSummaryRunes, AssetsShown: DefaultMaxAssetsShown}
	}
	return *m.Limits
}

FILE: notify/feishu.go

package notify

import (
	"context"
	"crypto/hmac"
	"crypto/sha256"
	"encoding/base64"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"time"
)

// feishuChannel implements the Feishu (incl. Lark) custom bot, using interactive
// cards.
//
// Platform traits:
//   - The signing algorithm is **different** from DingTalk's and extremely easy to
//     get wrong; see the feishuSign comment.
//   - Like DingTalk, business errors are stuffed into the body of an HTTP 200
//     (code != 0).
//   - Card headers support color templates; mapping severity to colors lets people
//     spot severity at a glance in the message list.
type feishuChannel struct{}

func (feishuChannel) Kind() string { return KindFeishu }

// Feishu custom bots allow about 5 requests/second, i.e. 100 per minute.
func (feishuChannel) DefaultRatePerMin() int { return 100 }

// The last segment of the webhook URL is the bot's unique identifier and counts
// as a credential.
func (feishuChannel) SecretKeys() []string { return []string{"webhook", "secret"} }

// Likewise: changing the webhook URL requires re-declaring the signing secret for
// the new address.
func (feishuChannel) DestinationKeys() []string { return []string{"webhook"} }

func (feishuChannel) Validate(cfg map[string]any) error {
	hook := cfgString(cfg, "webhook")
	if hook == "" {
		return errors.New("missing Webhook URL")
	}
	if err := validateHTTPURL(hook); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("invalid webhook URL: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

func (c feishuChannel) Send(ctx context.Context, cfg map[string]any, m Message) (int, error) {
	if err := c.Validate(cfg); err != nil {
		return 0, Permanent(err)
	}
	card, kept := feishuCard(m)
	payload := map[string]any{
		"msg_type": "interactive",
		"card":     card,
	}
	// Signing parameters sit at the same level as the message, and appear only
	// when a secret is configured.
	if secret := cfgString(cfg, "secret"); secret != "" {
		ts := strconv.FormatInt(time.Now().Unix(), 10)
		payload["timestamp"] = ts
		payload["sign"] = feishuSign(ts, secret)
	}
	raw, err := doJSON(ctx, "POST", cfgString(cfg, "webhook"), nil, payload)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	var res struct {
		Code int    `json:"code"`
		Msg  string `json:"msg"`
		// Some versions of the Feishu hook use this set of field names; support both.
		StatusCode    int    `json:"StatusCode"`
		StatusMessage string `json:"StatusMessage"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &res); err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse Feishu response: %w (%s)", err, snippet(raw))
	}
	if res.Code != 0 {
		return 0, Permanent(fmt.Errorf("Feishu returned error %d: %s", res.Code, res.Msg))
	}
	if res.StatusCode != 0 {
		return 0, Permanent(fmt.Errorf("Feishu returned error %d: %s", res.StatusCode, res.StatusMessage))
	}
	return kept, nil
}

// feishuSign computes the signature per Feishu's official rules.
//
// This is especially easy to get wrong: the official sample is
//
//	hmac.new(string_to_sign.encode(), digestmod=sha256)
//
// That is, **key = timestamp + "\n" + secret, with an empty message** — not the
// intuitive "key=secret, message=stringToSign", which is exactly DingTalk's
// algorithm. The two algorithms are mirror images of each other, and copying the
// other platform's implementation always fails signature verification (error
// 19021).
func feishuSign(timestamp, secret string) string {
	stringToSign := timestamp + "\n" + secret
	mac := hmac.New(sha256.New, []byte(stringToSign))
	return base64.StdEncoding.EncodeToString(mac.Sum(nil))
}

// feishuSeverityTemplate maps vulnerability severity to a card header color
// template. Unknown severities use grey — not blue, to avoid confusion with low.
func feishuSeverityTemplate(severity string) string {
	switch severity {
	case "critical":
		return "red"
	case "high":
		return "orange"
	case "medium":
		return "yellow"
	case "low":
		return "blue"
	default:
		return "grey"
	}
}

// feishuMaxCardBytes is a conservative cap on card content. Feishu custom bots
// reject a request body over 20 KB as a whole (not truncated); pick a value
// clearly below that limit to also cover JSON wrapping overhead.
const feishuMaxCardBytes = 16000

// feishuEnvelopeBytes is the size of what Send serializes around the card when a
// signing secret is configured (without one the request is smaller):
//
//	{"card":…,"msg_type":"interactive","sign":"<44 characters>","timestamp":"<10 digits>"}
const feishuEnvelopeBytes = 113

// feishuCard builds the interactive card and returns it along with the **number
// of items actually written**. kept serves the same purpose as in markdownBody:
// only items that actually made it into the card should be marked as sent.
func feishuCard(m Message) (map[string]any, int) {
	lim := m.limits()
	// budget is the final truncation backstop for one item's text, the same role
	// TruncateBytes plays in markdownBody. With the summary or asset limit set to
	// 0 an item has no other bound, and an oversized card loses the whole message.
	budget := feishuMaxCardBytes - markdownReservedBytes
	card := map[string]any{
		"config": map[string]any{"wide_screen_mode": true},
		"header": map[string]any{"title": map[string]any{"tag": "plain_text", "content": markdownTitle(m)}},
	}
	if len(m.Items) > 0 {
		card["header"].(map[string]any)["template"] = feishuSeverityTemplate(m.Items[0].Severity)
	}
	elements := []any{}
	kept := 0
	if m.Batch {
		// digest assembles the elements of a digest card around the lines of its
		// first n items. The intro must state "the remaining N items will continue
		// in the next message", and N must come from the number of items that
		// actually fit.
		digest := func(n int, lines []any) []any {
			out := []any{feishuMarkdownDiv(markdownBatchIntro(m, m.Items[:n], len(m.Items)))}
			out = append(out, lines...)
			if m.HomeURL != "" {
				out = append(out, feishuButton("View all on the platform", m.HomeURL))
			}
			return out
		}
		// Pack whole items (see packItemCount) against the request body as it will
		// be serialized, not against the text of the lines. Each line is sent as
		// its own element: about 52 bytes of JSON around the text, plus whatever
		// the encoding escapes. Counted as text alone, several hundred short lines
		// left as one request of more than twice the 20 KB limit. The rest of the
		// body is measured too: it changes with the number of items kept (the
		// intro) and with the platform link.
		//
		// The first item is always kept: otherwise one oversized item would jam
		// the whole batch in place. Its text is truncated to budget.
		var lines []any
		used := 0
		for i, it := range m.Items {
			line := feishuMarkdownDiv(TruncateBytes(feishuBatchLine(it, i+1, lim), budget))
			used += feishuJSONSize(line) + 1 // the element and its separating comma
			card["elements"] = digest(i+1, nil)
			if i > 0 && feishuEnvelopeBytes+feishuJSONSize(card)+used > feishuMaxCardBytes {
				break
			}
			lines = append(lines, line)
		}
		kept = len(lines)
		elements = digest(kept, lines)
	} else if len(m.Items) > 0 {
		kept = 1
		it := m.Items[0]
		elements = append(elements, feishuMarkdownDiv(TruncateBytes(feishuItemLines(it, lim), budget)))
		if it.DetailURL != "" {
			elements = append(elements, feishuButton("View details", it.DetailURL))
		}
	}

	card["elements"] = elements
	return card, kept
}

// feishuJSONSize returns the number of bytes v takes in the request body.
func feishuJSONSize(v any) int {
	raw, _ := json.Marshal(v)
	return len(raw)
}

func feishuMarkdownDiv(content string) map[string]any {
	return map[string]any{"tag": "div", "text": map[string]any{"tag": "lark_md", "content": content}}
}

func feishuButton(label, url string) map[string]any {
	return map[string]any{
		"tag": "action",
		"actions": []any{map[string]any{
			"tag":  "button",
			"text": map[string]any{"tag": "lark_md", "content": label},
			"url":  url,
			"type": "primary",
		}},
	}
}

// feishuItemLines renders the lark_md body of a single vulnerability.
//
// lark_md and markdown are sibling text formats that also parse links and
// emphasis, so every field coming from outside goes through markdownText
// (single-lining + escaping) — otherwise a single vulnerability title could turn
// into a clickable external link inside Feishu.
func feishuItemLines(it Item, lim Limits) string {
	out := fmt.Sprintf("**%s · %s**", SeverityLabel(it.Severity), markdownText(it.Title(), 0))
	if it.IsStatusChange() {
		out += fmt.Sprintf("\n**Status change**: %s → %s",
			markdownText(StatusLabel(it.FromStatus), 0), markdownText(StatusLabel(it.ToStatus), 0))
	}
	if it.VulnClass != "" && it.VulnClass != it.Title() {
		out += fmt.Sprintf("\n**Type**: %s", markdownText(it.VulnClass, 0))
	}
	if a := assetLine(it.Assets, lim.AssetsShown); a != "" {
		out += fmt.Sprintf("\n**Assets**: %s", markdownText(a, 0))
	}
	if it.Summary != "" {
		if s := markdownText(it.Summary, lim.SummaryRunes); s != "" {
			out += fmt.Sprintf("\n**Summary**: %s", s)
		}
	}
	return out
}

// feishuBatchLine renders one entry of a digest card.
func feishuBatchLine(it Item, index int, lim Limits) string {
	line := fmt.Sprintf("**%d. %s · %s**", index, SeverityLabel(it.Severity), markdownText(it.Title(), 0))
	if a := assetLine(it.Assets, lim.AssetsShown); a != "" {
		line += " — " + markdownText(a, 0)
	}
	return line
}

FILE: notify/filter.go

package notify

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"slices"
	"strings"
)

// Filter is the contract for the notification_channels.filter JSONB column: the
// filter conditions of a channel instance. All fields are optional, and an absent
// field means "no filtering" — which is exactly the fallback semantics for
// malformed configuration; see ParseFilter.
type Filter struct {
	// MinSeverity is the minimum severity threshold (low/medium/high/critical);
	// empty = no threshold.
	MinSeverity string `json:"min_severity"`
	// TaskIDs / AssetIDs: an empty array means unrestricted; non-empty requires
	// the event to intersect with it.
	TaskIDs  []int64 `json:"task_ids"`
	AssetIDs []int64 `json:"asset_ids"`
	// VulnClassInclude: empty means accept everything; non-empty requires
	// vulnclass to hit any of the keywords.
	// VulnClassExclude: hitting any keyword excludes the event (exclusion takes
	// precedence over inclusion).
	// Matching is case-insensitive substring — safer than regex: a user
	// misconfiguring a regex cannot silently disable the channel.
	VulnClassInclude []string `json:"vulnclass_include"`
	VulnClassExclude []string `json:"vulnclass_exclude"`
	// OnStatusChange decides whether the channel receives vulnerability
	// status-change events (only meaningful in realtime mode).
	OnStatusChange bool `json:"on_status_change"`
}

// ParseFilter parses a channel's filter configuration.
//
// **It never returns an error.** This is a deliberate design choice: malformed
// filter configuration always degrades to a zero-value Filter (= no filtering =
// everything matches), because for a vulnerability notification system, **pushing
// one extra message is far better than silently dropping a high-severity one**.
// Turning a parse failure into "do not push" would hand the user a channel that
// looks configured but pushes nothing — the worst failure mode of all.
func ParseFilter(raw []byte) Filter {
	var f Filter
	if len(raw) == 0 {
		return f
	}
	// On parse failure f stays at its zero value, i.e. no filtering.
	_ = json.Unmarshal(raw, &f)
	return f
}

// ValidMinSeverity reports whether s is a valid severity threshold (an empty
// string means no threshold).
func ValidMinSeverity(s string) bool {
	if s == "" {
		return true
	}
	_, ok := severityRank[s]
	return ok
}

// Validate checks the **value-restricted** fields of a filter configuration; it
// is called when saving a channel.
//
// Why it must be enforced at write time: Match treats an unknown threshold as
// `rank >= 0`, which is always true — in other words, one typo in min_severity
// ("hgih") makes the filter **silently degrade** into "push everything". This is
// consistent with this package's "rather over-push than miss" trade-off (nothing
// is missed), but the consequence is that the user believes they are doing
// tiered pushing while actually flooding the group with every vulnerability, and
// nothing hints at the misconfiguration. This kind of "silent degradation" is
// exactly what should be blocked at the entry point.
//
// Note that Validate is only used on the **write** path. The read path still
// follows ParseFilter's lenient semantics, so bad values already present in
// historical data do not make the whole channel unreadable.
func (f Filter) Validate() error {
	if !ValidMinSeverity(f.MinSeverity) {
		return fmt.Errorf("invalid min_severity %q; valid values: low / medium / high / critical, or empty for no threshold", f.MinSeverity)
	}
	return nil
}

// Match decides whether an event should be delivered to a channel carrying this
// filter.
//
// **It never returns an error**, for the same reason as ParseFilter: any internal
// anomaly is treated as "match". Order of checks: event kind → severity
// threshold → task/asset scope → vulnerability class keywords.
func Match(f Filter, s Snapshot) bool {
	// Status-change events are only received by channels that explicitly opted
	// in. Default is off, because the vast majority of users expect "push" to
	// mean "a new vulnerability was found", not a running log of every status
	// transition.
	if s.Kind == EventFindingStatusChanged && !f.OnStatusChange {
		return false
	}
	if !AtLeast(s.Severity, f.MinSeverity) {
		return false
	}
	if len(f.TaskIDs) > 0 && !slices.Contains(f.TaskIDs, s.TaskID) {
		return false
	}
	if len(f.AssetIDs) > 0 && !intersectsInt(f.AssetIDs, s.AssetIDs) {
		return false
	}
	// Exclusion first: hitting any exclusion keyword knocks the event out, even
	// if it also hits the include list.
	if len(f.VulnClassExclude) > 0 && containsAnyFold(s.VulnClass, f.VulnClassExclude) {
		return false
	}
	if len(f.VulnClassInclude) > 0 && !containsAnyFold(s.VulnClass, f.VulnClassInclude) {
		return false
	}
	return true
}

func intersectsInt(a, b []int64) bool {
	// Linear scan is fine for small sets; both sides are on the order of "a few
	// dozen hand-picked entries", so building a map costs more than it saves.
	for _, v := range b {
		if slices.Contains(a, v) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

// containsAnyFold reports whether s contains any of the keywords
// (case-insensitive).
func containsAnyFold(s string, keywords []string) bool {
	lower := strings.ToLower(s)
	for _, kw := range keywords {
		kw = strings.ToLower(strings.TrimSpace(kw))
		if kw != "" && strings.Contains(lower, kw) {
			return true
		}
	}
	return false
}

package notify

import "testing"

func TestParseFilterMalformedFallsBackToMatchAll(t *testing.T) {
	// Malformed JSON, empty input, fields of the wrong type — all must degrade to
	// a zero-value Filter, i.e. "no filtering". This invariant is where "rather
	// over-push than miss" lands: if this ever changes to erroring or partial
	// parsing, one mistyped character silently drops every high-severity
	// notification.
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		raw  string
	}{
		{"empty input", ""},
		{"invalid JSON", `{not json`},
		{"truncated JSON", `{"min_severity":`},
		{"type mismatch", `{"min_severity": 123, "task_ids": "abc"}`},
		{"top-level array", `[1,2,3]`},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			f := ParseFilter([]byte(tc.raw))
			if f.MinSeverity != "" || len(f.TaskIDs) != 0 || len(f.AssetIDs) != 0 {
				t.Fatalf("malformed configuration should degrade to a zero-value Filter, got %+v", f)
			}
			// A zero-value Filter must match any event.
			ev := Snapshot{Kind: EventFindingCreated, Severity: "low", VulnClass: "XSS"}
			if !Match(f, ev) {
				t.Fatal("a zero-value Filter should match all events")
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestMatchSeverityThreshold(t *testing.T) {
	ev := func(sev string) Snapshot {
		return Snapshot{Kind: EventFindingCreated, Severity: sev}
	}
	cases := []struct {
		min    string
		sev    string
		expect bool
	}{
		{"", "low", true},
		{"", "critical", true},
		{"high", "critical", true},
		{"high", "high", true},
		{"high", "medium", false},
		{"high", "low", false},
		{"critical", "high", false},
		{"critical", "critical", true},
		// Unknown severities have ordinal 0 and should be stopped by any non-empty
		// threshold (when in doubt, do not push).
		{"low", "", false},
		{"low", "unknown", false},
		{"", "", true},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		got := Match(Filter{MinSeverity: tc.min}, ev(tc.sev))
		if got != tc.expect {
			t.Errorf("min=%q sev=%q: want %v got %v", tc.min, tc.sev, tc.expect, got)
		}
	}
}

func TestMatchScopeRestrictions(t *testing.T) {
	ev := Snapshot{
		Kind:      EventFindingCreated,
		Severity:  "high",
		TaskID:    7,
		AssetIDs:  []int64{10, 20},
		VulnClass: "SQL injection",
	}
	cases := []struct {
		name   string
		filter Filter
		expect bool
	}{
		{"empty scope = unrestricted", Filter{}, true},
		{"task hit", Filter{TaskIDs: []int64{7}}, true},
		{"task miss", Filter{TaskIDs: []int64{8}}, false},
		{"task multi-select with hit", Filter{TaskIDs: []int64{8, 7}}, true},
		{"assets intersect", Filter{AssetIDs: []int64{20, 99}}, true},
		{"assets do not intersect", Filter{AssetIDs: []int64{99}}, false},
		{"task and asset both hit", Filter{TaskIDs: []int64{7}, AssetIDs: []int64{10}}, true},
		{"task hit but asset miss", Filter{TaskIDs: []int64{7}, AssetIDs: []int64{99}}, false},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := Match(tc.filter, ev); got != tc.expect {
				t.Errorf("want %v got %v", tc.expect, got)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestMatchVulnClassKeywords(t *testing.T) {
	ev := func(class string) Snapshot {
		return Snapshot{Kind: EventFindingCreated, Severity: "high", VulnClass: class}
	}
	cases := []struct {
		name   string
		filter Filter
		class  string
		expect bool
	}{
		{"empty include = accept all", Filter{}, "any class", true},
		{"include hit", Filter{VulnClassInclude: []string{"SQL"}}, "SQL injection", true},
		{"include miss", Filter{VulnClassInclude: []string{"command execution"}}, "SQL injection", false},
		{"include multi-word any hit", Filter{VulnClassInclude: []string{"command execution", "SQL"}}, "SQL injection", true},
		{"case insensitive", Filter{VulnClassInclude: []string{"sql"}}, "SQL injection", true},
		{"exclude hit excludes", Filter{VulnClassExclude: []string{"information disclosure"}}, "information disclosure", false},
		{"exclude miss passes", Filter{VulnClassExclude: []string{"information disclosure"}}, "SQL injection", true},
		// Exclusion takes precedence over inclusion: an event hitting both should
		// be knocked out.
		{"exclusion takes precedence over inclusion", Filter{
			VulnClassInclude: []string{"SQL"},
			VulnClassExclude: []string{"injection"},
		}, "SQL injection", false},
		// Pure-whitespace keywords must be ignored, otherwise they degrade into
		// "match any string containing a space".
		{"whitespace keywords ignored", Filter{VulnClassInclude: []string{"", "  "}}, "SQL injection", false},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			if got := Match(tc.filter, ev(tc.class)); got != tc.expect {
				t.Errorf("want %v got %v", tc.expect, got)
			}
		})
	}
}

func TestMatchStatusChangeRequiresOptIn(t *testing.T) {
	ev := Snapshot{Kind: EventFindingStatusChanged, Severity: "critical", FromStatus: "pending", ToStatus: "fixed"}
	// Default off: what most people mean by "push vulnerabilities" is discovering
	// new vulnerabilities, not a running log of status changes.
	if Match(Filter{MinSeverity: "low"}, ev) {
		t.Fatal("status-change events should be skipped when not enabled")
	}
	if !Match(Filter{OnStatusChange: true}, ev) {
		t.Fatal("status-change events should match once on_status_change is enabled")
	}
	// Creation events are not affected by on_status_change.
	created := Snapshot{Kind: EventFindingCreated, Severity: "critical"}
	if !Match(Filter{MinSeverity: "low"}, created) {
		t.Fatal("creation events should not depend on on_status_change")
	}
}

package notify

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// This file renders the HTML body of emails. It deliberately uses inline styles +
// simple table layout instead of modern CSS: email clients (especially Outlook
// and enterprise mailboxes) vary wildly in their support for <style> blocks and
// flex/grid; inline styles are the only way to render correctly everywhere.

// htmlSeverityColor returns the accent color for a severity, used for the left
// color bar and the title.
func htmlSeverityColor(severity string) string {
	switch severity {
	case "critical":
		return "#d32029"
	case "high":
		return "#e8830c"
	case "medium":
		return "#d4b106"
	case "low":
		return "#1677ff"
	default:
		return "#8c8c8c"
	}
}

// htmlTitle returns the email subject.
func htmlTitle(m Message) string {
	return markdownTitle(m)
}

// htmlBody renders the email body HTML. maxRunes<=0 means no truncation.
func htmlBody(m Message, maxRunes int) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(`<div style="font-family:-apple-system,BlinkMacSystemFont,'Segoe UI','PingFang SC','Microsoft YaHei',sans-serif;font-size:14px;color:#262626;line-height:1.6;">`)
	if m.Batch {
		b.WriteString(htmlBatchIntro(m))
		for _, it := range m.Items {
			b.WriteString(htmlItem(it, false, m.limits()))
		}
	} else if len(m.Items) > 0 {
		b.WriteString(htmlItem(m.Items[0], true, m.limits()))
	}
	if m.HomeURL != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<p style="margin:16px 0 0;"><a href="%s" style="color:#1677ff;">View all on the platform</a></p>`, htmlEscapeAttr(m.HomeURL))
	}
	b.WriteString(`</div>`)
	return TruncateHTML(b.String(), maxRunes)
}

// htmlBatchIntro renders the opening of a digest email: item count and severity
// distribution.
func htmlBatchIntro(m Message) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	if m.WindowMinutes > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<h2 style="font-size:16px;margin:0 0 4px;">%d new vulnerabilities in the last %d minutes</h2>`, len(m.Items), m.WindowMinutes)
	} else {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<h2 style="font-size:16px;margin:0 0 4px;">%d new vulnerabilities</h2>`, len(m.Items))
	}
	counts := map[string]int{}
	for _, it := range m.Items {
		counts[it.Severity]++
	}
	var parts []string
	for _, sev := range []string{"critical", "high", "medium", "low"} {
		if n := counts[sev]; n > 0 {
			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf(`<span style="color:%s;font-weight:600;">%s %d</span>`,
				htmlSeverityColor(sev), htmlEscape(SeverityLabel(sev)), n))
		}
	}
	if len(parts) > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<p style="margin:0 0 12px;">%s</p>`, strings.Join(parts, " &middot; "))
	}
	return b.String()
}

// htmlItem renders a single vulnerability. full=true includes the summary and
// backlink (single push); false compresses it into one line (digest list).
func htmlItem(it Item, full bool, lim Limits) string {
	color := htmlSeverityColor(it.Severity)
	var b strings.Builder
	if full {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<div style="border-left:4px solid %s;padding:8px 0 8px 12px;margin-bottom:12px;">`, color)
	} else {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<div style="border-left:3px solid %s;padding:4px 0 4px 10px;margin-bottom:8px;">`, color)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<div style="font-weight:600;">%s &middot; %s</div>`,
		htmlEscape(SeverityLabel(it.Severity)), htmlEscape(it.Title()))

	if !full {
		var extras []string
		if a := assetLine(it.Assets, lim.AssetsShown); a != "" {
			extras = append(extras, htmlEscape(a))
		}
		if it.Summary != "" {
			extras = append(extras, htmlEscape(OneLine(it.Summary, 60)))
		}
		if len(extras) > 0 {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<div style="color:#595959;font-size:13px;">%s</div>`, strings.Join(extras, " &middot; "))
		}
		b.WriteString(`</div>`)
		return b.String()
	}

	if it.IsStatusChange() {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<div><b>Status change</b>: %s → %s</div>`,
			htmlEscape(StatusLabel(it.FromStatus)), htmlEscape(StatusLabel(it.ToStatus)))
	}
	if it.VulnClass != "" && it.VulnClass != it.Title() {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<div><b>Type</b>: %s</div>`, htmlEscape(it.VulnClass))
	}
	if a := assetLine(it.Assets, lim.AssetsShown); a != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<div><b>Assets</b>: %s</div>`, htmlEscape(a))
	}
	if s := OneLine(it.Summary, lim.SummaryRunes); s != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<div><b>Summary</b>: %s</div>`, htmlEscape(s))
	}
	if it.DetailURL != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, `<div style="margin-top:6px;"><a href="%s" style="color:#1677ff;">View details</a></div>`, htmlEscapeAttr(it.DetailURL))
	}
	b.WriteString(`</div>`)
	return b.String()
}

// htmlEscape escapes HTML text content. Vulnerability titles and summaries come
// from the tested target and model output — untrusted content. Not escaping them
// amounts to allowing arbitrary HTML (including external images) to be injected
// into the email.
func htmlEscape(s string) string {
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "&", "&amp;")
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "<", "&lt;")
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, ">", "&gt;")
	return s
}

// htmlEscapeAttr escapes an HTML attribute value (on top of text escaping it
// also handles quotes, preventing a quote in a URL from closing the href
// attribute early).
func htmlEscapeAttr(s string) string {
	s = htmlEscape(s)
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\"", "&quot;")
	return s
}

package notify

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"io"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"syscall"
	"time"
)

// allowLocalTargets decides whether delivering messages to loopback / link-local
// addresses is allowed.
//
// Default is deny. These address ranges are not where IM bots or public mail
// servers live, and what they can reach is very sensitive: the admin port of
// another service on the same machine, and the cloud metadata endpoint
// (169.254.169.254, which gives out instance credentials). Delivery addresses
// are configured by admins, but an admin session hijacked via XSS/CSRF, or a
// second person sharing the same JWT, can change the configuration to read
// response content back — doJSON writes the first 200 bytes of a 4xx/5xx
// response body into last_error, and the delivery history API echoes it back,
// which amounts to a half-blind read primitive.
//
// However, a "local SMTP relay" (postfix on 127.0.0.1:25) is a common setup for
// self-hosted email, and an across-the-board ban would strand people. So there
// is an explicit escape hatch instead of a hardcoded allowance:
// set HIVE_NOTIFY_ALLOW_LOCAL=1 to allow it.
//
// It is exported as AllowLocalTargetsEnv so tests can turn it on explicitly —
// many test cases in this package and the server package use httptest fake
// receivers on 127.0.0.1, and without turning it on they would all be stopped by
// the guard.
const AllowLocalTargetsEnv = "HIVE_NOTIFY_ALLOW_LOCAL"

func allowLocalTargets() bool {
	v := strings.TrimSpace(os.Getenv(AllowLocalTargetsEnv))
	return v == "1" || strings.EqualFold(v, "true")
}

// isBlockedDialIP reports whether the target IP belongs to the ranges "not
// allowed for delivery by default".
//
// Only loopback, link-local (including the cloud metadata 169.254.169.254),
// unspecified, and multicast are rejected. RFC1918 private networks are **not**
// rejected: self-hosted Mattermost / SMTP relays on an intranet are very common
// legitimate uses, and blocking them too would make the feature flat-out
// unusable in real environments. This trade-off is deliberate — the protection
// must stop the truly sensitive targets without killing normal deployments along
// the way.
func isBlockedDialIP(ip net.IP) bool {
	if ip == nil {
		return true
	}
	// IPv4-mapped IPv6 (::ffff:127.0.0.1) must be converted back to IPv4 before
	// the check, otherwise it bypasses it.
	if v4 := ip.To4(); v4 != nil {
		ip = v4
	}
	return ip.IsLoopback() || ip.IsLinkLocalUnicast() || ip.IsLinkLocalMulticast() ||
		ip.IsInterfaceLocalMulticast() || ip.IsUnspecified() || ip.IsMulticast()
}

// blockInternalDial is the Control hook of the http.Transport dialer, checking
// the target address **when the connection is established**.
//
// Why at dial time instead of only validating when the configuration is saved:
// this is the final point of enforcement. It covers both ways of bypassing
// configuration-time validation — DNS rebinding (resolving to a public IP at
// validation time but to an intranet IP at connection time) and redirects
// (cross-host redirects are already refused, but a same-host redirect can still
// point the path elsewhere).
func blockInternalDial(_, address string, _ syscall.RawConn) error {
	if allowLocalTargets() {
		return nil
	}
	host, _, err := net.SplitHostPort(address)
	if err != nil {
		return err
	}
	ip := net.ParseIP(host)
	if ip == nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("cannot parse target address %q", host)
	}
	if isBlockedDialIP(ip) {
		return fmt.Errorf("refusing to deliver to loopback/link-local address %s (if you really need to deliver to a local service, set %s=1)", ip, AllowLocalTargetsEnv)
	}
	return nil
}

// notifyTransport adds only a dial guard on top of the default Transport. Clone
// keeps all of the default tuning (connection pool, HTTP/2, timeouts, proxy,
// etc.), avoiding changing other behaviors just to add one check.
var notifyTransport = func() *http.Transport {
	t, ok := http.DefaultTransport.(*http.Transport)
	if !ok {
		return &http.Transport{}
	}
	clone := t.Clone()
	clone.DialContext = (&net.Dialer{Timeout: 10 * time.Second, Control: blockInternalDial}).DialContext
	return clone
}()

// httpClient is the client shared by all channel deliveries.
//
// It deliberately does **not** reuse the project's global egress proxy (the
// server-side GlobalProxy): that proxy is for traffic to penetration-testing
// targets, often an unstable tunnel, and notification availability should not be
// hostage to jitter in the target network. IM pushes go direct. The timeout is
// 15 seconds — a peer slower than that is effectively down.
//
// Cross-host redirects are refused: delivery targets in this feature all take
// the shape of "one fixed endpoint" and would not normally redirect to another
// host; and the credentials of these platforms (DingTalk's access_token, WeCom's
// key, Telegram's bot token) **are in the URL** — following a cross-host redirect
// means handing the credentials to the redirect target. Same-host redirects
// (such as adding a trailing slash) are still allowed.
var httpClient = &http.Client{
	Timeout:   15 * time.Second,
	Transport: notifyTransport,
	CheckRedirect: func(req *http.Request, via []*http.Request) error {
		if len(via) >= 5 {
			return errors.New("too many redirects")
		}
		if len(via) > 0 && req.URL.Host != via[0].URL.Host {
			return fmt.Errorf("refusing cross-host redirect (%s → %s)", via[0].URL.Host, req.URL.Host)
		}
		return nil
	},
}

// respBodyLimit caps how much of the response body is read. An abnormal peer may
// spit back oversized content, while all we need is the error code and a short
// error description to show in the delivery history.
const respBodyLimit = 8 << 10

// doJSON sends one request and returns the response body (length-capped).
//
// A nil payload sends an empty body (for GET or platforms that do not require a
// body). Key-value pairs in headers are appended verbatim, for the generic
// webhook's custom headers.
//
// Error classification is a core responsibility of this function: network-layer
// failures and 5xx/408/429 are "retryable"; the remaining 4xx are "permanent
// failures" — retrying a 403 just logs the same error 3 times.
func doJSON(ctx context.Context, method, url string, headers map[string]string, payload any) ([]byte, error) {
	var body io.Reader
	if payload != nil {
		raw, err := json.Marshal(payload)
		if err != nil {
			// A serialization failure is a local bug (wrong config field type);
			// retrying will not make it better.
			return nil, Permanent(fmt.Errorf("failed to build request body: %w", err))
		}
		body = bytes.NewReader(raw)
	}
	req, err := http.NewRequestWithContext(ctx, method, url, body)
	if err != nil {
		// Invalid URL — most likely the user mistyped the address; a permanent
		// failure. err must not be passed through here either: url.Parse's error
		// text contains the full address.
		return nil, Permanent(fmt.Errorf("invalid request URL: %s", redactRequestTarget(url)))
	}
	if payload != nil {
		req.Header.Set("Content-Type", "application/json; charset=utf-8")
	}
	for k, v := range headers {
		req.Header.Set(k, v)
	}
	resp, err := httpClient.Do(req)
	if err != nil {
		// Connection refused, DNS failure, timeout — mostly transient, handed to
		// backoff retries.
		//
		// The error text must be redacted before being passed on. Reason:
		// http.Client.Do returns a *url.Error whose Error() is
		// `Op "full URL": underlying error`, and the credentials of these
		// platforms **are in the URL** (DingTalk access_token, WeCom key, Feishu
		// hook id, Telegram /bot<token>/). Without redaction, the credentials
		// ride this error string to four places: the last_error column of
		// notification_deliveries (stored in plaintext), the delivery history
		// API response (**bypassing the channel config masking**), server logs,
		// and the 502 text the test-send API returns to the frontend.
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("request failed: %s", redactTransportError(err))
	}
	defer resp.Body.Close()
	raw, readErr := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(resp.Body, respBodyLimit))
	if readErr != nil {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("failed to read response: %w", readErr)
	}
	if resp.StatusCode >= 200 && resp.StatusCode < 300 {
		return raw, nil
	}
	// 429 (rate limit) and 408 (timeout) are worth retrying; the remaining 4xx
	// are configuration or permission problems, and retrying is pointless.
	if resp.StatusCode == http.StatusTooManyRequests || resp.StatusCode == http.StatusRequestTimeout {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("peer rate limit or timeout (HTTP %d): %s", resp.StatusCode, snippet(raw))
	}
	if resp.StatusCode >= 500 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("peer server error (HTTP %d): %s", resp.StatusCode, snippet(raw))
	}
	return nil, Permanent(fmt.Errorf("peer rejected the request (HTTP %d): %s", resp.StatusCode, snippet(raw)))
}

// snippet compresses a response body into a one-line short text for error
// messages. Responses can carry newlines and lots of whitespace, and stuffing
// them raw into last_error would wreck the layout of the delivery history page.
func snippet(raw []byte) string {
	return OneLine(string(raw), 200)
}

// redactRequestTarget compresses a delivery address into "scheme://host/…" for
// error messages.
//
// This is the package's only address redaction convention, deliberately made
// **crude enough**: everything except scheme and host is dropped. The reason is
// that there is no "generic and safe" way to tell which part of a URL is the
// credential:
//
//	DingTalk  credential in query            /robot/send?access_token=xxx
//	WeCom     credential in query            /cgi-bin/webhook/send?key=xxx
//	Feishu    credential in the **last path segment** /open-apis/bot/v2/hook/<hook_id>
//	Telegram  credential in the **middle of the path** /bot<token>/sendMessage
//
// "Keeping only the useful parts" means patching per channel, and missing any
// one of them is a credential leak. Keeping the host is already enough for
// troubleshooting (DNS failures, connection failures, certificate problems can
// all be located), and which bot it is can be told from the masked tail hint in
// the channel configuration.
//
// On parse failure a fixed placeholder is returned — the raw string is never
// echoed back.
func redactRequestTarget(raw string) string {
	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
	if err != nil || u.Host == "" {
		return "(unparseable address)"
	}
	return u.Scheme + "://" + u.Host + "/…"
}

// redactTransportError strips the address from a transport-layer error, keeping
// only the underlying cause.
//
// A *url.Error is structured as {Op, URL, Err}, and Error() prints the URL along
// with it. Here the Err field is taken explicitly, bypassing its Error() — more
// reliable than string replacement after the fact, because replacement has to
// cope correctly with all the URL-encoded/escaped variants and is easy to get
// wrong.
func redactTransportError(err error) string {
	var uerr *url.Error
	if errors.As(err, &uerr) {
		host := ""
		if u, parseErr := url.Parse(uerr.URL); parseErr == nil {
			host = u.Host
		}
		if uerr.Err != nil {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: %s", uerr.Op, host, uerr.Err)
		}
		return fmt.Sprintf("%s %s: unknown error", uerr.Op, host)
	}
	// Non-*url.Error errors (such as the ones returned by the redirect policy)
	// can also carry addresses; redact them uniformly.
	return redactURLsInText(err.Error())
}

// redactURLsInText replaces http(s) addresses appearing in a piece of text with
// their redacted form.
//
// A fallback for errors whose structured fields are unavailable (redirect policy
// errors, custom errors from third-party libraries). Only http/https prefixes
// are recognized, split on whitespace and quotes — addresses never contain
// either.
func redactURLsInText(s string) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	for i := 0; i < len(s); {
		rest := s[i:]
		if strings.HasPrefix(rest, "http://") || strings.HasPrefix(rest, "https://") {
			end := len(rest)
			if j := strings.IndexAny(rest, " \t\n\"'"); j >= 0 {
				end = j
			}
			b.WriteString(redactRequestTarget(rest[:end]))
			i += end
			continue
		}
		b.WriteByte(s[i])
		i++
	}
	return b.String()
}

package notify

import (
	"context"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strconv"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// This file covers doJSON's HTTP-layer error classification.
//
// Why test it separately: each channel adapter only handles its own platform's
// business error codes (DingTalk errcode, Feishu code, Telegram ok field), while
// the **HTTP-layer** classification is done uniformly by doJSON — two independent
// lines of defense. Without this one, a relay gateway returning 503 would be
// treated as a permanent failure and retries abandoned outright; and a 403 would
// be treated as retryable, backing off three rounds for nothing.

func replyServer(t *testing.T, status int, body string) *httptest.Server {
	t.Helper()
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "application/json")
		w.WriteHeader(status)
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte(body))
	}))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	return srv
}

func TestDoJSONClassifiesHTTPStatus(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name      string
		status    int
		permanent bool
	}{
		{"200 success is not an error", 200, false},
		{"429 rate limit is retryable", 429, false},
		{"408 request timeout is retryable", 408, false},
		{"500 server error is retryable", 500, false},
		{"502 gateway error is retryable", 502, false},
		{"503 service unavailable is retryable", 503, false},
		{"400 bad parameters is permanent", 400, true},
		{"401 auth failure is permanent", 401, true},
		{"403 forbidden is permanent", 403, true},
		{"404 not found is permanent", 404, true},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			srv := replyServer(t, tc.status, `{"detail":"upstream says no"}`)
			_, err := doJSON(context.Background(), "GET", srv.URL, nil, nil)
			if tc.status < 300 {
				if err != nil {
					t.Fatalf("2xx should not error: %v", err)
				}
				return
			}
			if err == nil {
				t.Fatal("non-2xx should error")
			}
			if got := IsPermanent(err); got != tc.permanent {
				t.Fatalf("HTTP %d permanent classification wrong: want %v got %v (%v)",
					tc.status, tc.permanent, got, err)
			}
			// The status code must appear in the error, otherwise the user cannot
			// tell their own misconfiguration from a peer outage. Assert the
			// number rather than Go's English StatusText: the wording of this
			// package's messages may change, while the number is the
			// language-independent, stable part to assert on.
			if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), strconv.Itoa(tc.status)) {
				t.Errorf("error message should carry HTTP status code %d, got %v", tc.status, err)
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestDoJSONIncludesResponseSnippet covers snippet: the peer's error description
// must come back, otherwise the user only knows "it failed" without knowing why
// the peer refused.
func TestDoJSONIncludesResponseSnippet(t *testing.T) {
	srv := replyServer(t, 400, `{"error":"invalid webhook token"}`)
	_, err := doJSON(context.Background(), "GET", srv.URL, nil, nil)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("should error")
	}
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "invalid webhook token") {
		t.Errorf("error message should bring back the peer's description, got %v", err)
	}
}

// TestDoJSONSnippetIsSingleLineAndBounded constrains the shape of snippet: the
// peer response goes verbatim into the last_error column and the frontend table,
// and multiple lines / excessive length would break layout and payload.
func TestDoJSONSnippetIsSingleLineAndBounded(t *testing.T) {
	// A response with newlines, tabs, and 5000 characters of oversized content.
	long := strings.Repeat("x", 5000)
	srv := replyServer(t, 500, "line1\nline2\r\n\tline3 "+long)
	_, err := doJSON(context.Background(), "GET", srv.URL, nil, nil)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("should error")
	}
	msg := err.Error()
	if strings.ContainsAny(msg, "\r\n\t") {
		t.Errorf("error message should be compressed to a single line, got %q", msg)
	}
	// snippet cap of 200 characters + fixed prefix; the total must be far smaller
	// than the original response.
	if len(msg) > 400 {
		t.Errorf("error message too long (%d bytes), should have been truncated by snippet: %q", len(msg), msg)
	}
}

// TestDoJSONRejectsOversizedResponse confirms reads are capped: when a peer
// abnormally returns oversized content, the whole response must not be read into
// memory (every entry in the delivery history stores a copy of last_error).
func TestDoJSONRejectsOversizedResponse(t *testing.T) {
	huge := strings.Repeat("A", 1<<20) // 1 MiB
	srv := replyServer(t, 400, huge)
	_, err := doJSON(context.Background(), "GET", srv.URL, nil, nil)
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("should error")
	}
	if len(err.Error()) > 400 {
		t.Errorf("oversized responses should be read length-capped and truncated, error message length %d", len(err.Error()))
	}
}

package notify

import (
	"context"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"unicode/utf8"
)

// This file covers the configurable render limits (Message.Limits). The summary
// length and the number of assets listed used to be the fixed constants 120 / 3;
// they now come from the caller, with 0 meaning "no truncation" and nil meaning
// "the old defaults".

// limitsItem returns an item whose summary (200 characters) and asset list (8)
// both exceed the defaults. It contains no markdown/HTML metacharacters, so
// every renderer emits the text verbatim and one set of assertions fits all.
func limitsItem() Item {
	assets := make([]string, 8)
	for i := range assets {
		assets[i] = "host" + itoa(i+1)
	}
	return Item{Severity: "high", Name: "title", Summary: strings.Repeat("Z", 200), Assets: assets}
}

// feishuContent returns the lark_md text of the card's element idx.
func feishuContent(t *testing.T, m Message, idx int) string {
	t.Helper()
	card, _ := feishuCard(m)
	elements, _ := card["elements"].([]any)
	if idx >= len(elements) {
		t.Fatalf("card has %d elements, cannot get element %d", len(elements), idx)
	}
	div, _ := elements[idx].(map[string]any)
	text, _ := div["text"].(map[string]any)
	content, _ := text["content"].(string)
	return content
}

// limitsRenderings returns the body of every channel family that applies the
// limits. For a digest, the Feishu entry is the first item line (element 0 is
// the intro).
func limitsRenderings(t *testing.T, m Message) map[string]string {
	t.Helper()
	md, _ := markdownBody(m, 0)
	tg, _ := telegramHTML(m)
	feishuIdx := 0
	if m.Batch {
		feishuIdx = 1
	}
	return map[string]string{
		"markdown": md,
		"feishu":   feishuContent(t, m, feishuIdx),
		"telegram": tg,
		"email":    htmlBody(m, 0),
	}
}

func TestMessageLimitsApplyToSinglePush(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		name  string
		lim   *Limits
		must  []string
		wrong []string
	}{
		{
			name:  "unset keeps the 120 / 3 defaults",
			lim:   nil,
			must:  []string{strings.Repeat("Z", 119) + ellipsis, "host1, host2, host3 and 5 more"},
			wrong: []string{strings.Repeat("Z", 120), "host4"},
		},
		{
			name:  "zero means no truncation",
			lim:   &Limits{},
			must:  []string{strings.Repeat("Z", 200), "host7, host8"},
			wrong: []string{ellipsis, " more"},
		},
		{
			name:  "custom values",
			lim:   &Limits{SummaryRunes: 10, AssetsShown: 1},
			must:  []string{strings.Repeat("Z", 9) + ellipsis, "host1 and 7 more"},
			wrong: []string{strings.Repeat("Z", 10), "host2"},
		},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			m := Message{Items: []Item{limitsItem()}, Limits: tc.lim}
			for channel, got := range limitsRenderings(t, m) {
				for _, want := range tc.must {
					if !strings.Contains(got, want) {
						t.Errorf("%s: missing %q:\n%s", channel, want, got)
					}
				}
				for _, bad := range tc.wrong {
					if strings.Contains(got, bad) {
						t.Errorf("%s: %q should not appear:\n%s", channel, bad, got)
					}
				}
			}
		})
	}
}

// TestMessageLimitsApplyToDigestAssets covers the digest lines, which list the
// assets too. The digest summary is not governed by Limits.SummaryRunes: it
// stays at its own fixed 60 characters (markdown and email), a digest being a
// list of one-liners.
func TestMessageLimitsApplyToDigestAssets(t *testing.T) {
	m := Message{Batch: true, Items: []Item{limitsItem()}}
	for channel, got := range limitsRenderings(t, m) {
		if !strings.Contains(got, "host1, host2, host3 and 5 more") {
			t.Errorf("%s: unset should keep 3 assets:\n%s", channel, got)
		}
	}
	m.Limits = &Limits{}
	for channel, got := range limitsRenderings(t, m) {
		if !strings.Contains(got, "host7, host8") || strings.Contains(got, " more") {
			t.Errorf("%s: 0 should list every asset:\n%s", channel, got)
		}
		if strings.Contains(got, strings.Repeat("Z", 60)) {
			t.Errorf("%s: the digest summary should stay within 60 characters:\n%s", channel, got)
		}
	}
}

// TestFeishuUntruncatedItemStaysWithinBodyLimit is the guard that goes with
// "0 = no truncation". Feishu custom bots reject a request body over 20 KB as a
// whole, so an unbounded summary or asset list would not arrive shortened — it
// would not arrive at all. The body measured here is the real one sent on the
// wire, signature included.
func TestFeishuUntruncatedItemStaysWithinBodyLimit(t *testing.T) {
	const feishuBodyLimit = 20000

	huge := limitsItem()
	huge.DetailURL = "https://hive.local/function/findings/detail?id=42"
	// 36000 bytes of CJK: also checks that the cut lands on a character boundary.
	huge.Summary = strings.Repeat("漏洞摘要", 3000)
	huge.Assets = nil
	for i := 0; i < 1500; i++ {
		huge.Assets = append(huge.Assets, "host"+itoa(i+1)+".example.com")
	}

	cases := []struct {
		name string
		m    Message
		idx  int
	}{
		{"single push", Message{Items: []Item{huge}, Limits: &Limits{}}, 0},
		{"digest whose first item is oversized", Message{
			Batch: true, WindowMinutes: 30, HomeURL: "https://hive.local/function/findings",
			Items: []Item{huge, huge}, Limits: &Limits{},
		}, 1},
	}
	for _, tc := range cases {
		t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
			size := 0
			srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
				raw, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
				size = len(raw)
				_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"code":0,"msg":"success"}`)
			}))
			defer srv.Close()

			kept, err := (feishuChannel{}).Send(context.Background(), map[string]any{"webhook": srv.URL, "secret": "SECtest123"}, tc.m)
			if err != nil {
				t.Fatalf("delivery failed: %v", err)
			}
			if kept != 1 {
				t.Fatalf("exactly the first item should be reported as delivered, got %d", kept)
			}
			if size == 0 || size > feishuBodyLimit {
				t.Fatalf("request body of %d bytes, want 1..%d", size, feishuBodyLimit)
			}
			content := feishuContent(t, tc.m, tc.idx)
			if !utf8.ValidString(content) || !strings.HasSuffix(content, ellipsis) {
				t.Fatalf("the item should be cut on a character boundary and end with an ellipsis, got tail %q", content[len(content)-12:])
			}
		})
	}
}

FILE: notify/markdown.go

package notify

import (
	"fmt"
	"strings"
)

// This file is the message rendering shared by the "Markdown family" channels
// (DingTalk, WeCom). Feishu uses card JSON, Telegram uses HTML, and email uses
// HTML; each renders in its own adapter.

// DefaultMaxAssetsShown is the default maximum number of assets listed in a
// message (Limits.AssetsShown). A vulnerability can be anchored to dozens of
// assets; listing them all would blow up the message with no informational
// value — nobody reads the 4th domain onwards in an IM.
const DefaultMaxAssetsShown = 3

// DefaultMaxSummaryRunes is the default number of characters the summary is
// compressed to (Limits.SummaryRunes). An IM message is a "go look at the
// details" hint, not the report itself; the full content lives on the platform.
const DefaultMaxSummaryRunes = 120

// markdownReservedBytes is reserved for the message header (digest line +
// severity distribution + possible truncation notice) and footer (platform
// link). When packing whole items, this part is deducted from the budget so the
// head and tail are never cut off — once they are, readers cannot even tell
// "which batch this is and how many items are not shown".
const markdownReservedBytes = 320

// markdownEscape escapes markdown metacharacters.
//
// Why this is mandatory: vulnerability titles, summaries, classes, and asset
// display names all come from **untrusted sources** — titles and summaries come
// from model output (the model reads the tested target's responses), and an
// asset's url is the full URL obtained from scanning (including a
// target-controlled query string). Without escaping, a vulnerability titled
//
//	SQL injection on login page\n[URGENT: click to verify your account](http://attacker.tld)
//
// would render in the security engineer's DingTalk/Feishu as a **clickable
// external link**; and `![](http://attacker.tld/beacon)` would be fetched by the
// client at render time, effectively reporting "this vulnerability has been
// read" and leaking the reader's IP. Even for non-malicious content, injected
// bold text or quote blocks can push the critical vulnerabilities below the
// fold.
//
// The escape set covers the characters for headings/links/emphasis/lists/
// quotes/strikethrough — the ones that change structure or produce clickable
// elements. `\` must be handled first, otherwise the backslashes added later
// would be escaped again.
func markdownEscape(s string) string {
	replacer := strings.NewReplacer(
		`\`, `\\`,
		"`", "\\`",
		"*", `\*`,
		"_", `\_`,
		"[", `\[`,
		"]", `\]`,
		"(", `\(`,
		")", `\)`,
		"!", `\!`,
		"#", `\#`,
		">", `\>`,
		"|", `\|`,
		"~", `\~`,
	)
	return replacer.Replace(s)
}

// markdownText compresses untrusted text into a single line and escapes it, for
// use in markdown bodies. Single-lining is the other half beyond escaping: a
// newline by itself can forge a new list item or quote block, and escape
// characters cannot stop it.
func markdownText(s string, maxRunes int) string {
	return markdownEscape(OneLine(s, maxRunes))
}

// markdownTitle returns the message title (the title bar of IM platforms / card
// title); its content is the **unescaped original text**.
//
// The lack of escaping here is deliberate: this title is shared by renderers in
// four contexts — markdown bodies, Telegram's HTML, Feishu card plain_text, and
// the generic webhook's JSON plus the email subject. Each context has different
// escaping rules (markdown escapes put into HTML leave visible backslashes; put
// into JSON they pollute the data), so escaping must be done by each output side;
// see writeItem / feishuItemLines / telegramEscape. A markdown escape was once
// added to the shared function, and Telegram messages ended up showing visible
// backslashes like `\(1\)`.
func markdownTitle(m Message) string {
	if m.Batch {
		return fmt.Sprintf("Vulnerability digest · %d total", len(m.Items))
	}
	if len(m.Items) == 0 {
		return "Vulnerability notification"
	}
	it := m.Items[0]
	return fmt.Sprintf("[%s] %s", SeverityLabel(it.Severity), OneLine(it.Title(), 0))
}

// markdownBody renders the message body and returns it together with the
// **number of items actually written**.
//
// The returned kept is the number of items actually delivered by this send, and
// the caller uses it to mark only the first kept items as sent — items kept out
// by the channel's length limit must remain for the next batch instead of being
// marked as succeeded along with the rest. This is exactly where "silent loss"
// comes from: the message was truncated, but the delivery records show all
// delivered, and nowhere can you tell the second half was never sent.
//
// maxBytes<=0 means unlimited.
func markdownBody(m Message, maxBytes int) (string, int) {
	if !m.Batch {
		if len(m.Items) == 0 {
			return "", 0
		}
		var b strings.Builder
		writeItem(&b, m.Items[0], "", true, m.limits())
		// A single message is sent even if oversized (with final truncation as
		// the backstop): partial information about one vulnerability is better
		// than sending nothing at all.
		return TruncateBytes(b.String(), maxBytes), 1
	}

	footer := ""
	if m.HomeURL != "" {
		footer = fmt.Sprintf("\n[View all on the platform](%s)\n", m.HomeURL)
	}
	kept := packItemCount(m.Items, maxBytes, markdownReservedBytes, footer, byteSize, func(it Item, idx int) string {
		var b strings.Builder
		writeItem(&b, it, fmt.Sprintf("%d. ", idx+1), false, m.limits())
		return b.String()
	})

	items := m.Items[:kept]
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString(markdownBatchIntro(m, items, len(m.Items)))
	for i, it := range items {
		writeItem(&b, it, fmt.Sprintf("%d. ", i+1), false, m.limits())
	}
	b.WriteString(footer)
	return TruncateBytes(b.String(), maxBytes), kept
}

// markdownBatchIntro renders the opening of a digest message: time window, item
// count, and severity distribution. With these, whoever receives the digest can
// judge whether this batch needs immediate handling without opening the
// platform.
//
// items are the ones **actually included**; total is the number the batch should
// have. When the two differ it must be stated explicitly — "how many more items
// are in the next message" — otherwise readers take the number in the header for
// the whole batch, and the items never sent simply do not exist anywhere in the
// UI.
func markdownBatchIntro(m Message, items []Item, total int) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	if m.WindowMinutes > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "**%d new vulnerabilities in the last %d minutes**", total, m.WindowMinutes)
	} else {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "**%d new vulnerabilities**", total)
	}
	if extra := total - len(items); extra > 0 {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, " (this message shows the first %d, the remaining %d will continue in the next message)", len(items), extra)
	}
	// Give the distribution by severity so readers can spot critical items at a
	// glance. Only count the items **actually included in this message**, so that
	// "Critical 3" matches what can be counted below.
	counts := map[string]int{}
	for _, it := range items {
		counts[it.Severity]++
	}
	var parts []string
	for _, sev := range []string{"critical", "high", "medium", "low"} {
		if n := counts[sev]; n > 0 {
			parts = append(parts, fmt.Sprintf("%s %d", SeverityLabel(sev), n))
		}
	}
	if len(parts) > 0 {
		b.WriteString("\n" + strings.Join(parts, " · "))
	}
	b.WriteString("\n\n")
	return b.String()
}

// writeItem renders a single vulnerability item.
//
// prefix is the sequence number in a digest list; single=true renders the full
// version (with summary and backlink), while the digest list renders only a
// one-line summary — otherwise a 50-item digest becomes a long document.
//
// All content from outside (title/class/assets/summary) goes through
// markdownText: single-lining + escaping. The backlink is built from the
// admin-configured public_base_url, is not untrusted content, and must be a
// clickable link, so it is emitted as-is.
func writeItem(b *strings.Builder, it Item, prefix string, single bool, lim Limits) {
	line := fmt.Sprintf("%s**%s · %s**", prefix, SeverityLabel(it.Severity), markdownText(it.Title(), 0))
	if !single {
		// Digest mode: single-line presentation, with assets and summary
		// compressed and appended.
		var extras []string
		if a := assetLine(it.Assets, lim.AssetsShown); a != "" {
			extras = append(extras, markdownText(a, 0))
		}
		if it.Summary != "" {
			extras = append(extras, markdownText(it.Summary, 60))
		}
		if len(extras) > 0 {
			line += " — " + strings.Join(extras, " · ")
		}
		b.WriteString(line + "\n")
		return
	}
	b.WriteString(line + "\n")
	if it.IsStatusChange() {
		fmt.Fprintf(b, "**Status change**: %s → %s\n",
			markdownText(StatusLabel(it.FromStatus), 0), markdownText(StatusLabel(it.ToStatus), 0))
	}
	if it.VulnClass != "" && it.VulnClass != it.Title() {
		fmt.Fprintf(b, "**Type**: %s\n", markdownText(it.VulnClass, 0))
	}
	if a := assetLine(it.Assets, lim.AssetsShown); a != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(b, "**Assets**: %s\n", markdownText(a, 0))
	}
	if it.Summary != "" {
		if s := markdownText(it.Summary, lim.SummaryRunes); s != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(b, "**Summary**: %s\n", s)
		}
	}
	if it.DetailURL != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(b, "[View details](%s)\n", it.DetailURL)
	}
}

FILE: notify/mask.go
