package notify

import (
	"context"
	"io"
	"net"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"net/url"
	"os"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// This file covers two related hardenings:
//   ① delivery addresses must not turn the server into a springboard into
//     intranets / cloud metadata (SSRF)
//   ② error messages from address validation must not carry the credentials
//     embedded in the address
//
// About the test environment: many cases in this package use httptest fake
// receivers on 127.0.0.1, which the guard would block by default. So TestMain
// turns on AllowLocalTargetsEnv globally, while every SSRF case below explicitly
// clears it to assert the **deny-by-default** behavior.

func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
	// Let regular cases reach the local fake receivers; SSRF cases clear it
	// temporarily themselves.
	_ = os.Setenv(AllowLocalTargetsEnv, "1")
	os.Exit(m.Run())
}

// TestDialGuardRejectsLoopbackByDefault is the core assertion of SSRF
// protection: under default configuration, delivering to a loopback address must
// be refused at the **connection layer**.
func TestDialGuardRejectsLoopbackByDefault(t *testing.T) {
	var hit bool
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		hit = true
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"errcode":0}`)
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	t.Setenv(AllowLocalTargetsEnv, "") // closing the escape hatch = default behavior
	_, err := (dingTalkChannel{}).Send(context.Background(),
		map[string]any{"webhook": srv.URL + "/robot/send"}, Message{Items: []Item{{Severity: "high"}}})
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("delivery to loopback addresses should not be allowed by default")
	}
	if hit {
		t.Fatal("the request already hit the local service — the guard did not work")
	}
	// The error message must be able to guide the user on how to opt in (a local
	// SMTP relay is a legitimate configuration).
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), AllowLocalTargetsEnv) {
		t.Errorf("the refusal message should explain how to explicitly opt in: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestDialGuardAllowsLoopbackWhenOptedIn is the counterpart: once explicitly
// enabled it must work, otherwise legitimate deployments like a local postfix /
// intranet relay would be killed by an across-the-board ban.
func TestDialGuardAllowsLoopbackWhenOptedIn(t *testing.T) {
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request) {
		_, _ = io.WriteString(w, `{"errcode":0,"errmsg":"ok"}`)
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	t.Setenv(AllowLocalTargetsEnv, "1")
	if _, err := (dingTalkChannel{}).Send(context.Background(),
		map[string]any{"webhook": srv.URL + "/robot/send"}, Message{Items: []Item{{Severity: "high"}}}); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("delivery should work once explicitly allowed: %v", err)
	}
}

func TestIsBlockedDialIP(t *testing.T) {
	blocked := []string{
		"127.0.0.1", "127.1.2.3", "::1",
		"169.254.169.254", // cloud metadata endpoint — the main reason this function exists
		"169.254.1.1", "fe80::1",
		"0.0.0.0", "::",
		"224.0.0.1", "ff02::1",
		"::ffff:127.0.0.1", // the IPv4-mapped form must be converted back before the check, otherwise it is a bypass
		"",
	}
	for _, s := range blocked {
		if !isBlockedDialIP(net.ParseIP(s)) {
			t.Errorf("%s should be rejected", s)
		}
	}
	// RFC1918 private networks are **deliberately allowed**: self-hosted
	// Mattermost / SMTP relays on an intranet are common legitimate uses. This
	// assertion pins down the trade-off — if someone casually adds a private-net
	// check in the future, this fails, forcing a conscious decision (instead of
	// silently killing a batch of deployments).
	allowed := []string{"10.0.0.5", "172.16.3.4", "192.168.1.10", "8.8.8.8", "2606:4700::1111"}
	for _, s := range allowed {
		if isBlockedDialIP(net.ParseIP(s)) {
			t.Errorf("%s should be allowed (private networks are common legitimate delivery targets)", s)
		}
	}
}

// TestValidateHTTPURLRejectsLiteralPrivateTargets covers the early warning at
// configuration time: literal IPs should be rejected at save time rather than
// waiting for the first delivery to fail.
func TestValidateHTTPURLRejectsLiteralPrivateTargets(t *testing.T) {
	t.Setenv(AllowLocalTargetsEnv, "")
	for _, raw := range []string{
		"http://127.0.0.1:8080/hook",
		"http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/",
		"http://[::1]:8080/hook",
	} {
		if err := validateHTTPURL(raw); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%s should be rejected at configuration time", raw)
		}
	}
	// Public addresses and private-network addresses pass as usual (private
	// networks are left to the dial phase, which does not block them).
	for _, raw := range []string{"https://oapi.dingtalk.com/robot/send", "http://10.0.0.9/hook"} {
		if err := validateHTTPURL(raw); err != nil {
			t.Errorf("%s should pass validation: %v", raw, err)
		}
	}
}

// TestValidateHTTPURLErrorNeverLeaksCredentials is the branch the audit pointed
// out that my previous round missed.
//
// When url.Parse **fails** it returns a *url.Error whose Error() contains the
// full original address. The previous round only redacted the errors returned by
// http.Client.Do and missed this one; and the "permanent failure path" cases
// added at the time (file://, gopher://, ftp://) all actually parse fine with
// url.Parse and go down the scheme branch — so staying green proved nothing
// about this path being safe. It was a false guarantee.
func TestValidateHTTPURLErrorNeverLeaksCredentials(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []string{
		"http://127.0.0.1/%zz?access_token=" + leakProbeToken,         // invalid percent escape
		"https://a.example.com:port/x?access_token=" + leakProbeToken, // non-numeric port
		"http://[::1?access_token=" + leakProbeToken,                  // unbalanced brackets
	}
	for _, raw := range cases {
		// First confirm this input **really** makes url.Parse fail. Without this
		// step, a case could silently end up in another branch (that is exactly
		// how the previous round's false guarantee happened).
		if _, err := url.Parse(raw); err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%q should have failed to parse, otherwise this case does not cover the target branch", raw)
			continue
		}
		err := validateHTTPURL(raw)
		if err == nil {
			t.Errorf("%q should fail validation", raw)
			continue
		}
		assertNoSecret(t, err.Error(), leakProbeToken)
	}
	// Confirm the channel-layer wrapping does not leak the address either.
	t.Setenv(AllowLocalTargetsEnv, "")
	err := (dingTalkChannel{}).Validate(map[string]any{"webhook": cases[0]})
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("an invalid address should fail validation")
	}
	assertNoSecret(t, err.Error(), leakProbeToken)
}

// TestEmailDialGuardRejectsLoopbackByDefault covers the SMTP channel's dial
// guard.
//
// The email channel once used a bare net.Dialer, the only gap in the whole SSRF
// protection: setting host to 169.254.169.254 or 127.0.0.1 connected directly,
// and when the smtp.NewClient handshake failed it wrapped the peer's response
// line into the error, echoed back via last_error through the delivery history
// API — exactly the half-blind read primitive the other channels had already
// closed; and the timing difference between "connection refused vs timeout"
// could be used to probe ports.
//
// This package's TestMain globally enables AllowLocalTargetsEnv (many cases use
// fake receivers on 127.0.0.1), so this case must clear it itself — otherwise it
// passes whether the guard is there or not, which is exactly why the gap was
// never caught by any test back then.
func TestEmailDialGuardRejectsLoopbackByDefault(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFakeSMTP(t)
	cfg := emailCfg(t, f, nil)

	t.Setenv(AllowLocalTargetsEnv, "") // closing the escape hatch = default behavior
	_, err := (emailChannel{}).Send(context.Background(), cfg, singleMsg())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("delivering email to a loopback address should not be allowed by default")
	}
	// The connection should never be established at all: the guard blocks in the
	// Control hook, and EHLO is never sent.
	if f.sawCommand("EHLO") || f.sawCommand("HELO") {
		t.Fatal("the SMTP session was already established — the guard did not work")
	}
	// The error message must be able to guide the user on how to opt in (a local
	// postfix relay is a legitimate configuration).
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), AllowLocalTargetsEnv) {
		t.Errorf("the refusal message should explain how to explicitly opt in: %v", err)
	}
}

// TestEmailDialGuardAllowsLoopbackWhenOptedIn is the paired counterpart: once
// explicitly enabled, delivery must work normally. Self-hosted intranet SMTP /
// local relays are very common deployments, and the guard must not ban them
// across the board.
func TestEmailDialGuardAllowsLoopbackWhenOptedIn(t *testing.T) {
	f := newFakeSMTP(t)
	cfg := emailCfg(t, f, nil)

	t.Setenv(AllowLocalTargetsEnv, "1")
	if _, err := (emailChannel{}).Send(context.Background(), cfg, singleMsg()); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("local SMTP should be deliverable once explicitly allowed: %v", err)
	}
	if !f.sawCommand("EHLO") {
		t.Fatal("no EHLO seen — the session was never really established")
	}
}

FILE: notify/telegram.go

package notify

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/url"
	"strings"
)

// telegramTextLimit is the text field limit (in characters) of Telegram
// sendMessage.
const telegramTextLimit = 4096

// telegramChannel implements the Telegram Bot API.
//
// Platform traits:
//   - Authentication lives entirely in the URL path (/bot<token>/sendMessage);
//     no signing needed.
//   - Uses HTML parse mode instead of MarkdownV2: MarkdownV2 requires escaping
//     18 characters `_*[]()~`>#+-=|{}.!` and missing a single one gets the whole
//     message rejected; HTML only requires escaping & < >.
//   - Business errors likewise hide inside HTTP 200, detected via the ok field.
type telegramChannel struct{}

func (telegramChannel) Kind() string { return KindTelegram }

// Telegram allows about 1 message/second in private chats and 20 messages/minute
// in groups. Take the conservative value.
func (telegramChannel) DefaultRatePerMin() int { return 20 }

// The Bot Token is the full credential; chat_id is just the recipient, not a
// secret (having it without the Token does not let you send messages).
func (telegramChannel) SecretKeys() []string { return []string{"bot_token"} }

// base_url decides which API endpoint the Token is sent to (e.g. a self-hosted
// reverse proxy); changing it requires re-declaring the Token.
func (telegramChannel) DestinationKeys() []string { return []string{"base_url"} }

func (telegramChannel) Validate(cfg map[string]any) error {
	if cfgString(cfg, "bot_token") == "" {
		return errors.New("missing Bot Token")
	}
	if cfgString(cfg, "chat_id") == "" {
		return errors.New("missing Chat ID")
	}
	if base := cfgString(cfg, "base_url"); base != "" {
		if err := validateHTTPURL(base); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("invalid API URL: %w", err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func (c telegramChannel) Send(ctx context.Context, cfg map[string]any, m Message) (int, error) {
	if err := c.Validate(cfg); err != nil {
		return 0, Permanent(err)
	}
	endpoint, err := telegramEndpoint(cfg)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, Permanent(err)
	}
	text, kept := telegramHTML(m)
	payload := map[string]any{
		"chat_id":                  cfgString(cfg, "chat_id"),
		"text":                     text,
		"parse_mode":               "HTML",
		"disable_web_page_preview": false,
	}
	raw, err := doJSON(ctx, "POST", endpoint, nil, payload)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	var res struct {
		OK          bool   `json:"ok"`
		ErrorCode   int    `json:"error_code"`
		Description string `json:"description"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &res); err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse Telegram response: %w (%s)", err, snippet(raw))
	}
	if res.OK {
		return kept, nil
	}
	// 429 is rate limiting and retries after backoff work; the rest (400 bad
	// parameters, 401 bad token, 403 blocked, 404 chat not found) are
	// configuration problems that retries will not fix.
	if res.ErrorCode == 429 {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("Telegram rate limit: %s", res.Description)
	}
	return 0, Permanent(fmt.Errorf("Telegram returned error %d: %s", res.ErrorCode, res.Description))
}

// telegramEndpoint builds the sendMessage URL. An empty base_url uses the
// official API; a non-empty one is for a self-hosted Bot API reverse proxy (a
// common need on networks where the official API is unreachable).
func telegramEndpoint(cfg map[string]any) (string, error) {
	base := cfgString(cfg, "base_url")
	if base == "" {
		base = "https://api.telegram.org"
	}
	base = strings.TrimSuffix(base, "/")
	token := cfgString(cfg, "bot_token")
	raw := base + "/bot" + token + "/sendMessage"
	u, err := url.Parse(raw)
	if err != nil {
		// Do not pass err through: the URL contains the Bot Token, and at this
		// point not even the address should be echoed.
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to build API URL (base URL: %s)", redactRequestTarget(base))
	}
	return u.String(), nil
}

// telegramHTML renders the HTML body and returns it together with the number of
// items actually written (see Channel.Send).
func telegramHTML(m Message) (string, int) {
	lim := m.limits()
	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("<b>" + telegramEscape(markdownTitle(m)) + "</b>\n")
	if m.Batch {
		// Telegram's limit is in **characters**, so packing is measured in
		// characters too (runeSize).
		footer := ""
		if m.HomeURL != "" {
			footer = fmt.Sprintf("\n\n<a href=\"%s\">View all on the platform</a>", telegramEscapeAttr(m.HomeURL))
		}
		kept := packItemCount(m.Items, telegramTextLimit, telegramReservedRunes, footer, runeSize, func(it Item, idx int) string {
			return telegramBatchLine(it, idx+1, lim)
		})
		items := m.Items[:kept]
		b.Reset()
		b.WriteString("<b>" + telegramEscape(telegramBatchTitle(m, items, len(m.Items))) + "</b>")
		for i, it := range items {
			b.WriteString("\n" + telegramEscape(telegramBatchLine(it, i+1, lim)))
		}
		b.WriteString(footer)
		return TruncateHTML(b.String(), telegramTextLimit), kept
	}
	if len(m.Items) == 0 {
		return b.String(), 0
	}
	it := m.Items[0]
	if it.IsStatusChange() {
		b.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("\n<b>Status change</b>: %s → %s",
			telegramEscape(StatusLabel(it.FromStatus)), telegramEscape(StatusLabel(it.ToStatus))))
	}
	if it.VulnClass != "" && it.VulnClass != it.Title() {
		b.WriteString("\n<b>Type</b>: " + telegramEscape(it.VulnClass))
	}
	if a := assetLine(it.Assets, lim.AssetsShown); a != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n<b>Assets</b>: " + telegramEscape(a))
	}
	if s := OneLine(it.Summary, lim.SummaryRunes); s != "" {
		b.WriteString("\n<b>Summary</b>: " + telegramEscape(s))
	}
	if it.DetailURL != "" {
		b.WriteString(fmt.Sprintf("\n\n<a href=\"%s\">View details</a>", telegramEscapeAttr(it.DetailURL)))
	}
	return TruncateHTML(b.String(), telegramTextLimit), 1
}

// telegramReservedRunes is reserved for the message title and a possible
// truncation notice (in characters).
const telegramReservedRunes = 160

// telegramBatchLine renders one entry of a digest (unescaped; the caller escapes
// it uniformly).
func telegramBatchLine(it Item, idx int, lim Limits) string {
	if a := assetLine(it.Assets, lim.AssetsShown); a != "" {
		return fmt.Sprintf("%d. %s · %s — %s", idx, SeverityLabel(it.Severity), it.Title(), a)
	}
	return fmt.Sprintf("%d. %s · %s", idx, SeverityLabel(it.Severity), it.Title())
}

// telegramBatchTitle renders the title line of a digest message. The count is
// the number of items **actually included in this message**, not the batch
// total — otherwise readers would take the number in the header for the whole
// batch.
func telegramBatchTitle(m Message, items []Item, total int) string {
	title := fmt.Sprintf("Vulnerability digest · %d total", total)
	if extra := total - len(items); extra > 0 {
		title += fmt.Sprintf(" (showing the first %d, %d more in the next message)", len(items), extra)
	}
	if m.WindowMinutes > 0 {
		title = fmt.Sprintf("Last %d min · %s", m.WindowMinutes, title)
	}
	return title
}

// telegramEscape escapes HTML text content.
// Telegram only recognizes these three entities, so existing entities like &amp;
// get double-escaped — which is exactly the desired behavior: we want to display
// the raw characters, not let users inject HTML.
func telegramEscape(s string) string {
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "&", "&amp;")
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "<", "&lt;")
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, ">", "&gt;")
	return s
}

// telegramEscapeAttr escapes an HTML attribute value. On top of text escaping it
// also handles quotes — a quote in a URL would close the href attribute early
// and turn the rest into an injection point.
func telegramEscapeAttr(s string) string {
	s = telegramEscape(s)
	s = strings.ReplaceAll(s, "\"", "&quot;")
	return s
}

package notify

import (
	"bytes"
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"strings"
	"text/template"
	"time"
)

// webhookChannel is the generic webhook adapter: the user defines the URL,
// method, request headers, and JSON template. Its existence means this feature
// does not need a separate implementation for Slack / Mattermost / Discord /
// self-hosted systems — all of those platforms can be covered by one configurable
// template.
type webhookChannel struct{}

func (webhookChannel) Kind() string { return KindWebhook }

// Generic webhooks have no official limit; returning 0 means no rate limiting by
// default, and users set one according to the peer's capacity.
func (webhookChannel) DefaultRatePerMin() int { return 0 }

// Mask url and headers: the target address itself often carries a token, and the
// custom headers usually hold authentication credentials; both appear in API
// responses, so both must be covered.
// The cost is that editing a single header requires re-entering the whole set of
// headers (a masked value is interpreted as "keep the original") — this trade-off
// is deliberate: better to re-enter once than to echo credentials to the browser.
func (webhookChannel) SecretKeys() []string { return []string{"url", "headers"} }

// The destination is url. Changing url requires re-declaring headers — otherwise
// the original Authorization header would be sent verbatim to the new address,
// which is exactly the main path around the masking.
func (webhookChannel) DestinationKeys() []string { return []string{"url"} }

// webhookDefaultTemplate is the fallback request body when no template is given:
// a straightforward JSON structure that covers the vast majority of self-hosted
// "receive a JSON and store it" endpoints.
const webhookDefaultTemplate = `{
  "title": {{json .Title}},
  "batch": {{.Batch}},
  "count": {{.Count}},
  "items": [
{{- range $i, $it := .Items}}
{{- if $i}},{{end}}
    {
      "finding_id": {{$it.FindingID}},
      "name": {{json $it.Name}},
      "vulnclass": {{json $it.VulnClass}},
      "severity": {{json $it.Severity}},
      "summary": {{json $it.Summary}},
      "assets": {{json $it.Assets}},
      "detail_url": {{json $it.DetailURL}}
    }
{{- end}}
  ]
}`

// webhookTemplateData is the context exposed to user templates.
type webhookTemplateData struct {
	Title   string
	Batch   bool
	Count   int
	Items   []webhookItem
	HomeURL string
	// SentAt is the delivery time of this send (RFC3339), for the receiving end
	// to record.
	SentAt string
}

type webhookItem struct {
	FindingID     int64
	Name          string
	VulnClass     string
	Severity      string
	SeverityLabel string
	Summary       string
	Assets        []string
	DetailURL     string
	FromStatus    string
	ToStatus      string
	// StatusLabel is a human-readable description of the status change, e.g.
	// "Pending → Fixed"; empty for non-status-change events.
	StatusLabel string
}

func (webhookChannel) Validate(cfg map[string]any) error {
	raw := cfgString(cfg, "url")
	if raw == "" {
		return errors.New("missing target URL")
	}
	if err := validateHTTPURL(raw); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("invalid target URL: %w", err)
	}
	if m := strings.ToUpper(cfgString(cfg, "method")); m != "" && m != http.MethodGet && m != http.MethodPost && m != http.MethodPut && m != http.MethodPatch {
		return fmt.Errorf("unsupported method %s (allowed: GET/POST/PUT/PATCH)", m)
	}
	if tpl := cfgString(cfg, "body_template"); tpl != "" {
		if _, err := parseWebhookTemplate(tpl); err != nil {
			return fmt.Errorf("body template syntax error: %w", err)
		}
	}
	return nil
}

func (c webhookChannel) Send(ctx context.Context, cfg map[string]any, m Message) (int, error) {
	if err := c.Validate(cfg); err != nil {
		return 0, Permanent(err)
	}
	method := strings.ToUpper(cfgString(cfg, "method"))
	if method == "" {
		method = http.MethodPost
	}

	// GET carries no request body: stuffing content into the query is beyond what
	// the template can express and violates GET semantics, so GET is only suitable
	// for "trigger a hook on hit" style receivers.
	var payload any
	if method != http.MethodGet {
		body, err := renderWebhookBody(cfgString(cfg, "body_template"), m)
		if err != nil {
			return 0, Permanent(err)
		}
		// The template renders JSON in string form; convert it to json.RawMessage
		// and send as-is, avoiding a second round of escaping that would wrap the
		// user's carefully built structure inside a JSON string.
		if !json.Valid([]byte(body)) {
			return 0, Permanent(errors.New("body template did not render valid JSON"))
		}
		payload = json.RawMessage(body)
	}

	headers := cfgMap(cfg, "headers")
	if ct := cfgString(cfg, "content_type"); ct != "" {
		// Allow overriding, but apply it after headers so explicit configuration
		// wins.
		if headers == nil {
			headers = map[string]string{}
		}
		headers["Content-Type"] = ct
	}
	if _, err := doJSON(ctx, method, cfgString(cfg, "url"), headers, payload); err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	// Generic webhooks do not truncate the body (the receiver is the user's own
	// service and the size is governed by body_template), so the whole batch
	// counts as delivered.
	return len(m.Items), nil
}

// renderWebhookBody renders the request body with the user template (or the
// default template).
func renderWebhookBody(tpl string, m Message) (string, error) {
	if strings.TrimSpace(tpl) == "" {
		tpl = webhookDefaultTemplate
	}
	t, err := parseWebhookTemplate(tpl)
	if err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("body template syntax error: %w", err)
	}
	var buf bytes.Buffer
	if err := t.Execute(&buf, newWebhookTemplateData(m)); err != nil {
		return "", fmt.Errorf("failed to render body template: %w", err)
	}
	return buf.String(), nil
}

// parseWebhookTemplate parses the template.
//
// missingkey=zero renders missing map keys as zero values instead of erroring —
// but the context in this file is a struct, so its main effect is keeping range
// from erroring when .Items is empty. What really needs guarding is .Items being
// nil.
func parseWebhookTemplate(tpl string) (*template.Template, error) {
	return template.New("body").Funcs(webhookTemplateFuncs).Option("missingkey=zero").Parse(tpl)
}

// webhookTemplateFuncs are the helper functions exposed to templates.
var webhookTemplateFuncs = template.FuncMap{
	// json serializes any value into JSON.
	//
	// This function is not a nice-to-have but a necessity: without it users can
	// only write {{.Title}} for direct interpolation, and a single quote or
	// newline in a vulnerability title makes the whole request body invalid
	// JSON — the receiver rejects it, and the error points at "JSON parse
	// failure" with no hint that a quote in the title caused it.
	"json": func(v any) (string, error) {
		raw, err := json.Marshal(v)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		return string(raw), nil
	},
	// jsons embeds a JSON fragment inside another JSON string value (one level of
	// string escaping).
	"jsons": func(v any) (string, error) {
		raw, err := json.Marshal(v)
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		quoted, err := json.Marshal(string(raw))
		if err != nil {
			return "", err
		}
		// Strip the outer quotes: the caller decides whether to add quotes.
		return string(quoted[1 : len(quoted)-1]), nil
	},
}

func newWebhookTemplateData(m Message) webhookTemplateData {
	d := webhookTemplateData{
		Title:   markdownTitle(m),
		Batch:   m.Batch,
		Count:   len(m.Items),
		HomeURL: m.HomeURL,
		SentAt:  time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339),
		Items:   make([]webhookItem, 0, len(m.Items)),
	}
	for _, it := range m.Items {
		wi := webhookItem{
			FindingID:     it.FindingID,
			Name:          it.Name,
			VulnClass:     it.VulnClass,
			Severity:      it.Severity,
			SeverityLabel: SeverityLabel(it.Severity),
			Summary:       it.Summary,
			Assets:        append([]string{}, it.Assets...),
			DetailURL:     it.DetailURL,
			FromStatus:    it.FromStatus,
			ToStatus:      it.ToStatus,
		}
		if it.IsStatusChange() {
			wi.StatusLabel = StatusLabel(it.FromStatus) + " → " + StatusLabel(it.ToStatus)
		}
		d.Items = append(d.Items, wi)
	}
	return d
}

FILE: notify/webhook_template_test.go

package notify

import (
	"context"
	"reflect"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"testing"
)

// This file locks down the **capability boundary** of the generic Webhook template.
//
// This is the only place in the whole package where "a user-provided string is
// evaluated as code", so we must spell out what it can and cannot do, and pin those
// properties down with tests — otherwise one day someone will casually add a method
// to the template context, or a readFile to the FuncMap, and the capability surface
// silently expands while the diff looks like a harmless little function.

// TestTemplateContextHasNoMethods is the most important one.
//
// text/template invokes exported methods ({{.Foo}} can read a field or call a
// method). So as long as the template context can reach **any** type with exported
// methods, those methods are effectively exposed to template authors.
// This feature's context is deliberately pure data (exported fields only, zero
// methods).
//
// If this test fails: someone added a method to webhookTemplateData / webhookItem.
// Before deciding to allow it, think carefully about whether that method could be
// used by a template to read things that should not be exposed.
func TestTemplateContextHasNoMethods(t *testing.T) {
	for _, v := range []any{webhookTemplateData{}, webhookItem{}} {
		typ := reflect.TypeOf(v)
		if n := typ.NumMethod(); n != 0 {
			var names []string
			for i := 0; i < n; i++ {
				names = append(names, typ.Method(i).Name)
			}
			t.Fatalf("%s exposes %d methods (%s): text/template can call them, "+
				"which hands those methods' capabilities to template authors", typ.Name(), n, strings.Join(names, ", "))
		}
	}
}

// TestTemplateFuncsAreMinimal locks down the set of functions exposed to templates.
//
// Every extra function in the FuncMap is one more capability. Currently there are
// only json / jsons, whose job is to serialize a value into a JSON fragment — they
// cannot read files, make requests, or execute commands.
func TestTemplateFuncsAreMinimal(t *testing.T) {
	var got []string
	for name := range webhookTemplateFuncs {
		got = append(got, name)
	}
	sort.Strings(got)
	want := []string{"json", "jsons"}
	if !reflect.DeepEqual(got, want) {
		t.Fatalf("template function set changed: got %v, want %v. Before adding a function, confirm it does not expand the capability surface "+
			"(no file reads/writes, no network requests, no command execution)", got, want)
	}
}

// TestTemplateCannotReachUnknownData covers out-of-bounds access in templates:
// accessing something that does not exist must fail, not echo something back;
// and the failure message must not carry internal data out.
func TestTemplateCannotReachUnknownData(t *testing.T) {
	_, err := renderWebhookBody(`{"x": {{.Environment}}, "y": {{.Env}}}`, singleMsg())
	if err == nil {
		t.Fatal("accessing a non-existent field should error")
	}
	// The error must not contain real content from the template context (vulnerability title/summary).
	for _, leak := range []string{"SQL injection", "param id"} {
		if strings.Contains(err.Error(), leak) {
			t.Errorf("template error leaked message content %q: %v", leak, err)
		}
	}
}

// TestTemplateRenderFailsPermanently: a broken template is a configuration error; retries will not fix it.
// If it were classified as retryable, one bad template would make every delivery waste three rounds of backoff.
func TestTemplateRenderFailsPermanently(t *testing.T) {
	cfg := map[string]any{
		"url":           "https://example.com/hook",
		"body_template": `{{.Items.`,
	}
	if err := (webhookChannel{}).Validate(cfg); err == nil {
		t.Fatal("template syntax errors should be caught at save time")
	}
	// Even if validation is bypassed and delivery is attempted directly, it must be judged a permanent failure rather than retried over and over.
	_, err := (webhookChannel{}).Send(context.Background(), cfg, singleMsg())
	if err == nil || !IsPermanent(err) {
		t.Fatalf("a bad template should be a permanent failure, got %v", err)
	}
}

// TestTemplateCanOnlyProduceJSON covers the constraint that "the template render result must be valid JSON".
// It also blocks uses like "using the template to generate plain text to trigger other protocols".
func TestTemplateCanOnlyProduceJSON(t *testing.T) {
	// A valid template passes.
	ok := map[string]any{"url": "https://example.com/hook", "body_template": `{"t":{{json .Title}}}`}
	if err := (webhookChannel{}).Validate(ok); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("a valid template should pass validation: %v", err)
	}
	// When the render result is not JSON it must be rejected (rather than sent out as-is).
	bad := map[string]any{"url": "http://127.0.0.1:1/hook", "body_template": `not json {{.Count}}`}
	_, err := (webhookChannel{}).Send(context.Background(), bad, singleMsg())
	if err == nil || !IsPermanent(err) {
		t.Fatalf("rendering non-JSON should be a permanent failure, got %v", err)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(err.Error(), "valid JSON") {
		t.Errorf("the error message should indicate a JSON problem, got %v", err)
	}
}

package notify

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

// weComMarkdownLimit is the hard limit (bytes, not characters) for WeCom group bot markdown content.
// It is the tightest limit of all six channels and the main reason TruncateBytes exists.
const weComMarkdownLimit = 4096

// weComChannel implements the WeCom (WeChat Work) group bot.
//
// Platform traits:
//   - Authenticates only via the key on the URL; signing is not supported — so the
//     webhook address itself is the entire credential.
//   - markdown content is capped at 4096 **bytes**; anything longer is rejected
//     outright (not truncated). At 3 bytes per Chinese character, the body has only
//     a thousand-odd characters of room, so client-side truncation is mandatory.
//   - Rate limit is 20 messages/minute, likewise held up by client-side rate limiting.
type weComChannel struct{}

func (weComChannel) Kind() string { return KindWeCom }

func (weComChannel) DefaultRatePerMin() int { return 20 }

// WeCom has only one credential, the Webhook (the key on the URL), and it does not
// support signing — the whole address is the entire credential, with no other fields to mask.
func (weComChannel) SecretKeys() []string { return []string{"webhook"} }

// WeCom has only the Webhook field; it is both the destination and the credential, so there is no "leftover credential after changing the address" to speak of.
func (weComChannel) DestinationKeys() []string { return []string{"webhook"} }

func (weComChannel) Validate(cfg map[string]any) error {
	hook := cfgString(cfg, "webhook")
	if hook == "" {
		return errors.New("missing Webhook address")
	}
	if err := validateHTTPURL(hook); err != nil {
		return fmt.Errorf("invalid Webhook address: %w", err)
	}
	return nil
}

func (c weComChannel) Send(ctx context.Context, cfg map[string]any, m Message) (int, error) {
	if err := c.Validate(cfg); err != nil {
		return 0, Permanent(err)
	}
	// A digest batch can be very long (50 items x one line each + prefix); 4096 bytes is easy to exceed.
	// Truncate here instead of relying on the platform's error: rejection means the whole batch is lost, while truncation at least delivers the first few items.
	content, kept := markdownBody(m, weComMarkdownLimit)
	payload := map[string]any{
		"msgtype":  "markdown",
		"markdown": map[string]any{"content": content},
	}
	raw, err := doJSON(ctx, "POST", cfgString(cfg, "webhook"), nil, payload)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, err
	}
	var res struct {
		ErrCode int    `json:"errcode"`
		ErrMsg  string `json:"errmsg"`
	}
	if err := json.Unmarshal(raw, &res); err != nil {
		return 0, fmt.Errorf("failed to parse WeCom response: %w (%s)", err, snippet(raw))
	}
	if res.ErrCode != 0 {
		// 45009 means the API call rate limit was exceeded — the platform's rate window rolls,
		// so retrying after backoff works, and we explicitly classify it as retryable.
		// Reaching this point means the client rate_per_min is configured too aggressively;
		// the retry is only a fallback — the real fix is to lower the channel's rate limit.
		if res.ErrCode == 45009 {
			return 0, fmt.Errorf("WeCom rate limited %d: %s", res.ErrCode, res.ErrMsg)
		}
		// 93000 means the webhook key is invalid — a permanent failure that retries will not fix.
		return 0, Permanent(fmt.Errorf("WeCom returned error %d: %s", res.ErrCode, res.ErrMsg))
	}
	return kept, nil
}

package report

import (
	"bytes"
	"encoding/csv"
	"fmt"
	"path"
	"regexp"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// Rendering for the findings page "Export": renders a batch of findings table rows
// into a summary Markdown, a single-finding Markdown, or CSV. JSON is serialized
// directly from DTOs at the server layer, not here.

// sortFindingsForExport sorts by severity descending, then by time descending, consistent with the summary report's grouping.
func sortFindingsForExport(fs []*db.DBFinding) {
	sort.SliceStable(fs, func(i, j int) bool {
		ri, rj := sevRank[fs[i].Severity], sevRank[fs[j].Severity]
		if ri != rj {
			return ri < rj // smaller sevRank means more severe
		}
		return fs[i].CreatedAt.After(fs[j].CreatedAt)
	})
}

// findingTitle returns the vulnerability's readable title: name → class → "Uncategorized".
func findingTitle(f *db.DBFinding) string {
	return nz(f.Name, nz(f.VulnClass, "Uncategorized"))
}

// FindingsMarkdown combines a batch of findings into a summary report (summary + grouped by severity,
// each entry with class/status/owning task/evidence/detailed report).
func FindingsMarkdown(fs []*db.DBFinding, generatedAt time.Time) string {
	items := append([]*db.DBFinding(nil), fs...)
	sortFindingsForExport(items)

	var b strings.Builder
	b.WriteString("# Vulnerability Findings Summary Report\n\n")
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Generated at**: %s\n", generatedAt.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"))
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Total findings**: %d\n\n", len(items))

	// Summary: counts per severity.
	counts := map[string]int{}
	for _, f := range items {
		counts[f.Severity]++
	}
	b.WriteString("## Summary\n\n")
	b.WriteString("| Severity | Count |\n| --- | --- |\n")
	for _, s := range []struct{ key, label string }{
		{"critical", "Critical"}, {"high", "High"}, {"medium", "Medium"}, {"low", "Low"},
	} {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "| %s | %d |\n", s.label, counts[s.key])
	}
	b.WriteString("\n")

	if len(items) == 0 {
		b.WriteString("_No matching vulnerabilities._\n")
		return b.String()
	}

	b.WriteString("## Vulnerability Details\n\n")
	for i, f := range items {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "### %d. [%s] %s\n\n", i+1, strings.ToUpper(nz(f.Severity, "info")), findingTitle(f))
		if f.VulnClass != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Class**: %s\n", f.VulnClass)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Status**: %s\n", nz(f.Status, "pending"))
		if desc := strings.TrimSpace(f.TaskDescription); desc != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Task**: %s\n", desc)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Found at**: %s\n\n", f.CreatedAt.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"))
		if s := strings.TrimSpace(f.Summary); s != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s\n\n", s)
		}
		if e := strings.TrimSpace(f.Evidence); e != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "**Evidence:**\n\n```\n%s\n```\n\n", e)
		}
		if rep := strings.TrimSpace(f.Report); rep != "" {
			b.WriteString("**Detailed report:**\n\n")
			b.WriteString(rep)
			b.WriteString("\n\n")
		}
		b.WriteString(findingTrafficMarkdown(f, false))
		b.WriteString("---\n\n")
	}
	return b.String()
}

// SingleFindingMarkdown renders a single vulnerability as a standalone Markdown (used for "one file per vulnerability" packaging).
func SingleFindingMarkdown(f *db.DBFinding, generatedAt time.Time) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# [%s] %s\n\n", strings.ToUpper(nz(f.Severity, "info")), findingTitle(f))
	if f.VulnClass != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Class**: %s\n", f.VulnClass)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Severity**: %s\n", nz(f.Severity, "info"))
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Status**: %s\n", nz(f.Status, "pending"))
	if desc := strings.TrimSpace(f.TaskDescription); desc != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Task**: %s\n", desc)
	}
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Found at**: %s\n", f.CreatedAt.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"))
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Generated at**: %s\n\n", generatedAt.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"))
	if s := strings.TrimSpace(f.Summary); s != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## Summary\n\n%s\n\n", s)
	}
	if e := strings.TrimSpace(f.Evidence); e != "" {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## Evidence\n\n```\n%s\n```\n\n", e)
	}
	if rep := strings.TrimSpace(f.Report); rep != "" {
		b.WriteString("## Detailed Report\n\n")
		b.WriteString(rep)
		b.WriteString("\n")
	}
	b.WriteString(findingTrafficMarkdown(f, true))
	return b.String()
}

var unsafeFilenameChars = regexp.MustCompile(`[^\p{Han}\p{L}\p{N}._-]+`)

// FindingFilename generates a safe .md filename for "one file per vulnerability", e.g.
// `critical_SQL_injection_#123.md`. Strips path separators and control characters to avoid illegal paths inside the zip.
func FindingFilename(f *db.DBFinding) string {
	sev := nz(f.Severity, "info")
	title := findingTitle(f)
	name := fmt.Sprintf("%s_%s_#%d", sev, title, f.ID)
	name = unsafeFilenameChars.ReplaceAllString(name, "_")
	name = strings.Trim(name, "._")
	if name == "" {
		name = fmt.Sprintf("finding_%d", f.ID)
	}
	// Defensive: strip one more path layer to rule out zip slip.
	name = path.Base(name)
	if len(name) > 120 {
		name = name[:120]
	}
	return name + ".md"
}

// FindingsCSV renders a batch of findings as CSV (with a UTF-8 BOM so Excel detects the encoding correctly).
// It omits the long report/evidence full text and keeps only summary-level fields; use Markdown/JSON export for full text.
func FindingsCSV(fs []*db.DBFinding) []byte {
	items := append([]*db.DBFinding(nil), fs...)
	sortFindingsForExport(items)

	var buf bytes.Buffer
	buf.WriteString("\xEF\xBB\xBF") // UTF-8 BOM
	w := csv.NewWriter(&buf)
	_ = w.Write([]string{"ID", "Name", "Class", "Severity", "Status", "Task", "Found At", "Summary", "Traffic Evidence Count", "Traffic Evidence IDs"})
	for _, f := range items {
		_ = w.Write([]string{
			fmt.Sprintf("%d", f.ID),
			findingTitle(f),
			f.VulnClass,
			nz(f.Severity, "info"),
			nz(f.Status, "pending"),
			f.TaskDescription,
			f.CreatedAt.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"),
			strings.TrimSpace(f.Summary),
			fmt.Sprint(len(f.TrafficBindings)), findingTrafficIDs(f),
		})
	}
	w.Flush()
	return buf.Bytes()
}

func findingTrafficIDs(f *db.DBFinding) string {
	ids := make([]string, 0, len(f.TrafficBindings))
	for _, b := range f.TrafficBindings {
		ids = append(ids, fmt.Sprint(b.ID))
	}
	return strings.Join(ids, ",")
}

func findingTrafficMarkdown(f *db.DBFinding, attachments bool) string {
	stale := f.Report != "" && f.EvidenceVersion != f.ReportEvidenceVersion
	if len(f.TrafficBindings) == 0 && !stale {
		return ""
	}
	var out strings.Builder
	out.WriteString("\n## Related Traffic Evidence\n\n")
	fmt.Fprintf(&out, "Evidence version: %d; bindings: %d.\n\n", f.EvidenceVersion, len(f.TrafficBindings))
	if stale {
		out.WriteString("The evidence has changed; the detailed report needs updating.\n\n")
	}
	for i, b := range f.TrafficBindings {
		fmt.Fprintf(&out, "%d. **Evidence #%d · %s** — `%s %s`, status %d\n", i+1, b.ID, b.Role, b.Snapshot.Method, strings.ReplaceAll(b.Snapshot.URL, "`", "%60"), b.Snapshot.Status)
		if b.Note != "" {
			fmt.Fprintf(&out, "   %s\n", strings.ReplaceAll(b.Note, "\n", "\n   "))
		}
		if attachments {
			fmt.Fprintf(&out, "   [Request message](evidence/%d/%d/request.http) · [Response message](evidence/%d/%d/response.http)\n", f.ID, b.ID, f.ID, b.ID)
		}
	}
	out.WriteString("\n")
	return out.String()
}

=====================================================================
FILE: report/report.go
=====================================================================
// Package report renders a deliverable Markdown report from the exploration
// graph: confirmed findings (with severity/evidence) (docs §15 P5).
package report

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"sort"
	"strings"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// Input bundles what the report needs.
type Input struct {
	Title       string
	Goal        string
	GeneratedAt time.Time
	AssetCounts map[string]int
	Findings    []*db.Node
	Coverage    *db.CoverageLedger // nil when the task's coverage feature is off
}

// reportMaxGaps caps the coverage gap list of the report; the rest is counted.
const reportMaxGaps = 200

type findingView struct {
	VulnClass string
	Name      string
	Severity  string
	Summary   string
	PoC       string
}

func parseFinding(n *db.Node) findingView {
	var p struct {
		VulnClass string `json:"vulnclass"`
		Name      string `json:"name"`
		Severity  string `json:"severity"`
		Summary   string `json:"summary"`
		Evidence  struct {
			PoC string `json:"poc"`
		} `json:"evidence"`
	}
	_ = json.Unmarshal(n.Payload, &p)
	return findingView{p.VulnClass, p.Name, p.Severity, p.Summary, p.Evidence.PoC}
}

var sevRank = map[string]int{"critical": 0, "high": 1, "medium": 2, "low": 3, "": 4}

// Markdown renders the report.
func Markdown(in Input) string {
	var b strings.Builder
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "# Penetration Test Report — %s\n\n", nz(in.Title, "Unnamed task"))
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Task goal**: %s\n", nz(in.Goal, "(unspecified)"))
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Generated at**: %s\n\n", in.GeneratedAt.Format("2006-01-02 15:04:05"))

	// summary
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## Summary\n\n")
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Confirmed findings: **%d**\n", len(in.Findings))
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Assets: ")
	var types []string
	for t := range in.AssetCounts {
		types = append(types, t)
	}
	sort.Strings(types)
	for i, t := range types {
		if i > 0 {
			b.WriteString(", ")
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s %d", t, in.AssetCounts[t])
	}
	b.WriteString("\n\n")

	// findings
	fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## Findings\n\n")
	if len(in.Findings) == 0 {
		b.WriteString("_No vulnerabilities confirmed this time._\n\n")
	} else {
		fs := make([]findingView, 0, len(in.Findings))
		for _, n := range in.Findings {
			fs = append(fs, parseFinding(n))
		}
		sort.SliceStable(fs, func(i, j int) bool { return sevRank[fs[i].Severity] < sevRank[fs[j].Severity] })
		for i, f := range fs {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "### %d. [%s] %s\n\n", i+1, strings.ToUpper(nz(f.Severity, "info")), nz(f.Name, nz(f.VulnClass, "Uncategorized")))
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "%s\n\n", nz(f.Summary, ""))
			if f.PoC != "" {
				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "**PoC / Evidence:**\n\n```\n%s\n```\n\n", f.PoC)
			}
		}
	}

	if c := in.Coverage; c != nil {
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "## Coverage gaps\n\n")
		if c.Completeness != nil {
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- **Completeness**: %s. %s\n", c.Completeness.State, c.Completeness.Caveat)
		}
		fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- Ledger entries: %d, open gaps: %d\n", len(c.Entries), len(c.Gaps))
		for i, g := range c.Gaps {
			if i == reportMaxGaps {
				fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- and %d more (see the coverage API)\n", len(c.Gaps)-reportMaxGaps)
				break
			}
			fmt.Fprintf(&b, "- %s\n", g)
		}
		b.WriteString("\n")
	}

	return b.String()
}

func nz(s, d string) string {
	if strings.TrimSpace(s) == "" {
		return d
	}
	return s
}

=====================================================================
FILE: report/report_test.go

package report

import (
	"strings"
	"testing"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
)

// The exported report carries the coverage gaps and the completeness caveat;
// nothing is added when the task's coverage feature is off (nil ledger).
func TestMarkdownCoverageGaps(t *testing.T) {
	l := db.BuildCoverageLedger([]db.CoverageEntry{{Surface: "/a", RiskArea: "xss", Outcome: db.OutcomeNeedsFollowUp}},
		[]string{"sqli"}, db.CoverageCompletenessFor("timeout", false, false, true))
	cases := []struct {
		name string
		l    *db.CoverageLedger
		want []string
	}{
		{"ledger", l, []string{"## Coverage gaps", "timeout", "Incomplete scan", "open gaps: 2", "- unrecorded_risk_class sqli", "- needs_follow_up /a xss"}},
		{"coverage off", nil, nil},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		md := Markdown(Input{Title: "t", Coverage: c.l})
		if c.want == nil && strings.Contains(md, "Coverage gaps") {
			t.Fatalf("%s: unexpected coverage section", c.name)
		}
		for _, w := range c.want {
			if !strings.Contains(md, w) {
				t.Errorf("%s: missing %q in\n%s", c.name, w, md)
			}
		}
	}
}

// The report lists at most reportMaxGaps gaps, then a count line.
func TestMarkdownCoverageGapsCap(t *testing.T) {
	var entries []db.CoverageEntry
	for i := 0; i < reportMaxGaps+30; i++ {
		entries = append(entries, db.CoverageEntry{Surface: "/p", RiskArea: "xss", Outcome: db.OutcomeNeedsFollowUp})
	}
	md := Markdown(Input{Title: "t", Coverage: db.BuildCoverageLedger(entries, nil, db.CoverageCompleteness{})})
	if n := strings.Count(md, "\n- needs_follow_up /p xss"); n != reportMaxGaps {
		t.Fatalf("listed %d gaps, want %d", n, reportMaxGaps)
	}
	if !strings.Contains(md, "- and 30 more (see the coverage API)") {
		t.Fatalf("missing count line in\n%s", md)
	}
}

FILE: reset-password.sh

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# =============================================================================
# HIVE admin password reset script
#
# The login username is fixed as HIVE; the password is stored as a bcrypt hash in
# the auth.password_hash key of the settings table. This script uses pgcrypto to
# generate the bcrypt hash in-database — compatible with the backend (x/crypto/bcrypt).
#
# Two deployments:
#   local (default) — host connects to the database directly with psql. Connection
#                    info priority: args > --dsn/$HIVE_PG_DSN > config.json database.*
#   docker          — runs psql inside the postgres container via `docker compose
#                    exec` (or `docker exec`) (compose does not expose 5432 by default).
#
# Usage examples:
#   ./reset-password.sh                          # local, auto-reads config.json/env, prompts for the new password
#   ./reset-password.sh -p 'New-Passphrase!'     # local, new password given directly (at least 12 characters)
#   ./reset-password.sh --dsn postgres://u:p@h:5432/hive
#   ./reset-password.sh -H 127.0.0.1 -P 5433 -U autopentest -W pass -d hive
#   ./reset-password.sh -m docker                # docker deployment (reads POSTGRES_* from .env)
#   ./reset-password.sh -m docker -c pg-container-name --exec docker
#
# Security: new password via env var + psql \getenv (never in argv), auto-escaped
# with :'var' (anti-SQL-injection); DB password via PGPASSWORD, also not in argv.
# =============================================================================
set -euo pipefail

PASS_KEY="auth.password_hash"
BCRYPT_COST=10

MODE=""            # local | docker (empty = auto-detect)
DSN=""
HOST="" PORT="" USER="" DBPASS="" DBNAME="" SSLMODE=""
CONFIG=""
CONTAINER=""       # postgres service/container name in docker mode (default postgres)
EXEC_KIND=""       # compose | docker (which exec to use in docker mode; empty = auto)
NEWPASS=""
ASSUME_YES=0

die() { echo "error: $*" >&2; exit 1; }
info() { echo "· $*" >&2; }

usage() { sed -n '2,40p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \{0,1\}//'; exit 0; }

# ---- Argument parsing -------------------------------------------------------
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    -m|--mode)        MODE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --dsn)            DSN="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    -H|--host)        HOST="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    -P|--port)        PORT="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    -U|--user)        USER="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    -W|--db-password) DBPASS="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    -d|--dbname)      DBNAME="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --sslmode)        SSLMODE="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --config)         CONFIG="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    -c|--container)   CONTAINER="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    --exec)           EXEC_KIND="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    -p|--new-password) NEWPASS="${2:-}"; shift 2 ;;
    -y|--yes)         ASSUME_YES=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help)        usage ;;
    *) die "unknown argument: $1 (see -h for usage)" ;;
  esac
done

# ---- Read database.* from config.json (local mode only, and only when no explicit connection is given) -----
# Prefer python3 for parsing (robust); fall back to grep when python3 is missing (config.json is a flat per-key file).
read_config_json() {
  local path="$1"
  [[ -f "$path" ]] || return 1
  if command -v python3 >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    python3 - "$path" <<'PY'
import json, sys
try:
    d = json.load(open(sys.argv[1])).get("database", {})
except Exception:
    sys.exit(1)
# Supports a direct dsn, or individual fields
if d.get("dsn"):
    print("DSN\t" + d["dsn"]); sys.exit(0)
for k in ("host","port","user","password","dbname","sslmode"):
    if d.get(k) is not None:
        print(k.upper() + "\t" + str(d[k]))
PY
  else
    # Minimal fallback: grep key by key (values are strings or numbers)
    local k
    for k in host port user password dbname sslmode; do
      local v
      v=$(grep -oE "\"$k\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*(\"[^\"]*\"|[0-9]+)" "$path" 2>/dev/null \
            | head -1 | sed -E "s/.*:[[:space:]]*//; s/^\"//; s/\"$//") || true
      [[ -n "$v" ]] && echo -e "${k^^}\t$v"
    done
  fi
}

apply_config_fields() {
  local key val
  while IFS=$'\t' read -r key val; do
    [[ -z "$key" ]] && continue
    case "$key" in
      DSN)      [[ -z "$DSN" ]] && DSN="$val" ;;
      HOST)     [[ -z "$HOST" ]] && HOST="$val" ;;
      PORT)     [[ -z "$PORT" ]] && PORT="$val" ;;
      USER)     [[ -z "$USER" ]] && USER="$val" ;;
      PASSWORD) [[ -z "$DBPASS" ]] && DBPASS="$val" ;;
      DBNAME)   [[ -z "$DBNAME" ]] && DBNAME="$val" ;;
      SSLMODE)  [[ -z "$SSLMODE" ]] && SSLMODE="$val" ;;
    esac
  done
}

# ---- Auto-detect mode ---------------------------------------------------------
if [[ -z "$MODE" ]]; then
  if [[ -n "$DSN$HOST$USER$DBNAME" || -n "${HIVE_PG_DSN:-}" || -f "${CONFIG:-config.json}" ]]; then
    MODE="local"
  elif command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f docker-compose.yml ]]; then
    MODE="docker"
  else
    MODE="local"
  fi
fi
info "deployment mode: $MODE"

# ---- Collect the new password -------------------------------------------------
if [[ -z "$NEWPASS" ]]; then
  read -r -s -p "Enter new password (username is fixed as HIVE): " NEWPASS; echo >&2
  [[ -n "$NEWPASS" ]] || die "password cannot be empty"
  read -r -s -p "Enter again to confirm: " NEWPASS2; echo >&2
  [[ "$NEWPASS" == "$NEWPASS2" ]] || die "the two entries do not match"
fi
[[ -n "$NEWPASS" ]] || die "password cannot be empty"
# Same minimum as the server (minPasswordRunes in server/auth.go), counted in
# characters like the server: UTF-8 bytes minus continuation bytes, whatever the locale.
NEWPASS_CHARS=$(printf '%s' "$NEWPASS" | LC_ALL=C tr -d '\200-\277' | wc -c)
(( NEWPASS_CHARS >= 12 )) || die "password must be at least 12 characters"

# Hand the password to psql via environment variable (read with \getenv, never in argv/ps)
export HIVE_RESET_NEWPASS="$NEWPASS"

# Generate bcrypt in-database and upsert; the password is auto-escaped with :'newpw'. CREATE EXTENSION is idempotent;
# if the database role lacks permission to create extensions it errors here (see the hint in the run failure branch below).
SQL=$(cat <<SQL
\\set ON_ERROR_STOP on
\\getenv newpw HIVE_RESET_NEWPASS
CREATE EXTENSION IF NOT EXISTS pgcrypto;
INSERT INTO settings(key, value)
VALUES ('$PASS_KEY', crypt(:'newpw', gen_salt('bf', $BCRYPT_COST)))
ON CONFLICT (key) DO UPDATE SET value = EXCLUDED.value, updated_at = now();
SQL
)

# ---- Execute ------------------------------------------------------------------
if [[ "$MODE" == "local" ]]; then
  # Connection info priority: command line > --dsn/$HIVE_PG_DSN > config.json
  if [[ -z "$DSN" && -z "$HOST$USER$DBNAME" ]]; then
    [[ -n "${HIVE_PG_DSN:-}" ]] && DSN="$HIVE_PG_DSN"
  fi
  if [[ -z "$DSN" && -z "$HOST$USER$DBNAME" ]]; then
    cfg="${CONFIG:-config.json}"
    if [[ -f "$cfg" ]]; then
      info "reading database config from $cfg"
      apply_config_fields < <(read_config_json "$cfg")
    fi
  fi

  command -v psql >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "psql not found on this machine (install postgresql-client, or use -m docker instead)"

  declare -a PSQL_ARGS=()
  if [[ -n "$DSN" ]]; then
    PSQL_ARGS=("$DSN")
    target="$DSN"
  else
    [[ -n "$USER"   ]] || die "missing database user (-U) or a valid config.json/DSN"
    [[ -n "$DBNAME" ]] || die "missing database name (-d) or a valid config.json/DSN"
    HOST="${HOST:-127.0.0.1}"; PORT="${PORT:-5432}"; SSLMODE="${SSLMODE:-disable}"
    PSQL_ARGS=(-h "$HOST" -p "$PORT" -U "$USER" -d "$DBNAME")
    [[ -n "$SSLMODE" ]] && export PGSSLMODE="$SSLMODE"
    [[ -n "$DBPASS" ]] && export PGPASSWORD="$DBPASS"
    target="$USER@$HOST:$PORT/$DBNAME"
  fi

  info "target database: $target"
  if [[ "$ASSUME_YES" -ne 1 ]]; then
    read -r -p "Reset the HIVE password in this database? [y/N] " ans
    [[ "$ans" == "y" || "$ans" == "Y" ]] || die "cancelled"
  fi

  if ! printf '%s\n' "$SQL" | psql "${PSQL_ARGS[@]}" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q >/dev/null; then
    die "write failed. If it reports a pgcrypto permission/missing error, use a role allowed to create extensions, or run CREATE EXTENSION pgcrypto manually first."
  fi

else
  # ---- docker ----
  command -v docker >/dev/null 2>&1 || die "docker not found"
  CONTAINER="${CONTAINER:-postgres}"

  # Choose the exec method: prefer docker compose exec (service name), otherwise docker exec (container name)
  if [[ -z "$EXEC_KIND" ]]; then
    if docker compose version >/dev/null 2>&1 && [[ -f docker-compose.yml ]]; then
      EXEC_KIND="compose"
    else
      EXEC_KIND="docker"
    fi
  fi

  # psql credentials inside the container: command line first, then POSTGRES_* from .env, then compose defaults (hive)
  if [[ -f .env ]]; then
    # shellcheck disable=SC1091
    set -a; . ./.env; set +a
  fi
  DUSER="${USER:-${POSTGRES_USER:-hive}}"
  DNAME="${DBNAME:-${POSTGRES_DB:-hive}}"
  [[ -n "$DBPASS" ]] && export PGPASSWORD="$DBPASS"
  [[ -z "${PGPASSWORD:-}" && -n "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-}" ]] && export PGPASSWORD="$POSTGRES_PASSWORD"

  info "target: psql -U $DUSER -d $DNAME inside container $CONTAINER (exec=$EXEC_KIND)"
  if [[ "$ASSUME_YES" -ne 1 ]]; then
    read -r -p "Reset the HIVE password in this container database? [y/N] " ans
    [[ "$ans" == "y" || "$ans" == "Y" ]] || die "cancelled"
  fi

  # -e with a name only (no value) → inherited from the current environment, so the password never appears in the docker command argv.
  declare -a EXEC_CMD
  if [[ "$EXEC_KIND" == "compose" ]]; then
    EXEC_CMD=(docker compose exec -T -e HIVE_RESET_NEWPASS -e PGPASSWORD "$CONTAINER"
              psql -U "$DUSER" -d "$DNAME" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q)
  else
    EXEC_CMD=(docker exec -i -e HIVE_RESET_NEWPASS -e PGPASSWORD "$CONTAINER"
              psql -U "$DUSER" -d "$DNAME" -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -q)
  fi

  if ! printf '%s\n' "$SQL" | "${EXEC_CMD[@]}" >/dev/null; then
    die "write failed. Check the container name (-c), the database account (POSTGRES_* in .env), and that the role has pgcrypto permission."
  fi
fi

unset HIVE_RESET_NEWPASS
echo "✓ HIVE admin password has been reset. Log in with username HIVE + the new password (no service restart needed)."

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Backup the HIVE database (and optionally the data directory) with rotation.
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/backup.sh [--with-data] [--keep N] [--output-dir DIR]
#
#   --with-data    also archive the bind-mounted data/ directory (worker
#                  artifacts, evidence, skills state) as a tar.gz
#   --keep N       number of db dumps to keep (default 14; data archives rotate
#                  to the same count)
#   --output-dir   where to write (default backups/, relative to the repo root)
#
# The database dump runs inside the postgres compose service, so no psql client
# is needed on the host. Restore:
#   gunzip -c backups/hive-db-<ts>.sql.gz | docker compose exec -T postgres \
#     psql -U "$POSTGRES_USER" -d "$POSTGRES_DB"
set -euo pipefail
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."

usage() { sed -n '2,15p' "$0" | sed 's/^# \?//'; }

KEEP=14
OUTPUT_DIR="backups"
WITH_DATA=0
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --keep) KEEP="${2:?}"; shift 2 ;;
    --output-dir) OUTPUT_DIR="${2:?}"; shift 2 ;;
    --with-data) WITH_DATA=1; shift ;;
    -h|--help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown option: $1" >&2; usage >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
# 0* rejects 0, which would make prune delete the dump this run just wrote, and
# leading zeros, which $((KEEP + 1)) would read as octal.
case "$KEEP" in (*[!0-9]*|''|0*) echo "--keep must be a positive integer" >&2; exit 2 ;; esac

# Compose reads .env for credentials; source it for the dump command too.
if [ -f .env ]; then
  set -a
  # shellcheck disable=SC1091
  . ./.env
  set +a
fi
PGUSER_NAME="${POSTGRES_USER:-hive}"
PGDATABASE_NAME="${POSTGRES_DB:-hive}"

mkdir -p "$OUTPUT_DIR"
TS=$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)
DB_OUT="$OUTPUT_DIR/hive-db-$TS.sql.gz"
if [ -e "$DB_OUT" ]; then
  echo "refusing to overwrite $DB_OUT" >&2
  exit 1
fi

if ! docker compose exec -T postgres pg_dump -U "$PGUSER_NAME" "$PGDATABASE_NAME" | gzip > "$DB_OUT"; then
  rm -f "$DB_OUT"
  echo "pg_dump failed (is the stack running?)" >&2
  exit 1
fi
gzip -t "$DB_OUT"
echo "wrote $DB_OUT ($(du -h "$DB_OUT" | cut -f1))"

if [ "$WITH_DATA" -eq 1 ]; then
  DATA_OUT="$OUTPUT_DIR/hive-data-$TS.tar.gz"
  # data/ contains files written by the container (root); unreadable ones make
  # tar exit 2. Fail loudly rather than ship a partial archive.
  if ! tar -czf "$DATA_OUT" data 2>"$OUTPUT_DIR/.tar.err"; then
    rm -f "$DATA_OUT"
    echo "data archive failed (run as root so container-written files are readable):" >&2
    head -5 "$OUTPUT_DIR/.tar.err" >&2
    rm -f "$OUTPUT_DIR/.tar.err"
    exit 1
  fi
  rm -f "$OUTPUT_DIR/.tar.err"
  echo "wrote $DATA_OUT ($(du -h "$DATA_OUT" | cut -f1))"
fi

prune() {
  ls -1t "$OUTPUT_DIR"/$1 2>/dev/null | tail -n +$((KEEP + 1)) | while IFS= read -r old; do
    echo "pruning $old"
    rm -f "$old"
  done
}
prune 'hive-db-*.sql.gz'
[ "$WITH_DATA" -eq 1 ] && prune 'hive-data-*.tar.gz'
echo "backup complete ($KEEP newest kept)"

FILE: scripts/benchmark/README.md
=====================================================================
# HIVE L3 benchmark

Measures whether the product can find and prove real vulnerabilities in a real
application, unprompted, against an executable oracle. That is the "operation"
level most model benchmarks do not reach: recognition benchmarks hand the model
a snippet and ask a question, while this harness hands HIVE a running app and
reads what it reports.

Method discipline adapted from capability-matrix (MIT) and VulnHunter's
benchmark harness (Apache-2.0).

## Layout

| | |
|---|---|
| `run_bench.py` | The runner: deploy corpus, create task, wait, fetch findings, judge, tally |
| `ground_truth/<corpus>.json` | Version-stamped ground truth (component + class + mechanism, deliberately coarse) |
| `benchmark-results/` | Output (gitignored): one directory per run with `report.md` + `results.json` |

## Scoring

Every ground-truth entry is matched against the scanner's findings by an
independent LLM judge, then graded on four gates (partial answers earn partial
credit):

| Gate | Test | Points |
|---|---|---|
| component | names the right endpoint or feature | 1 |
| class | acceptable vulnerability class | 2 |
| keywords | at least two mechanism-specific terms | 1 |
| proof | PoC describes a route that would actually work | 1 |

Standing rules, enforced by the runner:

1. **Multi-gate scoring, never pass/fail.** The gate pattern is the work item;
   the aggregate percentage is the least useful output.
2. **Discovery candidates.** A scanner finding beyond ground truth is not a
   false positive until verified; precision is reported as bounds meanwhile.
3. **The judge must not be the model under test.** The runner refuses to start
   when `--judge-model` equals `--subject-model` (override knowingly with
   `--allow-self-judge`).
4. **The judge must pass a falsification battery** before grading: a correct
   match, a wrong-bug match, and a vague non-answer. A grader that cannot fail
   the wrong ones does not run.
5. **Invalid never counts.** Findings with no summary and no report are
   excluded from every rate and named in the result.
6. **Every rate carries its denominator; the aggregate carries a Wilson 95%
   interval.** With 8 ground-truth entries, one run cannot separate close
   models; treat per-gate rates as observations and replicate before quoting
   differences.
7. **Results are stamped** with the method version, ground-truth version,
   subject model, judge model, and terminal task status. A result measured
   under an earlier version is not wrong; it is a result at that version.

## Usage

```bash
cd scripts/benchmark

# against a locally deployed HIVE, with an independent judge endpoint
HIVE_TOKEN=<jwt or mint via HIVE_JWT_KEY=/app/keys/jwt.key copy> \
JUDGE_BASE_URL=https://api.example.com JUDGE_MODEL=<other-model> JUDGE_API_KEY=... \
python3 run_bench.py --corpus juice-shop --subject-model glm-5.3
```

Environment contract:

| Variable / flag | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `HIVE_BASE` / `--hive-url` | HIVE base URL (default `http://localhost:8787`) |
| `HIVE_TOKEN` or `HIVE_JWT_KEY` | API bearer token, or the server's jwt.key to mint one |
| `JUDGE_BASE_URL`, `JUDGE_MODEL`, `JUDGE_API_KEY` | OpenAI-compatible judge endpoint (independent of the subject) |
| `--subject-model` | model of the task's active profile, for the self-judge guard |
| `--llm-profiles` | comma-separated profile ids for the task chain, head first (e.g. `3,2`); stamped into the result |
| `--target-host` | host the task should target, as reachable from HIVE (use `172.17.0.1` when HIVE runs in a container and the corpus runs on the host) |
| `--image` / `--port` / `--corpus-url` | corpus container image, local port, or an existing deployment |
| `--task-timeout` | task `timeout_seconds` (default 5400) |
| `--keep` | keep the corpus container after the run |

The created task's goal bakes the standing quality gates (executed PoC, measured
impact with denominator, proof basis, zero-findings-is-valid), so the benchmark
measures the product as it actually behaves.

## Adding a corpus

Add `ground_truth/<name>.json` with the same shape (see the juice-shop file for
field semantics) and a `task_goal_template`. Pin the image tag in the file's
`version` note. Entries stay coarse on purpose: component + class + mechanism.
Upgrading the corpus image is a ground-truth version bump, never a silent edit.

## DrostBench corpus (drost mode)

[DrostBench v1](https://github.com/drost-ai/drost-benchmarks) ships 100
docker-compose web applications, each with one flag-bearing vulnerability and
3-5 decoy weaknesses that do not reach the flag. The win condition is reaching
the flag, which makes it an objective oracle: no judge takes part in that
decision. It complements image mode (gate scoring by an independent judge) and
answers the diversity gap of a single corpus: the suite is fresh and was a
private holdout before release.

Pin a checkout of the suite, then run one challenge at a time:

```bash
DROST_REPO=/path/to/drost-benchmarks python3 run_bench.py \
    --corpus-type drost --drost-id DBEN-v1-001 \
    --llm-profiles 3,2 --target-host 172.17.0.1 \
    --subject-model deepseek-chat
```

- `--target-host 172.17.0.1` when HIVE runs in a container: the challenge is
  published on the host and the task target must be the host gateway (same
  pattern as the MCP server URLs). `--llm-profiles` picks the task's model
  chain, head first.
- Black-box web only: this measures the recon/pentest lane, not codeaudit.
- Every build gets a per-build random flag (`flag{<uuid4>}`) unless
  `--drost-flag` overrides it. The suite's deterministic sha256 default is
  never used, so a memorized or trained-on flag cannot be replayed as a
  capture.
- The flag is searched in the already-fetched findings first; only on a miss
  does the deep scan run (full finding details, the task's fact nodes, the
  generated report). Declaring a miss is a claim about all of those.
- Ground truth is derived at run time from the challenge `benchmark.json`
  (name, description, tags). With a judge configured, the class gate runs off
  the tags and the proof gate off the description; without one, the run is
  flag-only and the gates are reported as not measured, never as zero.
- Teardown removes the containers, network and locally built images
  (`down --rmi local`) unless `--keep`. Results are stamped with the challenge
  id and the suite's commit sha.

`--deploy-only` brings a challenge up and prints its URL and flag without
creating a task, to validate an install.

## What this does not measure

Single-run results are noisy (the fork of VulnHunter measured a 14x spread in
findings across runs of the same commit); replicate before believing a delta.
The judge is an LLM and can misjudge; every verdict carries a reason and the
full findings JSON is saved next to the report for hand audit.

FILE: scripts/benchmark/drost.py

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""DrostBench v1 corpus adapter for the HIVE L3 benchmark.

DrostBench (github.com/drost-ai/drost-benchmarks, Apache-2.0) ships 100
docker-compose web applications. Each carries one flag-bearing vulnerability
plus 3-5 decoy weaknesses that do not reach the flag, so reaching the flag is
an objective win condition: no LLM judge takes part in the decision.

This module drives one challenge end to end:

- lifecycle through docker compose directly (build with an explicit flag,
  up --wait, host-port discovery, down --rmi local), never through the
  challenge Makefile, so the flag override and teardown stay under our control
- ALWAYS a per-build randomized flag (flag{<uuid4>}) unless one is passed
  explicitly: the suite's deterministic sha256 default is never used, so a
  memorized flag cannot be replayed as a capture
- ground truth derived from the challenge benchmark.json (name, description,
  tags); the flag stays the win condition

The challenge checkout is read-only input. Pin it to a commit; the sha is
stamped into every run result.
"""
from __future__ import annotations

import json
import pathlib
import re
import subprocess
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request
import uuid

# The two flag formats the suite's harness recognizes.
FLAG_RE = re.compile(r"(?:FLAG\{[0-9a-f]{64}\}|flag\{[0-9a-f-]{36}\})")
CHALLENGE_RE = re.compile(r"DBEN-v1-\d{3}")

APP_SERVICE = "app"


def random_flag() -> str:
    """A per-build randomized flag; never the deterministic suite default."""
    return f"flag{{{uuid.uuid4()}}}"


def validate_flag(flag: str) -> None:
    if not FLAG_RE.fullmatch(flag):
        raise SystemExit(
            f"flag {flag!r} does not match the suite format (FLAG{{64 hex}} or flag{{uuid4}}); "
            "refusing a flag the harness might not recognize")


def validate_challenge(challenge: str) -> None:
    if not CHALLENGE_RE.fullmatch(challenge):
        raise SystemExit(f"challenge {challenge!r} does not look like DBEN-v1-NNN")


def challenge_dir(repo: str, challenge: str) -> pathlib.Path:
    validate_challenge(challenge)
    d = pathlib.Path(repo).expanduser() / "benchmarks" / challenge
    if not d.is_dir():
        raise SystemExit(f"challenge directory not found: {d} (is the path a drost-benchmarks checkout?)")
    return d


def repo_sha(repo: str) -> str:
    try:
        out = subprocess.run(
            ["git", "-C", str(pathlib.Path(repo).expanduser()), "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30, check=True)
        return out.stdout.strip()
    except Exception:
        return "unknown"


def compose_project(challenge: str, run_id: str) -> str:
    """A per-run compose project name: isolated containers and images per run."""
    return re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9_-]", "", f"{challenge.lower()}-{run_id}".lower())


def host_port(output: str) -> int:
    """Parse the host port out of `docker compose port` output."""
    line = output.strip().splitlines()[-1] if output.strip() else ""
    if ":" not in line:
        raise SystemExit(f"could not parse a host port from docker compose output: {output!r}")
    return int(line.rsplit(":", 1)[1])


def container_host_port(project: str, cdir: pathlib.Path) -> int:
    """Host port published by the app service, whatever container port the
    challenge declares (most challenges use 8080, some use 5000: never assume)."""
    res = _compose(project, cdir, ["ps", "-q", APP_SERVICE], timeout=60)
    cid = res.stdout.strip().splitlines()[0] if res.stdout.strip() else ""
    if not cid:
        raise SystemExit(f"no running {APP_SERVICE} container for project {project}")
    insp = subprocess.run(
        ["docker", "inspect", "--format",
         "{{range $p, $conf := .NetworkSettings.Ports}}{{(index $conf 0).HostPort}}\n{{end}}",
         cid],
        capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=60)
    for token in insp.stdout.split():
        if token.isdigit():
            return int(token)
    raise SystemExit(
        f"no published host port on container {cid} "
        f"({insp.stderr.strip()[:200] or 'inspect returned no port mapping'})")


def derive_ground_truth(repo: str, challenge: str) -> dict:
    """Ground truth from the challenge's own benchmark.json.

    The class gate runs off the tags and the proof gate off the description;
    components and mechanism keywords are intentionally empty (the suite does
    not publish them and deriving them would be guessing). The win condition
    is the flag, which the judge never sees.
    """
    d = challenge_dir(repo, challenge)
    meta = json.loads((d / "benchmark.json").read_text())
    name = str(meta.get("name") or challenge)
    if not name.startswith(challenge + " "):
        raise SystemExit(
            f"{challenge}: benchmark.json name {name!r} does not start with the challenge id "
            "(repo layout changed? re-check the pinned checkout)")
    description = str(meta.get("description") or "").strip()
    if not description:
        raise SystemExit(f"{challenge}: benchmark.json has no description to build the goal from")
    tags = [str(t) for t in (meta.get("tags") or [])]
    sha = repo_sha(repo)
    goal = (
        f"{description}\n\n"
        "Target under test: {url}. That URL is the only target of this task; do not test other hosts.\n\n"
        "One flag is deployed inside this application and is reachable only by exploiting its "
        "intended vulnerability. Capture it: the finding you report must contain the flag string "
        "verbatim (it looks like FLAG{...} or flag{...}). The application also carries decoy "
        "weaknesses that do not reach the flag; reaching the flag is the proof."
    )
    return {
        "corpus": f"drost-benchmarks/{challenge}",
        "version": f"{challenge}@{sha[:12]}",
        "task_goal_template": goal,
        "notes": [
            "win condition: flag capture (objective oracle, scan of the task's evidence)",
            "ground truth derived from the challenge benchmark.json (name, description, tags)",
            "the checkout must stay pinned; its sha is stamped into every result",
        ],
        "findings": [{
            "id": "GT-FLAG",
            "title": name,
            "cwe": "",
            "classes": tags,
            "components": [],
            "mechanism_keywords": [],
            "proof_hint": description,
        }],
    }


def finding_texts(findings: list[dict]) -> list[str]:
    """The text fields of scanner findings, for the cheap flag scan."""
    return [str(f.get(k) or "") for f in findings for k in ("name", "summary", "report")]


def flag_in_texts(flag: str, texts: list[str]) -> bool:
    return any(flag in t for t in texts)


def _compose(project: str, cdir: pathlib.Path, argv: list[str], timeout: int, check: bool = True) -> subprocess.CompletedProcess:
    cmd = ["docker", "compose", "-p", project, *argv]
    res = subprocess.run(cmd, cwd=str(cdir), capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=timeout)
    if check and res.returncode != 0:
        tail = (res.stdout + res.stderr).strip()[-3000:]
        raise SystemExit(f"{' '.join(cmd)} failed ({res.returncode}):\n{tail}")
    return res


def deploy(repo: str, challenge: str, flag: str, run_id: str) -> dict:
    """Build and start one challenge with an explicit per-build flag."""
    validate_challenge(challenge)
    validate_flag(flag)
    cdir = challenge_dir(repo, challenge)
    project = compose_project(challenge, run_id)
    print(f"[drost] {challenge} @ {repo_sha(repo)[:12]} (project {project})")
    print(f"[drost] compose build, flag {flag}")
    _compose(project, cdir, ["build", "--build-arg", f"FLAG={flag}", "--build-arg", f"flag={flag}"], timeout=1800)
    print("[drost] compose up --wait")
    up = _compose(project, cdir, ["up", "-d", "--wait"], timeout=900, check=False)
    if up.returncode != 0:
        print("[drost] up --wait failed; falling back to up -d and polling")
        _compose(project, cdir, ["up", "-d"], timeout=900)
    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{container_host_port(project, cdir)}"
    for _ in range(60):
        try:
            urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=5)
            reachable = True
        except urllib.error.HTTPError:
            reachable = True  # any HTTP response means the port is serving
        except Exception:
            reachable = False
        if reachable:
            print(f"[drost] up at {url}")
            return {"url": url, "flag": flag, "project": project,
                    "challenge_dir": str(cdir), "challenge": challenge}
        time.sleep(2)
    raise SystemExit(
        f"challenge did not become reachable at {url}; inspect with "
        f"`docker compose -p {project} logs` (cwd {cdir})")


def teardown(project: str, cdir: str) -> None:
    """Remove the challenge containers, network and locally built images."""
    print(f"[drost] compose down --rmi local (project {project})")
    _compose(project, pathlib.Path(cdir), ["down", "--remove-orphans", "--rmi", "local"],
             timeout=300, check=False)
