// Step 1.8: the targets the custom tools render. The hook reads the parameters
// of a custom tool, not the URL or the command they produce: the tool runs the
// gate on what it is about to run. Plus the end-to-end run of a gated worker
// and the run of a task with the gate off.

// countingServer is an HTTP server on 127.0.0.1 that counts the requests it
// receives. Its host:port is an IP literal: the gate never resolves it.
func countingServer(t *testing.T) (srv *httptest.Server, hits *atomic.Int64, host, port string) {
	t.Helper()
	hits = &atomic.Int64{}
	srv = httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		hits.Add(1)
		w.Header().Set("Content-Type", "text/plain")
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte("probe-reached"))
	}))
	t.Cleanup(srv.Close)
	u, err := url.Parse(srv.URL)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	host, port, err = net.SplitHostPort(u.Host)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return srv, hits, host, port
}

// gatedCtx is the context of a worker tool call of task: its approval scope
// with the given wait bound.
func gatedCtx(task *Task, wait time.Duration) context.Context {
	ctx := intercept.WithTaskContext(context.Background(), task.ID, "worker", nil)
	return intercept.WithTargetScope(ctx, task.targetScope(wait))
}

func execJSON(t *testing.T, v any) json.RawMessage {
	t.Helper()
	b, err := json.Marshal(v)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return b
}

// callTool runs a custom tool the way the harness does and returns its text.
func callTool(t *testing.T, tool actool.CoreTool, ctx context.Context, input string, tc *actool.ToolContext) (string, bool) {
	t.Helper()
	res, err := tool.Call(ctx, json.RawMessage(input), tc)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("%s: %v", tool.Name(), err)
	}
	return res.Flatten(), res.IsError
}

// openTargetRequest returns the open target request of the task on key.
func openTargetRequest(t *testing.T, pg *db.DB, taskID, key string) (id int64, toolName, toolInput string, ok bool) {
	t.Helper()
	err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT id, tool_name, tool_input::text FROM intercept_pending
WHERE task_id=$1 AND status='pending' AND target_key=$2`, taskID, key).Scan(&id, &toolName, &toolInput)
	if err != nil {
		return 0, "", "", false
	}
	return id, toolName, toolInput, true
}

func targetRowCount(t *testing.T, pg *db.DB, taskID string) int {
	t.Helper()
	var n int
	if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM intercept_pending WHERE task_id=$1 AND (decision_source='target' OR target_key IS NOT NULL)`, taskID).Scan(&n); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	return n
}

// A custom http tool is gated on the URL it renders, whether the target comes
// from a parameter (here split over two parameters, so the hook reads no
// target in them) or is written in the template. Nothing is sent before an
// approval; an approval lets both through; a revoked pin asks again.
func TestCustomHTTPRenderedTargetGated(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	on := true
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on})
	pg := g.m.pg
	srv, hits, host, port := countingServer(t)
	key := net.JoinHostPort(host, port)
	dot := strings.LastIndexByte(host, '.')

	rendered := g.s.buildCustomTool(&db.Tool{Key: "probe_http", Kind: "http",
		Schema: json.RawMessage(`{"type":"object","properties":{"last":{"type":"string"},"port":{"type":"string"}}}`),
		Exec:   execJSON(t, map[string]any{"method": "GET", "url": "http://" + host[:dot+1] + "{last}:{port}/rendered"})})
	params := fmt.Sprintf(`{"last":%q,"port":%q}`, host[dot+1:], port)
	fixed := g.s.buildCustomTool(&db.Tool{Key: "probe_fixed", Kind: "http",
		Exec: execJSON(t, map[string]any{"method": "GET", "url": srv.URL + "/fixed"})})
	// The hook cannot see either target: neither input names one.
	for _, in := range []struct{ tool, input string }{{"probe_http", params}, {"probe_fixed", `{}`}} {
		if got := intercept.ExtractTargets(in.tool, []byte(in.input)); len(got) != 0 {
			t.Fatalf("%s: the hook reads %+v; the test needs a target only the rendering shows", in.tool, got)
		}
	}

	// The template's own URL, wait bound 0: blocked at once, nothing sent, the
	// request open with the rendered URL as its input.
	out, isErr := callTool(t, fixed, gatedCtx(task, 0), `{}`, nil)
	if !isErr || !strings.Contains(out, "TARGET_APPROVAL_PENDING") || !strings.Contains(out, key) || hits.Load() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("hard-coded URL: error=%v out=%q hits=%d", isErr, out, hits.Load())
	}
	id, toolName, toolInput, ok := openTargetRequest(t, pg, task.ID, key)
	if !ok || toolName != "probe_fixed" || !strings.Contains(toolInput, srv.URL+"/fixed") {
		t.Fatalf("request row: ok=%v tool=%q input=%s", ok, toolName, toolInput)
	}

	// The rendered URL names the same host and port: the call attaches to the
	// open request and waits. One click lets it through.
	type result struct {
		out   string
		isErr bool
	}
	done := make(chan result, 1)
	go func() {
		res, err := rendered.Call(gatedCtx(task, 30*time.Second), json.RawMessage(params), nil)
		if err != nil {
			done <- result{err.Error(), true}
			return
		}
		done <- result{res.Flatten(), res.IsError}
	}()
	time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond)
	if hits.Load() != 0 {
		t.Fatal("the rendered URL was fetched before the approval")
	}
	if n := targetRowCount(t, pg, task.ID); n != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d target rows, want the one request", n)
	}
	if code, body := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/intercept/pending/%d/decide", id), `{"decision":"allowed"}`); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("decide: %d %v", code, body)
	}
	select {
	case r := <-done:
		if r.isErr || !strings.Contains(r.out, "probe-reached") || hits.Load() != 1 {
			t.Fatalf("after the approval: error=%v out=%q hits=%d", r.isErr, r.out, hits.Load())
		}
	case <-time.After(30 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the waiting call did not end after the approval")
	}
	if out, isErr := callTool(t, fixed, gatedCtx(task, 0), `{}`, nil); isErr || hits.Load() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("pinned, hard-coded URL: error=%v out=%q hits=%d", isErr, out, hits.Load())
	}

	// Revoked: the next call asks again and sends nothing.
	pins, err := pg.ListTargetPins(taskRef(t, task))
	if err != nil || len(pins) != 1 || pins[0].Host != host || fmt.Sprint(pins[0].Port) != port {
		t.Fatalf("pins = %+v, %v", pins, err)
	}
	if code, _ := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/tasks/%s/target-pins/%d/revoke", task.ID, pins[0].ID), ""); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("revoke: %d", code)
	}
	out, isErr = callTool(t, rendered, gatedCtx(task, 0), params, nil)
	if !isErr || !strings.Contains(out, "TARGET_APPROVAL_PENDING") || hits.Load() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("revoked: error=%v out=%q hits=%d", isErr, out, hits.Load())
	}
	if again, toolName, _, ok := openTargetRequest(t, pg, task.ID, key); !ok || again == id || toolName != "probe_http" {
		t.Fatalf("after the revoke: open request %d (ok=%v, tool %q), want a new one", again, ok, toolName)
	}

	// A URL whose target cannot be read is blocked, never sent.
	broken := g.s.buildCustomTool(&db.Tool{Key: "probe_broken", Kind: "http",
		Schema: json.RawMessage(`{"type":"object","properties":{"host":{"type":"string"}}}`),
		Exec:   execJSON(t, map[string]any{"url": "http://{host}/x"})})
	out, isErr = callTool(t, broken, gatedCtx(task, 0), `{"host":"a b"}`, nil)
	if !isErr || !strings.Contains(out, "TARGET_GATE_UNAVAILABLE") {
		t.Fatalf("unreadable URL: error=%v out=%q", isErr, out)
	}
}

// A custom command tool is gated on the command it renders, with a target
// written in the template or formed by a parameter inside a host name. The
// command does not run before an approval.
func TestCustomCommandRenderedTargetGated(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	on := true
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on})
	pg := g.m.pg
	res := &countingResolver{answers: map[string][]string{"api.example.com": {"198.51.100.7"}}}
	g.m.interceptor.SetResolver(res)
	dir := t.TempDir()
	marker := filepath.Join(dir, "marker")
	ran := func() bool {
		_, err := os.Stat(marker)
		return err == nil
	}

	fixed := g.s.buildCustomTool(&db.Tool{Key: "probe_cmd_fixed", Kind: "command",
		Exec: execJSON(t, map[string]any{"command": "echo reached > '" + marker + "' && : http://198.51.100.7:8080/"})})
	glued := g.s.buildCustomTool(&db.Tool{Key: "probe_cmd", Kind: "command",
		Schema: json.RawMessage(`{"type":"object","properties":{"sub":{"type":"string"}}}`),
		Exec:   execJSON(t, map[string]any{"command": "echo reached > '" + marker + "' && : http://{sub}.example.com:8080/"})})
	if got := intercept.ExtractTargets("probe_cmd", []byte(`{"sub":"api"}`)); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the hook reads %+v; the test needs a target only the rendering shows", got)
	}
	tc := &actool.ToolContext{WorkingDir: dir}

	for _, c := range []struct {
		name  string
		tool  actool.CoreTool
		input string
		key   string
	}{
		{"template", fixed, `{}`, "198.51.100.7:8080"},
		{"parameter inside the host", glued, `{"sub":"api"}`, "api.example.com:8080"},
	} {
		out, isErr := callTool(t, c.tool, gatedCtx(task, 0), c.input, tc)
		if !isErr || !strings.Contains(out, "TARGET_APPROVAL_PENDING") || ran() {
			t.Fatalf("%s: error=%v out=%q ran=%v, want a block before the command runs", c.name, isErr, out, ran())
		}
		id, toolName, _, ok := openTargetRequest(t, pg, task.ID, c.key)
		if !ok || toolName != c.tool.Name() {
			t.Fatalf("%s: no open request on %s for %s", c.name, c.key, c.tool.Name())
		}
		if code, body := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/intercept/pending/%d/decide", id), `{"decision":"allowed"}`); code != 200 {
			t.Fatalf("%s: decide: %d %v", c.name, code, body)
		}
		if out, isErr := callTool(t, c.tool, gatedCtx(task, 0), c.input, tc); isErr || !ran() {
			t.Fatalf("%s, approved: error=%v out=%q ran=%v", c.name, isErr, out, ran())
		}
		_ = os.Remove(marker)
	}
	if res.lookups() == 0 {
		t.Fatal("the name formed by the parameter was never resolved")
	}
}

// The custom-tool test endpoint is the operator's own action (D14): it has no
// approval scope, so the gate is not on there, whatever the tasks say.
func TestCustomToolTestEndpointUngated(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	on := true
	g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on})
	_, hits, host, port := countingServer(t)
	before := 0
	if err := g.m.pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM intercept_pending WHERE decision_source='target' OR target_key IS NOT NULL`).Scan(&before); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	body := fmt.Sprintf(`{"kind":"http","exec":{"url":"http://%s:{port}/test"},"params":{"port":%q}}`, host, port)
	code, out := g.do(t, "POST", "/api/tools/custom/test", body)
	if code != 200 || out["is_error"] != false || !strings.Contains(fmt.Sprint(out["output"]), "probe-reached") || hits.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("http: %d %v hits=%d", code, out, hits.Load())
	}
	code, out = g.do(t, "POST", "/api/tools/custom/test", `{"kind":"command","exec":{"command":": http://198.51.100.7:8080/ && echo ran-ungated"}}`)
	if code != 200 || !strings.Contains(fmt.Sprint(out["output"]), "ran-ungated") {
		t.Fatalf("command: %d %v", code, out)
	}
	after := 0
	if err := g.m.pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM intercept_pending WHERE decision_source='target' OR target_key IS NOT NULL`).Scan(&after); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	if after != before {
		t.Fatalf("the test endpoint wrote %d target rows", after-before)
	}
}

// countingResolver answers from a table and counts every lookup.
type countingResolver struct {
	mu      sync.Mutex
	answers map[string][]string
	n       int
}

func (r *countingResolver) Name() string { return "counting" }

func (r *countingResolver) LookupIPs(_ context.Context, host string) ([]netip.Addr, error) {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	r.n++
	var out []netip.Addr
	for _, ip := range r.answers[host] {
		out = append(out, netip.MustParseAddr(ip))
	}
	if len(out) == 0 {
		return nil, fmt.Errorf("no answer for %s", host)
	}
	return out, nil
}

func (r *countingResolver) lookups() int {
	r.mu.Lock()
	defer r.mu.Unlock()
	return r.n
}

// scriptedCall is one tool call of a toolScript.
type scriptedCall struct{ tool, input string }

func fetches(urls ...string) []scriptedCall {
	calls := make([]scriptedCall, len(urls))
	for n, u := range urls {
		calls[n] = scriptedCall{"WebFetch", fmt.Sprintf(`{"url":%q}`, u)}
	}
	return calls
}

// toolScript is a model that makes each of its calls in turn, one per turn,
// then ends the run. It hands the result of every call to the test, and waits
// before turn n while hold[n] is open.
type toolScript struct {
	calls   []scriptedCall
	hold    map[int64]chan struct{}
	results chan string
	turn    atomic.Int64
}

func (p *toolScript) Stream(ctx context.Context, req llm.CompletionRequest) iter.Seq2[llm.StreamEvent, error] {
	n := p.turn.Add(1)
	if n > 1 {
		select {
		case p.results <- lastToolResult(req.Messages):
		default:
		}
	}
	if h := p.hold[n]; h != nil {
		select {
		case <-h:
		case <-ctx.Done():
		}
	}
	events := []llm.StreamEvent{{Type: llm.SETextDelta, Text: "done"}, {Type: llm.SEMessageDelta, StopReason: "end_turn"}}
	if int(n) <= len(p.calls) {
		call := p.calls[n-1]
		events = []llm.StreamEvent{
			{Type: llm.SEToolUseStart, ToolID: fmt.Sprintf("call-%d", n), ToolName: call.tool},
			{Type: llm.SEToolInputJSON, Text: call.input},
			{Type: llm.SEMessageDelta, StopReason: "tool_use"},
		}
	}
	return func(yield func(llm.StreamEvent, error) bool) {
		for _, event := range events {
			if !yield(event, nil) {
				return
			}
		}
	}
}

func (p *toolScript) Complete(ctx context.Context, req llm.CompletionRequest) (llm.Message, string, llm.Usage, error) {
	return accumulateStreamForTest(ctx, p.Stream, req)
}

func (p *toolScript) next(t *testing.T) string {
	t.Helper()
	select {
	case r := <-p.results:
		return r
	case <-time.After(60 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the worker did not hand back a tool result")
		return ""
	}
}

// lastToolResult is the text of the last tool result the model is shown.
func lastToolResult(msgs []llm.Message) string {
	for i := len(msgs) - 1; i >= 0; i-- {
		for _, b := range msgs[i].Content {
			if b.Type != llm.BlockToolResult {
				continue
			}
			var s strings.Builder
			if b.IsError {
				s.WriteString("[error] ")
			}
			for _, c := range b.Content {
				s.WriteString(c.Text)
			}
			return s.String()
		}
	}
	return ""
}

// runScriptedWorker claims one intent of task and runs it with a worker driven
// by p, in the background. extra are tools the worker has besides its own.
func runScriptedWorker(t *testing.T, g *gateServer, task *Task, p llm.Provider, extra ...actool.CoreTool) <-chan struct{} {
	t.Helper()
	if _, err := task.Store.AddIntent(map[string]any{"summary": "fetch the probe"}, 1, nil, "planner"); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	intent, token := g.s.engine.claimNext(task, "work#1")
	if intent == nil {
		t.Fatal("no intent claimed")
	}
	worker := agent.NewWorker(p, "test-model", g.m.dir, nil, 0, 8, extra...)
	done := make(chan struct{})
	go func() {
		defer close(done)
		g.s.engine.runIntent(context.Background(), task, "work#1", worker, intent, token, "", "")
	}()
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		select {
		case <-done:
		case <-time.After(60 * time.Second):
			t.Error("the worker run did not end")
		}
	})
	return done
}

// A gated task end to end: a worker's WebFetch waits on a request, a click
// through the API pins the address and the call is made, the next call passes
// on the pin, the pin is listed and revoked, and the call after asks again.
func TestTargetGateEndToEnd(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	on := true
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on})
	pg := g.m.pg
	srv, hits, host, port := countingServer(t)
	key := net.JoinHostPort(host, port)
	target := srv.URL + "/e2e"
	p := &toolScript{calls: fetches(target, target, target), results: make(chan string, 16),
		hold: map[int64]chan struct{}{3: make(chan struct{})}}
	done := runScriptedWorker(t, g, task, p)

	var id int64
	waitUntil(t, "the first request", func() bool {
		var ok bool
		id, _, _, ok = openTargetRequest(t, pg, task.ID, key)
		return ok
	})
	if hits.Load() != 0 {
		t.Fatal("fetched before the approval")
	}
	if code, body := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/intercept/pending/%d/decide", id), `{"decision":"allowed"}`); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("decide: %d %v", code, body)
	}
	if r := p.next(t); !strings.Contains(r, "probe-reached") || hits.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("first call after the approval: %q hits=%d", r, hits.Load())
	}
	if r := p.next(t); !strings.Contains(r, "probe-reached") || hits.Load() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("second call, pinned: %q hits=%d", r, hits.Load())
	}
	var requests int
	if err := pg.QueryRow(`SELECT count(*) FROM intercept_pending WHERE task_id=$1 AND target_key IS NOT NULL`, task.ID).Scan(&requests); err != nil || requests != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d requests, %v; want the one that was approved", requests, err)
	}

	code, body := g.do(t, "GET", "/api/tasks/"+task.ID+"/target-pins", "")
	pins, _ := body["pins"].([]any)
	if code != 200 || len(pins) != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("pins: %d %v", code, body)
	}
	pin := pins[0].(map[string]any)
	if pin["host"] != host || fmt.Sprint(pin["port"]) != port || pin["status"] != "active" || fmt.Sprint(pin["pinned_ips"]) != "["+host+"]" {
		t.Fatalf("listed pin = %v", pin)
	}
	pinID, _ := pin["id"].(float64)
	if code, _ := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/tasks/%s/target-pins/%d/revoke", task.ID, int64(pinID)), ""); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("revoke: %d", code)
	}
	close(p.hold[3])

	var again int64
	waitUntil(t, "the request after the revoke", func() bool {
		var ok bool
		again, _, _, ok = openTargetRequest(t, pg, task.ID, key)
		return ok && again != id
	})
	if code, body := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/intercept/pending/%d/decide", again), `{"decision":"denied"}`); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("deny: %d %v", code, body)
	}
	if r := p.next(t); !strings.Contains(r, "TARGET_DENIED") || hits.Load() != 2 {
		t.Fatalf("third call, revoked then denied: %q hits=%d", r, hits.Load())
	}
	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(60 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the worker run did not end")
	}
}

// A custom tool in a gated worker session. A deny rule on the call decides
// first, at the hook: the tool never runs, so its rendered target is never
// read, resolved or requested. The next call, which no rule refuses, is gated
// inside the tool on the URL it renders.
func TestDenyRuleWinsBeforeRenderedTarget(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	on := true
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on})
	pg, ic := g.m.pg, g.m.interceptor
	_, hits, _, port := countingServer(t)
	res := &countingResolver{answers: map[string][]string{"api.example.com": {"127.0.0.1"}}}
	ic.SetResolver(res)

	prior, err := ic.GetEnabledTools()
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() { _ = ic.SetEnabledTools(prior) })
	if err := ic.SetEnabledTools(append(slices.Clone(prior), "probe_http")); err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	const sentinel = "HIVE_RENDERED_DENY_PROBE"
	rule, err := pg.CreateInterceptRule("rendered deny probe", "tool_input", "string", sentinel, "deny", "", 1000000, true, false, 0, "deny")
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatal(err)
	}
	t.Cleanup(func() {
		_ = pg.DeleteInterceptRule(rule.ID)
		ic.Invalidate()
	})
	ic.Invalidate()

	tool := g.s.buildCustomTool(&db.Tool{Key: "probe_http", Kind: "http",
		Schema: json.RawMessage(`{"type":"object","properties":{"sub":{"type":"string"},"note":{"type":"string"}}}`),
		Exec:   execJSON(t, map[string]any{"url": "http://{sub}.example.com:" + port + "/deny"})})
	p := &toolScript{calls: []scriptedCall{
		{"probe_http", `{"sub":"api","note":"` + sentinel + `"}`},
		{"probe_http", `{"sub":"api"}`},
	}, results: make(chan string, 16), hold: map[int64]chan struct{}{2: make(chan struct{})}}
	done := runScriptedWorker(t, g, task, p, tool)

	if r := p.next(t); !strings.Contains(r, "intercepted by the platform") || strings.Contains(r, "TARGET_") {
		t.Fatalf("call refused by the rule: %q", r)
	}
	if n, rows := res.lookups(), targetRowCount(t, pg, task.ID); n != 0 || rows != 0 || hits.Load() != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("after the deny: %d lookups, %d target rows, %d requests sent; want none", n, rows, hits.Load())
	}
	close(p.hold[2])

	key := "api.example.com:" + port
	var id int64
	waitUntil(t, "the request for the rendered target", func() bool {
		var ok bool
		var tool string
		id, tool, _, ok = openTargetRequest(t, pg, task.ID, key)
		return ok && tool == "probe_http"
	})
	if code, body := g.do(t, "POST", fmt.Sprintf("/api/intercept/pending/%d/decide", id), `{"decision":"denied"}`); code != 200 {
		t.Fatalf("deny: %d %v", code, body)
	}
	if r := p.next(t); !strings.Contains(r, "TARGET_DENIED") || hits.Load() != 0 || res.lookups() == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("rendered target: %q, %d requests sent, %d lookups", r, hits.Load(), res.lookups())
	}
	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(60 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the worker run did not end")
	}
}

// Documents a known limit: script tools stay advisory (D9). A custom script
// tool's target is in its stored code, which neither the hook nor the tool
// reads, so in a gated task the call is allowed and the script reaches a target
// nobody approved: no lookup, no request, no row. This test changes only if
// that decision changes.
func TestBypass_CustomScriptToolTargetNotGated(t *testing.T) {
	if detectPython() == "" {
		t.Skip("python3 unavailable")
	}
	g := newGateServer(t)
	on := true
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{TargetGate: &on})
	res := &countingResolver{answers: map[string][]string{"localhost": {"127.0.0.1"}}}
	g.m.interceptor.SetResolver(res)
	_, hits, _, port := countingServer(t)

	code := "import urllib.request\n" +
		"opener = urllib.request.build_opener(urllib.request.ProxyHandler({}))\n" +
		"print(opener.open('http://localhost:" + port + "/script', timeout=20).read().decode())\n"
	tool := g.s.buildCustomTool(&db.Tool{Key: "probe_script", Kind: "script", Exec: execJSON(t, map[string]any{"code": code})})
	// The gate sees no target in the call: only the parameters reach the hook.
	if got := intercept.ExtractTargets("probe_script", []byte(`{}`)); len(got) != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("the hook reads %+v; the test needs a target only the stored code names", got)
	}

	p := &toolScript{calls: []scriptedCall{{"probe_script", `{}`}}, results: make(chan string, 16)}
	done := runScriptedWorker(t, g, task, p, tool)
	if r := p.next(t); !strings.Contains(r, "probe-reached") || strings.Contains(r, "TARGET_") {
		t.Fatalf("script tool in a gated task: %q, want it allowed and the target reached", r)
	}
	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(60 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the worker run did not end")
	}
	if hits.Load() != 1 {
		t.Fatalf("%d requests reached the unapproved target, want 1 (the gap)", hits.Load())
	}
	if n, rows := res.lookups(), targetRowCount(t, g.m.pg, task.ID); n != 0 || rows != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%d lookups, %d target rows; the gate did see the script's target", n, rows)
	}
}

// A task with the gate off (the default) runs as before: a worker's WebFetch
// and the custom tools reach their targets, and the gate writes no row and
// resolves no name.
func TestGateOffTaskIsUnchanged(t *testing.T) {
	g := newGateServer(t)
	task := g.newTask(t, db.TaskCreateOptions{})
	res := &countingResolver{answers: map[string][]string{"localhost": {"127.0.0.1"}}}
	g.m.interceptor.SetResolver(res)
	_, hits, _, port := countingServer(t)
	byName := "http://localhost:" + port

	p := &toolScript{calls: fetches(byName+"/a", byName+"/b"), results: make(chan string, 16)}
	done := runScriptedWorker(t, g, task, p)
	for n := 1; n <= 2; n++ {
		if r := p.next(t); !strings.Contains(r, "probe-reached") {
			t.Fatalf("WebFetch %d: %q", n, r)
		}
	}
	select {
	case <-done:
	case <-time.After(60 * time.Second):
		t.Fatal("the worker run did not end")
	}

	httpTool := g.s.buildCustomTool(&db.Tool{Key: "probe_http", Kind: "http",
		Schema: json.RawMessage(`{"type":"object","properties":{"port":{"type":"string"}}}`),
		Exec:   execJSON(t, map[string]any{"url": "http://localhost:{port}/c"})})
	if out, isErr := callTool(t, httpTool, gatedCtx(task, intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound), fmt.Sprintf(`{"port":%q}`, port), nil); isErr || !strings.Contains(out, "probe-reached") {
		t.Fatalf("custom http tool: error=%v out=%q", isErr, out)
	}
	cmdTool := g.s.buildCustomTool(&db.Tool{Key: "probe_cmd", Kind: "command",
		Exec: execJSON(t, map[string]any{"command": ": http://localhost:" + port + "/ && echo ran-gate-off"})})
	if out, isErr := callTool(t, cmdTool, gatedCtx(task, intercept.DefaultTargetWaitBound), `{}`, &actool.ToolContext{WorkingDir: t.TempDir()}); isErr || !strings.Contains(out, "ran-gate-off") {
		t.Fatalf("custom command tool: error=%v out=%q", isErr, out)
	}

	if hits.Load() != 3 {
		t.Fatalf("%d requests reached the server, want 3", hits.Load())
	}
	if n := targetRowCount(t, g.m.pg, task.ID); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%d target rows, want none", n)
	}
	if n := res.lookups(); n != 0 {
		t.Fatalf("%d lookups, want none", n)
	}
}

package server

import (
	"context"
	"encoding/json"
	"io"
	"net/http"
	"net/http/httptest"
	"os/exec"
	"strings"
	"testing"
	"time"
)

func TestRenderTemplateCommand(t *testing.T) {
	// command: string params shell-quoted; array → JSON (also quoted).
	got := renderTemplate("nmap -p {ports} {target}", map[string]any{
		"target": "10.0.0.1; rm -rf /", // injection attempt → must be single-quoted
		"ports":  []any{80.0, 443.0},
	}, shellQuote)
	if !strings.Contains(got, `'10.0.0.1; rm -rf /'`) {
		t.Fatalf("target not shell-quoted: %q", got)
	}
	if strings.Contains(got, "rm -rf /'") && !strings.Contains(got, `'10.0.0.1; rm -rf /'`) {
		t.Fatalf("possible injection leak: %q", got)
	}
	if strings.Contains(got, "{target}") || strings.Contains(got, "{ports}") {
		t.Fatalf("placeholders not replaced: %q", got)
	}
}

func TestRenderTemplateHTTP(t *testing.T) {
	// http: identity (no shell quoting) — raw substitution into url/body.
	got := renderTemplate("https://x/submit?flag={flag}", map[string]any{"flag": "CTF{abc}"}, identity)
	if got != "https://x/submit?flag=CTF{abc}" {
		t.Fatalf("http render: %q", got)
	}
}

func TestScalarStr(t *testing.T) {
	cases := []struct {
		v    any
		want string
		ok   bool
	}{
		{"hi", "hi", true},
		{true, "true", true},
		{float64(80), "80", true},   // integer-valued float → no decimal
		{float64(1.5), "1.5", true}, // real float
		{[]any{1, 2}, "", false},    // array → not scalar
		{map[string]any{}, "", false},
	}
	for _, c := range cases {
		got, ok := scalarStr(c.v)
		if ok != c.ok || (ok && got != c.want) {
			t.Fatalf("scalarStr(%v) = (%q,%v), want (%q,%v)", c.v, got, ok, c.want, c.ok)
		}
	}
}

func TestEnsureSchema(t *testing.T) {
	// empty → thin {args:string}
	m := ensureSchema(nil)
	props, _ := m["properties"].(map[string]any)
	if _, ok := props["args"]; !ok {
		t.Fatalf("empty schema should default to args: %v", m)
	}
	// non-empty → passthrough
	raw := json.RawMessage(`{"type":"object","properties":{"target":{"type":"string"}}}`)
	m2 := ensureSchema(raw)
	p2, _ := m2["properties"].(map[string]any)
	if _, ok := p2["target"]; !ok {
		t.Fatalf("non-empty schema should pass through: %v", m2)
	}
}

func TestShellQuote(t *testing.T) {
	if got := shellQuote("a'b"); got != `'a'\''b'` {
		t.Fatalf("shellQuote(a'b) = %q", got)
	}
}

// TestExecPython runs a real Python script end-to-end: it must read params from
// stdin JSON and the mirrored env var, then print — verifying the whole script
// param-passing path. Skips if no python3.
func TestExecPython(t *testing.T) {
	interp, err := exec.LookPath("python3")
	if err != nil {
		t.Skip("python3 unavailable")
	}
	code := `import json,sys,os
a = json.load(sys.stdin)
print("stdin_target=" + a["target"])
print("env_target=" + os.environ.get("TOOL_TARGET",""))
print("port=" + str(a["port"]))
`
	out, err := execPython(context.Background(), interp, "test", code,
		map[string]any{"target": "example.com", "port": float64(8080)},
		t.TempDir(), nil, 10*time.Second)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("execPython error: %v", err)
	}
	for _, want := range []string{"stdin_target=example.com", "env_target=example.com", "port=8080"} {
		if !strings.Contains(out, want) {
			t.Fatalf("output missing %q:\n%s", want, out)
		}
	}
}

// TestRunHTTPTool functionally exercises the http executor against a local server:
// method/url/header/body templates are rendered from params, the request is sent,
// and the response status+body are returned. No recording proxy → s.m untouched.
func TestRunHTTPTool(t *testing.T) {
	var gotMethod, gotAuth, gotBody string
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		gotMethod = r.Method
		gotAuth = r.Header.Get("Authorization")
		b, _ := io.ReadAll(r.Body)
		gotBody = string(b)
		w.WriteHeader(201)
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte(`{"ok":true}`))
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	execRaw, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{
		"method":  "POST",
		"url":     srv.URL + "/submit?flag={flag}",
		"headers": map[string]string{"Authorization": "Bearer {token}"},
		"body":    `{"flag":"{flag}"}`,
	})
	res, err := (&Server{}).runHTTPTool(context.Background(), "probe", execRaw,
		map[string]any{"flag": "CTF{x}", "token": "sekret"}, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("runHTTPTool: %v", err)
	}
	if res.IsError || len(res.Content) == 0 {
		t.Fatalf("unexpected result: %+v", res)
	}
	var out struct {
		Status int    `json:"status"`
		Body   string `json:"body"`
	}
	_ = json.Unmarshal([]byte(res.Content[0].Text), &out)

	if gotMethod != "POST" {
		t.Fatalf("method: %q", gotMethod)
	}
	if gotAuth != "Bearer sekret" {
		t.Fatalf("header template not rendered: %q", gotAuth)
	}
	if gotBody != `{"flag":"CTF{x}"}` {
		t.Fatalf("body template not rendered: %q", gotBody)
	}
	if out.Status != 201 || !strings.Contains(out.Body, `"ok":true`) {
		t.Fatalf("response not captured: %+v", out)
	}
}

func TestDetectPython(t *testing.T) {
	if _, err := exec.LookPath("python3"); err != nil {
		t.Skip("python3 unavailable")
	}
	if p := detectPython(); p == "" {
		t.Fatal("detectPython returned empty despite python3 on PATH")
	}
}

// The http tool must truncate an oversized response through norma's Capture, the
// same valve every other tool uses — a session with no OutputDir falls back to a
// head+tail cut, so a body far past the default cap comes back shortened.
func TestHTTPToolTruncatesLargeBody(t *testing.T) {
	big := strings.Repeat("x", 40000) // past Capture's 30000 default
	srv := httptest.NewServer(http.HandlerFunc(func(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
		_, _ = w.Write([]byte(big))
	}))
	defer srv.Close()

	execRaw, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]any{"method": "GET", "url": srv.URL})
	res, err := (&Server{}).runHTTPTool(context.Background(), "probe", execRaw, map[string]any{}, nil)
	if err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("runHTTPTool: %v", err)
	}
	out := res.Flatten()
	if len(out) >= 40000 {
		t.Fatalf("oversized http body was not truncated: len=%d", len(out))
	}
}

package server

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"net/http"
	"net/url"
	"strings"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/config"
)

// dbSecurityStatus tells the frontend whether the database is still on the
// built-in hive/hive/hive default and whether this session can rotate it.
type dbSecurityStatus struct {
	DefaultCredentials bool   `json:"default_credentials"`
	Changeable         bool   `json:"changeable"`
	Source             string `json:"source"`
}

func dbSecurityFromConfig() dbSecurityStatus {
	dsn, source, err := config.PostgresDSN()
	if err != nil {
		return dbSecurityStatus{Source: "unavailable: " + err.Error()}
	}
	u, perr := url.Parse(dsn)
	pw := ""
	if perr == nil && u.User != nil {
		pw, _ = u.User.Password()
	}
	return dbSecurityStatus{
		DefaultCredentials: perr == nil && u.User.Username() == "hive" && pw == "hive",
		Changeable:         !strings.HasPrefix(source, "environment variable"),
		Source:             source,
	}
}

// GET /api/system/db-security
func (s *Server) dbSecurity(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	writeJSON(w, 200, dbSecurityFromConfig())
}

// POST /api/system/db-credentials  {password}
//
// Rotates the database password away from the built-in default. Only available
// while the default credentials are in effect (the first-login prompt); it is
// not a general password manager. Runs ALTER USER on the pool (the hive role
// changing its own password needs no extra privilege), then persists the new
// password into config.json so restarts keep it. Existing pool connections
// stay valid after the rotation; new connections use the stored password.
func (s *Server) dbChangeCredentials(w http.ResponseWriter, r *http.Request) {
	st := dbSecurityFromConfig()
	if !st.DefaultCredentials {
		writeErr(w, 409, "the database is not using the default credentials; this rotation is only offered while the defaults are in effect")
		return
	}
	if !st.Changeable {
		writeErr(w, 400, "the database is configured via the HIVE_PG_DSN environment variable; rotate its password in the environment")
		return
	}
	var body struct {
		Password string `json:"password"`
	}
	if err := json.NewDecoder(r.Body).Decode(&body); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 400, err.Error())
		return
	}
	pw := body.Password
	if len(pw) < 8 || len(pw) > 72 {
		writeErr(w, 400, "password must be 8–72 bytes (PostgreSQL SCRAM limit)")
		return
	}
	dsn, _, err := config.PostgresDSN()
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, err.Error())
		return
	}
	u, err := url.Parse(dsn)
	if err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, "parse DSN: "+err.Error())
		return
	}
	user := u.User.Username()
	if user == "" {
		writeErr(w, 500, "no database user in resolved DSN")
		return
	}
	// Quote the identifier (double quotes, inner quotes doubled) — it comes from
	// the operator's own config, not a request field, but quote defensively.
	ident := `"` + strings.ReplaceAll(user, `"`, `""`) + `"`
	pg := s.pg(w)
	if pg == nil {
		return
	}
	if _, err := pg.Exec("ALTER USER "+ident+" WITH PASSWORD $1", pw); err != nil {
		writeErr(w, 500, "ALTER USER failed: "+err.Error())
		return
	}
	if err := config.SaveDatabaseCreds(pw); err != nil {
		log.Printf("[db-security] password rotated but config save failed: %v", err)
		writeErr(w, 500, fmt.Sprintf("password rotated but could not persist to %s: %v", config.Path(), err))
		return
	}
	log.Printf("[db-security] database password rotated away from default (user %s)", user)
	writeJSON(w, 200, map[string]any{"ok": true})
}

package server

import (
	"encoding/json"
	"fmt"
	"strconv"
	"time"

	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/db"
	"github.com/ProjectZeroDays/edg-hive/traffic"
)

// DTO/serialization layer: each handler emits EXACTLY the frontend's spec shapes
// (hive/web/src/lib/types.ts). These reshape db package structs so the
// internal DB model never leaks over the API. The db structs and the frontend are
// the canonical contracts; this file maps one onto the other.

func i64s(v int64) string { return strconv.FormatInt(v, 10) }

func rfc3339(t time.Time) string { return t.Format(time.RFC3339) }

// rawString stringifies a json.RawMessage, returning "" for empty/nil so omitempty
// fields drop out.
func rawString(raw json.RawMessage) string {
	if len(raw) == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return string(raw)
}

// ---- Task (frontend "Task") ---- created_at as RFC3339, plus a derived status.
type TaskDTO struct {
	ID                 string             `json:"id"`
	ExplorationID      int64              `json:"exploration_id"`
	Name               string             `json:"name"` // optional task name; empty = unnamed
	CategoryID         *int64             `json:"category_id,omitempty"`
	CategoryName       string             `json:"category_name,omitempty"`
	Pinned             bool               `json:"pinned"`
	PinnedAt           string             `json:"pinned_at,omitempty"`
	Description        string             `json:"description"`
	Goal               string             `json:"goal"`
	Status             string             `json:"status"` // created | running | paused | done | failed
	CreatedAt          string             `json:"created_at"`
	CreatedUnix        int64              `json:"created_unix"`       // created_at as unix seconds (for run-duration calc)
	CompletedAt        string             `json:"completed_at"`       // RFC3339 finish time (done/failed); "" if unfinished
	CompletedUnix      int64              `json:"completed_unix"`     // completed_at as unix seconds (0 if unfinished)
	LastActivity       int64              `json:"last_activity_unix"` // unix seconds of the last activity (0 if none)
	Paused             bool               `json:"paused"`
	Queued             bool               `json:"queued"`
	Tokens             TokenTotalDTO      `json:"tokens"` // whole-task token consumption
	GoalsTotal         int                `json:"goals_total"`
	GoalsMet           int                `json:"goals_met"`
	InFlight           int                `json:"in_flight"`                // number of running Workers (intents with state=running)
	Findings           FindingSeverityDTO `json:"findings"`                 // findings registered for this task (findings table, bucketed by severity)
	LLMProfileID       *int64             `json:"llm_profile_id,omitempty"` // LLM profile used for this task; nil = default
	LLMProfileIDs      []int64            `json:"llm_profile_ids"`
	ActiveLLMProfileID *int64             `json:"active_llm_profile_id,omitempty"`
	LLMRotate          bool               `json:"llm_rotate"`
	LLMFailoverState   string             `json:"llm_failover_state"`
	LLMFailoverReason  string             `json:"llm_failover_reason,omitempty"`
	SourceTaskIDs      []string           `json:"source_task_ids"`
	ArchiveBlockedBy   string             `json:"archive_blocked_by_task_id,omitempty"`
	CompanyIDs         []int64            `json:"company_ids"`
	CoverageEnabled    bool               `json:"coverage_enabled"` // asset coverage feature switch (fixed at creation)
	PlanQuietMode      bool               `json:"plan_quiet_mode"`  // planner quiet-mode switch (#86), editable mid-run
	TargetGate         bool               `json:"target_gate"`      // approval gate for asset targets, opt-in, editable mid-run
}

// FindingSeverityDTO is the per-severity finding count shown in the task list (critical/high/medium/low).
type FindingSeverityDTO struct {
	Critical int `json:"critical"`
	High     int `json:"high"`
	Medium   int `json:"medium"`
	Low      int `json:"low"`
}

func applyTaskArchiveBlocker(dto *TaskDTO, blockers map[int64]int64) {
	if dto == nil || len(blockers) == 0 {
		return
	}
	taskID, err := strconv.ParseInt(dto.ID, 10, 64)
	if err != nil {
		return
	}
	if dependentID := blockers[taskID]; dependentID > 0 {
		dto.ArchiveBlockedBy = strconv.FormatInt(dependentID, 10)
	}
}

// TokenTotalDTO is a whole-task (all agents) token aggregate.
type TokenTotalDTO struct {
	InputTokens      int `json:"input_tokens"`
	OutputTokens     int `json:"output_tokens"`
	CacheReadTokens  int `json:"cache_read_tokens"`
	CacheWriteTokens int `json:"cache_write_tokens"`
}

func tokenTotalDTO(u db.TokenUsage) TokenTotalDTO {
	return TokenTotalDTO{
		InputTokens:      u.InputTokens,
		OutputTokens:     u.OutputTokens,
		CacheReadTokens:  u.CacheReadTokens,
		CacheWriteTokens: u.CacheWriteTokens,
	}
}

func taskDTO(t *Task, status string) TaskDTO {
	lifecycle := t.lifecycleSnapshot()
	llmState := t.llmStateSnapshot()
	sourceIDs := make([]string, 0, len(lifecycle.SourceTaskIDs))
	for _, id := range lifecycle.SourceTaskIDs {
		sourceIDs = append(sourceIDs, i64s(id))
	}
	profileIDs := append(make([]int64, 0, len(llmState.ProfileIDs)), llmState.ProfileIDs...)
	return TaskDTO{
		ID:                 t.ID,
		ExplorationID:      t.ExpID,
		Name:               lifecycle.Name,
		CategoryID:         lifecycle.CategoryID,
		CategoryName:       lifecycle.CategoryName,
		Pinned:             lifecycle.PinnedAt > 0,
		PinnedAt:           completedRFC(lifecycle.PinnedAt),
		Description:        t.Description,
		Goal:               t.Goal,
		Status:             status,
		CreatedAt:          rfc3339(time.Unix(t.CreatedAt, 0)),
		CreatedUnix:        t.CreatedAt,
		CompletedAt:        completedRFC(lifecycle.CompletedAt),
		CompletedUnix:      lifecycle.CompletedAt,
		Paused:             lifecycle.Paused,
		Queued:             lifecycle.Queued,
		LLMProfileID:       llmState.ProfileID,
		LLMProfileIDs:      profileIDs,
		ActiveLLMProfileID: llmState.ActiveID,
		LLMRotate:          t.LLMRotate,
		LLMFailoverState:   llmState.FailoverState,
		LLMFailoverReason:  llmState.FailoverReason,
		SourceTaskIDs:      sourceIDs,
		CompanyIDs:         lifecycle.CompanyIDs,
		CoverageEnabled:    t.CoverageEnabled,
		PlanQuietMode:      t.PlanQuietMode,
		TargetGate:         t.targetGate.Load(),
	}
}

// completedRFC renders a unix completion time as RFC3339, or "" when unset (0).
func completedRFC(unix int64) string {
	if unix == 0 {
		return ""
	}
	return rfc3339(time.Unix(unix, 0))
}

// ---- TrafficExchange (frontend "TrafficExchange") ---- ts as RFC3339.
type TrafficExchangeDTO struct {
	ID          string `json:"id"`
	TS          string `json:"ts"`
	Host        string `json:"host"`
	Method      string `json:"method"`
	URL         string `json:"url"`
	Status      int    `json:"status"`
	ContentType string `json:"content_type"`
	RespLen     int    `json:"resp_len"`
}

func trafficDTOs(ex []traffic.ExchangeMeta) []TrafficExchangeDTO {
	out := make([]TrafficExchangeDTO, 0, len(ex))
	for _, e := range ex {
		out = append(out, TrafficExchangeDTO{
			ID:          e.ID,
			TS:          rfc3339(time.Unix(e.TS, 0)),
			Host:        e.Host,
			Method:      e.Method,
			URL:         e.URL,
			Status:      e.Status,
			ContentType: e.ContentType,
			RespLen:     e.RespLen,
		})
	}
	return out
}

// ---- TaskNode (frontend "TaskNode") — frontier, intents, exploration graph nodes ----

type TaskNodeDTO struct {
	ID           string `json:"id"`
	Type         string `json:"type"` // db Node.Kind
	Payload      string `json:"payload,omitempty"`
	Priority     int    `json:"priority"`
	State        string `json:"state"`
	Origin       string `json:"origin"`
	TS           string `json:"ts"`
	SourceTaskID string `json:"source_task_id,omitempty"`
	Inherited    bool   `json:"inherited,omitempty"`
	DeleteReason string `json:"delete_reason,omitempty"` // deletion reason when the intent is soft-deleted (state='deleted')
}

	d := TaskNodeDTO{
		ID:           i64s(n.ID),
		Type:         n.Kind,
		Payload:      rawString(n.Payload),
		DeleteReason: n.DeleteReason,
		Priority:     n.Priority,
		State:        n.State,
		Origin:       n.Origin,
		TS:           rfc3339(n.CreatedAt),
	}
	if n.SourceTaskID > 0 {
		d.SourceTaskID = i64s(n.SourceTaskID)
	}
	d.Inherited = n.Inherited
	return d
}

// GoalDTO is a goal node with its payload unpacked into text/vulnclass — the shape
// the overview "Goal Management" UI works with (vs TaskNodeDTO which carries raw payload JSON).
type GoalDTO struct {
	ID        string `json:"id"`
	Text      string `json:"text"`
	VulnClass string `json:"vulnclass,omitempty"`
	State     string `json:"state"`
	Origin    string `json:"origin,omitempty"`
	TS        string `json:"ts"`
}

func goalDTO(n *db.Node) GoalDTO {
	var p struct {
		Text      string `json:"text"`
		VulnClass string `json:"vulnclass"`
	}
	_ = json.Unmarshal(n.Payload, &p)
	return GoalDTO{
		ID:        i64s(n.ID),
		Text:      p.Text,
		VulnClass: p.VulnClass,
		State:     n.State,
		Origin:    n.Origin,
		TS:        rfc3339(n.CreatedAt),
	}
}

func goalDTOs(in []*db.Node) []GoalDTO {
	out := make([]GoalDTO, 0, len(in))
	for _, n := range in {
		out = append(out, goalDTO(n))
	}
	return out
}

// ---- Finding (frontend "Finding") ----

type FindingDTO struct {
	TrafficCount          int                        `json:"traffic_count"`
	EvidenceVersion       int64                      `json:"evidence_version"`
	ReportEvidenceVersion int64                      `json:"report_evidence_version"`
	ReportStale           bool                       `json:"report_stale"`
	TrafficBindings       []db.FindingTrafficBinding `json:"traffic_bindings,omitempty"`
	PoELevel              int                        `json:"poe_level"`
	VerificationStatus    string                     `json:"verification_status"`
	VerificationNote      string                     `json:"verification_note"`
	Counterevidence       string                     `json:"counterevidence,omitempty"`      // what was tested and did not work; optional
	ConfidenceRationale   string                     `json:"confidence_rationale,omitempty"` // why the conclusion holds; optional

	ID        string `json:"id"`
	FindingID string `json:"finding_id,omitempty"` // standalone findings-table id — the handle for status updates
	VulnClass string `json:"vulnclass"`
	Name      string `json:"name,omitempty"` // vulnerability name; the frontend falls back to displaying vulnclass when empty
	Severity  string `json:"severity"`       // critical | high | medium | low
	Status    string `json:"status"`         // pending | in_progress | confirmed | resolved | fixed | false_positive | ignored | duplicate | risk_accepted
	Summary   string `json:"summary"`
	Evidence  string `json:"evidence"`
	Report    string `json:"report,omitempty"` // detailed report (Markdown); returned only by the detail endpoint, empty in lists

	IntentID        string            `json:"intent_id,omitempty"`
	ParamID         string            `json:"param_id,omitempty"`
	TaskID          string            `json:"task_id,omitempty"`
	TaskDescription string            `json:"task_description,omitempty"`
	SourceTaskID    string            `json:"source_task_id,omitempty"`
	Inherited       bool              `json:"inherited,omitempty"`
	Assets          []FindingAssetDTO `json:"assets,omitempty"`
	TS              string            `json:"ts"`
}

// FindingAssetDTO is one asset a finding is anchored to, pre-labelled for display.
type FindingAssetDTO struct {
	ID    string `json:"id"`
	Type  string `json:"type"`
	Label string `json:"label"`
}

// assetLabel renders an asset's most identifying field for compact display.
func assetLabel(a *db.Asset) string {
	switch {
	case a.URL != "":
		if a.Method != "" {
			return a.Method + " " + a.URL
		}
		return a.URL
	case a.Domain != "":
		if a.Port != nil && *a.Port > 0 {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", a.Domain, *a.Port)
		}
		return a.Domain
	case a.IP != "":
		if a.Port != nil && *a.Port > 0 {
			return fmt.Sprintf("%s:%d", a.IP, *a.Port)
		}
		return a.IP
	case a.AppName != "":
		return a.AppName
	case a.BundleID != "":
		return a.BundleID
	case a.ServiceName != "":
		return a.ServiceName
	case a.RootDomain != "":
		return a.RootDomain
	default:
		return "#" + i64s(a.ID)
	}
}

// findingPayload mirrors the JSON written by the worker's report_finding tool
// (agent/tools.go addFinding): {vulnclass, severity, summary, evidence:{by,poc}}.
type findingPayload struct {
	VulnClass string          `json:"vulnclass"`
	Name      string          `json:"name"`
	Severity  string          `json:"severity"`
	Summary   string          `json:"summary"`
	Evidence  json.RawMessage `json:"evidence"`
}

func findingDTO(n *db.Node) FindingDTO {
	var p findingPayload
	_ = json.Unmarshal(n.Payload, &p)
	d := FindingDTO{
		ID:        i64s(n.ID),
		VulnClass: p.VulnClass,
		Name:      p.Name,
		Severity:  p.Severity,
		Status:    db.FindingPending,
		Summary:   p.Summary,
		Evidence:  rawString(p.Evidence),
		TS:        rfc3339(n.CreatedAt),
	}
	if n.SourceTaskID > 0 {
		d.SourceTaskID = i64s(n.SourceTaskID)
	}
	d.Inherited = n.Inherited
	return d
}

// findingDTOsForTask converts a task's finding nodes to DTOs, stamping each with
// the owning task's id/description so the global findings page can group across tasks.
// meta maps node id → the standalone findings row (id + status + asset ids), so the
// per-task view shows the same triage state and anchored assets as the global page;
// nodes with no row keep the 'pending' default and no finding_id (not editable).
// assets pre-resolves the anchored asset rows for label rendering.
func findingDTOsForTask(t *Task, in []*db.Node, meta map[int64]db.FindingMeta, assets map[int64]*db.Asset) []FindingDTO {
	return findingDTOsForOwner(t.ID, t.Description, in, meta, assets)
}

func findingDTOsForOwner(taskID, description string, in []*db.Node, meta map[int64]db.FindingMeta, assets map[int64]*db.Asset) []FindingDTO {
	out := make([]FindingDTO, 0, len(in))
	for _, n := range in {
		d := findingDTO(n)
		d.TaskID = taskID
		d.TaskDescription = description
		if m, ok := meta[n.ID]; ok {
			d.FindingID = i64s(m.ID)
			d.Status = m.Status
			d.TrafficCount = m.TrafficCount
			d.Assets = findingAssetDTOs(m.AssetIDs, assets)
		}
		out = append(out, d)
	}
	return out
}

// findingAssetDTOs maps anchored asset ids to display DTOs, skipping ids whose
// asset row is missing (e.g. deleted).
func findingAssetDTOs(ids []int64, assets map[int64]*db.Asset) []FindingAssetDTO {
	var out []FindingAssetDTO
	for _, aid := range ids {
		if a := assets[aid]; a != nil {
			out = append(out, FindingAssetDTO{ID: i64s(a.ID), Type: a.Type, Label: assetLabel(a)})
		}
	}
	return out
}

// findingFromDB converts a standalone DBFinding row to a FindingDTO. task_id and
// task_description are empty when the originating task has been deleted (NULL).
func findingFromDB(f *db.DBFinding, assets map[int64]*db.Asset) FindingDTO {
	status := f.Status
	if status == "" {
		status = db.FindingPending
	}
	d := FindingDTO{
		ID:           i64s(f.ID),
		FindingID:    i64s(f.ID),
		TrafficCount: f.TrafficCount, EvidenceVersion: f.EvidenceVersion, ReportEvidenceVersion: f.ReportEvidenceVersion,
		ReportStale: f.Report != "" && f.EvidenceVersion != f.ReportEvidenceVersion, TrafficBindings: f.TrafficBindings,
		PoELevel: f.PoELevel, VerificationStatus: f.VerificationStatus, VerificationNote: f.VerificationNote,
		Counterevidence: f.Counterevidence, ConfidenceRationale: f.ConfidenceRationale,
		VulnClass: f.VulnClass,
		Name:      f.Name,
		Severity:  f.Severity,
		Status:    status,
		Summary:   f.Summary,
		Evidence:  f.Evidence,
		Report:    f.Report,
		TS:        rfc3339(f.CreatedAt),
	}
	d.Assets = findingAssetDTOs(f.AssetIDs, assets)
	if f.TaskID != nil {
		d.TaskID = i64s(*f.TaskID)
		d.TaskDescription = f.TaskDescription
	}
	if f.NodeID != nil {
		d.IntentID = "" // node_id is the finding node, not the intent; keep IntentID empty
	}
	return d
}

// ---- Activity (frontend "Activity") ----

type ActivityDTO struct {
	Seq          int64           `json:"seq"`                 // db Activity.ID
	IntentID     string          `json:"intent_id,omitempty"` // db NodeID
	Worker       string          `json:"worker"`
	TS           string          `json:"ts"` // db CreatedAt
	Kind         string          `json:"kind"`
	Tool         string          `json:"tool,omitempty"`
	ToolUseID    string          `json:"tool_use_id,omitempty"`
	IsError      bool            `json:"is_error"`
	Summary      string          `json:"summary"`
	Detail       string          `json:"detail,omitempty"`
	Metadata     json.RawMessage `json:"metadata,omitempty"`
	SourceTaskID string          `json:"source_task_id,omitempty"`
	Inherited    bool            `json:"inherited,omitempty"`
	MainSeg      *int            `json:"main_seg,omitempty"` // main-agent conversation segment (nil for non-mainagent rows)
	// token usage (set only on kind='result'); used for per-session token totals.
	InputTokens      *int `json:"input_tokens,omitempty"`
	OutputTokens     *int `json:"output_tokens,omitempty"`
	CacheReadTokens  *int `json:"cache_read_tokens,omitempty"`
	CacheWriteTokens *int `json:"cache_write_tokens,omitempty"`
}

func activityDTO(a db.Activity) ActivityDTO {
	intent := ""
	if a.NodeID != nil {
		intent = i64s(*a.NodeID)
	}
	d := ActivityDTO{
		Seq:              a.ID,
		IntentID:         intent,
		Worker:           a.Worker,
		TS:               rfc3339(a.CreatedAt),
		Kind:             a.Kind,
		Tool:             a.Tool,
		ToolUseID:        a.ToolUseID,
		IsError:          a.IsError,
		Summary:          a.Summary,
		Detail:           a.Detail, // list endpoint leaves this empty (lazy)
		Metadata:         a.Metadata,
		InputTokens:      a.InputTokens,
		OutputTokens:     a.OutputTokens,
		CacheReadTokens:  a.CacheReadTokens,
		CacheWriteTokens: a.CacheWriteTokens,
		MainSeg:          a.MainSeg,
	}
	if a.SourceTaskID > 0 {
		d.SourceTaskID = i64s(a.SourceTaskID)
	}
	d.Inherited = a.Inherited
	return d
}

func activityDTOs(in []db.Activity) []ActivityDTO {
	out := make([]ActivityDTO, 0, len(in))
	for _, a := range in {
		out = append(out, activityDTO(a))
	}
	return out
}

// ---- LLMProfile (frontend "LLMProfile") — string id ----

type LLMProfileDTO struct {
	ID              string  `json:"id"`
	Name            string  `json:"name"`
	Format          string  `json:"format"`
	BaseURL         string  `json:"base_url,omitempty"`
	Proxy           string  `json:"proxy,omitempty"` // masked: the placeholder when set
	ProxySet        bool    `json:"proxy_set"`
	Model           string  `json:"model"`
	APIKeyHint      string  `json:"api_key_hint,omitempty"`
	RatePerSecond   float64 `json:"rate_per_second"`
	RatePerMinute   float64 `json:"rate_per_minute"`
	ContextWindowK  int     `json:"context_window_k"`
	ThinkingType    string  `json:"thinking_type"`
	ReasoningEffort string  `json:"reasoning_effort"`
	IsDefault       bool    `json:"is_default"`
	// Pooling (failover) parameters: higher priority is picked first (the active
	// profile is always the chain head); pool_exclude=true excludes it as a failover target, though agents/tasks can still bind it explicitly.
	Priority    int  `json:"priority"`
	PoolExclude bool `json:"pool_exclude"`
	// Send/receive mode: true=streaming (SSE) | false=non-streaming. No omitempty —
	// false must appear in the response, otherwise the frontend cannot read "non-streaming" and the switch falls back to streaming by default.
	Streaming bool `json:"streaming"`
	// Per-reply output cap (0=do not send; the server default applies) and which
	// request field name it uses (''=max_tokens | 'max_completion_tokens', only meaningful for the openai format).
	MaxTokens      int    `json:"max_tokens"`
	MaxTokensField string `json:"max_tokens_field"`
	// Custom session header name: when non-empty, every request carries this HTTP header,
	// its value = the current session/intent's session id. '' = do not send. For gateways that key prompt caching/sticky routing off a session-id header.
	SessionHeaderKey string `json:"session_header_key"`
	// Custom User-Agent: when non-empty, every outbound LLM request overrides its
	// User-Agent header with this value. '' = do not override (keep the default UA).
	UserAgent string `json:"user_agent"`
	// This profile's retry overrides (connect / empty response / same-provider safe
	// window). Per item attempts: 0=inherit the global policy | -1=disable that retry
	// layer | >0=count; interval_ms: 0=default exponential backoff | >0=use that fixed millisecond interval. All zero = fully follow the global policy, i.e. the historical behavior.
	Retry db.RetryOverride `json:"retry"`
}

func llmProfileDTO(p *db.LLMProfile) LLMProfileDTO {
	return LLMProfileDTO{
		ID:               i64s(p.ID),
		Name:             p.Name,
		Format:           p.Format,
		BaseURL:          p.BaseURL,
		Proxy:            maskedSecret(p.Proxy),
		ProxySet:         p.Proxy != "",
		Model:            p.Model,
		APIKeyHint:       p.APIKeyHint,
		RatePerSecond:    p.RatePerSecond,
		RatePerMinute:    p.RatePerMinute,
		ContextWindowK:   p.ContextWindowK,
		ThinkingType:     p.ThinkingType,
		ReasoningEffort:  p.ReasoningEffort,
		IsDefault:        p.IsDefault,
		Priority:         p.Priority,
		PoolExclude:      p.PoolExclude,
		Streaming:        p.Streaming,
		MaxTokens:        p.MaxTokens,
		MaxTokensField:   p.MaxTokensField,
		SessionHeaderKey: p.SessionHeaderKey,
		UserAgent:        p.UserAgent,
		Retry:            p.Retry,
	}
}

func llmProfileDTOs(in []*db.LLMProfile) []LLMProfileDTO {
	out := make([]LLMProfileDTO, 0, len(in))
	for _, p := range in {
		out = append(out, llmProfileDTO(p))
	}
	return out
}

// idStrings formats a slice of int64 ids as strings (for visibility agent ids).
func idStrings(in []int64) []string {
	out := make([]string, 0, len(in))
	for _, v := range in {
		out = append(out, i64s(v))
	}
	return out
}
